1. #!/usr/bin/env python3
2. """Query the local Chroma SQLite store with FTS and repo-specific path bias."""
3. 
4. from __future__ import annotations
5. 
6. import argparse
7. import json
8. import re
9. import sqlite3
10. import sys
11. from pathlib import Path
12. from typing import Iterable
13. 
14. 
15. REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
16. DB_PATH = REPO_ROOT / ".artifacts" / "chromadb" / "chroma.sqlite3"
17. COLLECTIONS = ("ucx_code", "obmm_code", "ompi_code")
18. 
19. PATH_BIAS_RULES = {
20.     "ucx_code": [
21.         ("ucx/src/uct/", -4.0),
22.         ("ucx/src/ucp/", -3.5),
23.         ("ucx/src/", -2.5),
24.         ("ucx/test/", 0.8),

31.         ("obmm/README", 1.5),

34.     "ompi_code": [

36.         ("ompi/opal/", -2.5),
37.         ("ompi/oshmem/", -2.5),
38.         ("ompi/docs/", 0.8),

44.     ],
45. }
46. 
47. 
48. def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
49.     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
50.         description="Query the local Chroma DB without relying on a mismatched embedding model."
51.     )
52.     parser.add_argument("query", help="Symbol, API, concept, or phrase to retrieve.")
53.     parser.add_argument(
54.         "--collection",
55.         action="append",
56.         choices=COLLECTIONS,
57.         dest="collections",
58.         help="Collection(s) to search. Defaults to all collections.",
59.     )
60.     parser.add_argument(
61.         "--k",
62.         type=int,
63.         default=8,
64.         help="Number of final ranked hits to return per collection.",
65.     )
66.     parser.add_argument(
67.         "--candidate-multiplier",
68.         type=int,
69.         default=4,
70.         help="Fetch this many multiples of k before reranking.",
71.     )
72.     parser.add_argument(
73.         "--path-hint",
74.         action="append",
75.         default=[],
76.         help="Prefer paths containing this substring. Repeatable.",
77.     )
78.     parser.add_argument(
79.         "--json",
80.         action="store_true",
81.         help="Emit machine-readable JSON.",
82.     )
83.     return parser.parse_args()
84. 
85. 
86. def tokenize(query: str) -> list[str]:
87.     return re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*|\d+", query)
88. 
89. 
90. def build_match_expressions(query: str) -> list[str]:
91.     raw = query.strip()
92.     if not raw:
93.         return []
94. 
95.     expressions: list[str] = []
96.     escaped = raw.replace('"', '""')
97. 
98.     if len(raw.split()) == 1 or "_" in raw or "/" in raw:
99.         expressions.append(f'"{escaped}"')
100. 
101.     tokens = tokenize(raw)
102.     if tokens:
103.         expressions.append(" AND ".join(f'"{token.replace(chr(34), chr(34) * 2)}"' for token in tokens))
104.         if len(tokens) > 1:
105.             expressions.append(" OR ".join(f'"{token.replace(chr(34), chr(34) * 2)}"' for token in tokens))
106. 
107.     if f'"{escaped}"' not in expressions:
108.         expressions.append(f'"{escaped}"')
109. 
110.     deduped: list[str] = []
111.     for expr in expressions:
112.         if expr not in deduped:
113.             deduped.append(expr)
114.     return deduped
115. 
116. 
117. def clean_snippet(document: str, limit: int = 220) -> str:
118.     lines = document.splitlines()
119.     if lines[:3] and lines[0].startswith("path: ") and any(line.startswith("root: ") for line in lines[:4]):
120.         body_start = 0
121.         blank_seen = False
122.         for i, line in enumerate(lines):
123.             if line.strip():
124.                 if blank_seen:
125.                     body_start = i
126.                     break
127.             else:
128.                 blank_seen = True
129.         body = "\n".join(lines[body_start:]).strip()
130.     else:
131.         body = document.strip()
132.     body = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", body)
133.     return body[:limit]
134. 
135. 
136. def path_bias(collection: str, path: str) -> float:
137.     for prefix, bias in PATH_BIAS_RULES.get(collection, []):
138.         if path.startswith(prefix):
139.             return bias
140.     return 0.0
141. 
142. 
143. def hint_bias(path: str, hints: Iterable[str]) -> float:
144.     path_lower = path.lower()
145.     bias = 0.0
146.     for hint in hints:
147.         if hint.lower() in path_lower:
148.             bias -= 1.5
149.     return bias
150. 
151. 
152. def exact_bias(query: str, path: str, document: str) -> float:
153.     lowered = query.lower()
154.     bias = 0.0
155.     if lowered in path.lower():
156.         bias -= 1.0
157.     if lowered in document.lower():
158.         bias -= 1.5
159.     return bias
160. 
161. 
162. def fetch_candidates(
163.     con: sqlite3.Connection,
164.     collection: str,
165.     query: str,
166.     limit: int,
167. ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
168.     results: dict[tuple[str, int, int], dict[str, object]] = {}
169.     expressions = build_match_expressions(query)
170.     if not expressions:
171.         return []
172. 
173.     sql = """
174.         select bm25(embedding_fulltext_search) as bm25_score,
175.                p.string_value as path,
176.                s.int_value as start_line,
177.                e.int_value as end_line,
178.                d.string_value as document
179.         from embedding_fulltext_search
180.         join embeddings emb on emb.id = embedding_fulltext_search.rowid
181.         join segments seg on seg.id = emb.segment_id and seg.scope = 'METADATA'
182.         join collections c on c.id = seg.collection
183.         join embedding_metadata d on d.id = emb.id and d.key = 'chroma:document'
184.         join embedding_metadata p on p.id = emb.id and p.key = 'path'
185.         join embedding_metadata s on s.id = emb.id and s.key = 'start_line'
186.         join embedding_metadata e on e.id = emb.id and e.key = 'end_line'
187.         where c.name = ? and embedding_fulltext_search match ?
188.         order by bm25_score
189.         limit ?
190.     """
191. 
192.     for expr in expressions:
193.         for row in con.execute(sql, (collection, expr, limit)):
194.             key = (row["path"], row["start_line"], row["end_line"])
195.             candidate = {
196.                 "collection": collection,
197.                 "path": row["path"],
198.                 "start_line": row["start_line"],
199.                 "end_line": row["end_line"],
200.                 "document": row["document"],
201.                 "bm25": float(row["bm25_score"]),
202.                 "match_expression": expr,
203.             }
204.             prev = results.get(key)
205.             if prev is None or candidate["bm25"] < prev["bm25"]:
206.                 results[key] = candidate
207.     return list(results.values())
208. 
209. 
210. def rerank(candidates: list[dict[str, object]], query: str, hints: list[str]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
211.     reranked = []
212.     for item in candidates:
213.         doc = str(item["document"])
214.         path = str(item["path"])
215.         collection = str(item["collection"])
216.         adjusted = (
217.             float(item["bm25"])
218.             + path_bias(collection, path)
219.             + hint_bias(path, hints)
220.             + exact_bias(query, path, doc)
221.         )
222.         reranked.append(
223.             {
224.                 **item,
225.                 "adjusted_score": adjusted,
226.                 "snippet": clean_snippet(doc),
227.             }
228.         )
229.     reranked.sort(key=lambda item: (item["adjusted_score"], item["bm25"], item["path"], item["start_line"]))
230.     return reranked
231. 
232. 
233. def render_text(collection: str, query: str, results: list[dict[str, object]]) -> str:
234.     lines = [f"[{collection}] query={query}"]
235.     if not results:
236.         lines.append("(no hits)")
237.         return "\n".join(lines)
238. 
239.     for index, item in enumerate(results, 1):
240.         score = item.get("adjusted_score", item.get("score"))
241.         lines.append(
242.             f"{index}. {item['path']}:{item['start_line']}-{item['end_line']} "
243.             f"(score={float(score):.3f}, bm25={float(item['bm25']):.3f})"
244.         )
245.         lines.append(f"   {item['snippet']}")
246.     return "\n".join(lines)
247. 
248. 
249. def main() -> int:
250.     args = parse_args()
251.     if not DB_PATH.exists():
252.         print(f"Chroma DB not found: {DB_PATH}", file=sys.stderr)
253.         return 1
254. 
255.     con = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
256.     con.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
257. 
258.     collections = args.collections or list(COLLECTIONS)
259.     candidate_limit = max(args.k * args.candidate_multiplier, args.k)
260.     payload = []
261. 
262.     for collection in collections:
263.         candidates = fetch_candidates(con, collection, args.query, candidate_limit)
264.         ranked = rerank(candidates, args.query, args.path_hint)[: args.k]
265.         payload.append(
266.             {
267.                 "collection": collection,
268.                 "query": args.query,
269.                 "results": [
270.                     {
271.                         "path": item["path"],
272.                         "start_line": item["start_line"],
273.                         "end_line": item["end_line"],
274.                         "score": round(float(item["adjusted_score"]), 6),
275.                         "bm25": round(float(item["bm25"]), 6),
276.                         "snippet": item["snippet"],
277.                     }
278.                     for item in ranked
279.                 ],
280.             }
281.         )
282. 
283.     if args.json:

11. # OBMM API and Test Environment
12. 
13. This skill is the **single source of truth** for what the agent may assume
14. about libobmm and the deployment topology. If something is not stated here,
15. the agent must ASK the user instead of inventing it.
16. 
17. ## libobmm public API (from `obmm/src/libobmm/libobmm.h`)
18. 
19. ```c
20. mem_id obmm_export(const size_t length[OBMM_MAX_LOCAL_NUMA_NODES],
21.                    unsigned long flags, struct obmm_mem_desc *desc);
22. int    obmm_unexport(mem_id id, unsigned long flags);
23. 
24. int    obmm_preimport(struct obmm_preimport_info *preimport_info,
25.                       unsigned long flags);
26. int    obmm_unpreimport(const struct obmm_preimport_info *preimport_info,
27.                         unsigned long flags);
28. 
29. mem_id obmm_export_useraddr(int pid, void *va, size_t length,
30.                             unsigned long flags, struct obmm_mem_desc *desc);
31. 
32. mem_id obmm_import(const struct obmm_mem_desc *desc, unsigned long flags,
33.                    int base_dist, int *numa);
34. int    obmm_unimport(mem_id id, unsigned long flags);
35. 
36. int    obmm_set_ownership(int fd, void *start, void *end, int prot);
37. 
38. int    obmm_query_memid_by_pa(unsigned long pa, mem_id *id,
39.                               unsigned long *offset);
40. int    obmm_query_pa_by_memid(mem_id id, unsigned long offset,
41.                               unsigned long *pa);
42. ```
43. 
44. Key data structures:
45. 
46. - `struct obmm_mem_desc { addr; length; seid[16]; deid[16]; tokenid; scna;
47.   dcna; priv_len; priv[]; }` — the descriptor returned by export and
48.   consumed by import.
49. - `struct obmm_preimport_info { pa; length; base_dist; numa_id; seid; deid;
50.   scna; dcna; priv_len; priv[]; }`
51. - `mem_id` is `uint64_t`; `OBMM_INVALID_MEMID == 0`.
52. 
53. ## Test environment — IMMUTABLE FACTS
54. 
55. These were stated by the project owner. The transport implementation MUST
56. be designed against exactly this topology:
57. 
58. 1. **Two nodes**, node 0 and node 1.
59. 2. Each node has **already exported a 128 MiB memory region** to the other
60.    side, before any UCX / MPI process starts.
61. 3. Each node has **already imported** the peer's 128 MiB region.
62. 4. The export / import / preimport / unimport / unexport lifecycle is
63.    handled outside the UCX transport — **the obmm UCT transport must NOT
64.    call** `obmm_export`, `obmm_unexport`, `obmm_import`, `obmm_unimport`,
65.    `obmm_preimport`, or `obmm_unpreimport` at runtime.
66. 5. Inside UCT, access to the local and peer regions is done with
67.    **`open("/dev/obmm_shmdev${memid}", O_RDWR | O_SYNC)` + `mmap`**
68.    (NC mapping; see "Locked-in design decisions" below).
69.    The local export memid and peer import memid are discovered by
70.    scanning `/sys/devices/obmm/obmm_shmdev*/` and inspecting whether
71.    each contains an `export_info/` or `import_info/` subdirectory.
72. 6. **No hardware is available** in the development environment. Do not
73.    attempt to run `mpirun`, real `ucx_perftest`, or any test that requires
74.    the obmm device. Validation is limited to:
75.      - `make` / `make install` succeeding,
76.      - `ucx_info -d` listing the obmm component, md, and tl,
77.      - `ucx_info -c` showing OBMM_* env vars,
78.      - static review against this skill and `uct-transport-patterns`.
79. 
80. ## Locked-in design decisions (do not change without re-asking)
81. 
82. These were explicitly decided with the project owner during the v1
83. am_short plan review. They override any conflicting suggestion the
84. agent may otherwise default to (notably the mm transport's behavior).
85. 
86. 1. **NC mapping for the data path.** Open shmdev with
87.    `O_RDWR | O_SYNC` and mmap with `MAP_SHARED`. This puts the FIFO
88.    region into a non-cacheable mapping, which:
89.      - bypasses the OBMM cacheable consistency model (writers and
90.        readers from any host coexist),
91.      - removes the need to ever call `obmm_set_ownership` from the
92.        transport.
93. 2. **Cross-node atomic RMW on NC is guaranteed.** The project owner
94.    has stated that the obmm fabric supports atomic FAA / CAS on NC
95.    mappings across nodes. The transport may therefore use mm-style
96.    multi-producer FIFOs (FAA on a shared head) without redesigning
97.    for SPSC.
98. 3. **UCT owns the in-region layout.** The 128 MiB exported region is
99.    zero-filled at platform export time. The transport places its own
100.    header (state / version / slot bitmap / slot_meta / fixed-size
101.    slots) at the start of the region. A two-phase init is used:
102.    `state` transitions UNINIT→INITING (CAS) → fill geometry → bus
103.    fence → store READY. Losers spin on READY then bus-load fence.
104.    Single-magic init is racy (geometry not yet visible) and must
105.    not be used.
106. 4. **Topology**: per node there is exactly 1 export region and 1
107.    import region (the peer node's export). Discovered via
108.    `/sys/devices/obmm/obmm_shmdev*/{export_info,import_info}`.
109.    Reachability and mapping table keys are
110.    `(exporter_dcna, exporter_deid, memid)` from sysfs — NOT memid
111.    alone (collision-prone).
112. 5. **Self-loopback inside one node** is supported: same-node processes
113.    communicate by both mapping the local export region (the imported
114.    "peer region" entry simply will not exist in the single-node case,
115.    or will equal the local one — handle both).
116. 6. **Slot lifecycle uses generation tokens.** Each slot has
117.    `(owner_pid, owner_starttime, generation, state)` in slot_meta.
118.    `iface_addr` and every FIFO elem carry `generation`; receiver
119.    discards mismatches. Destroy = mark DEAD → bus fence → bump
120.    generation → clear bit. Crash recovery: scan bitmap, validate
121.    `/proc/<pid>/stat starttime`, reclaim. PID alone is insufficient
122.    (PID reuse).
123. 7. **Cross-node memory ordering uses BUS-domain fences.**
124.    `ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()` / `ucs_memory_bus_load_fence()`
125.    (sfence/lfence on x86, `dmb oshst`/`dmb oshld` on arm64). The
126.    CPU-domain fences mm uses (`ucs_memory_cpu_*_fence`) are
127.    inner-shareable only and DO NOT cover cross-host NC visibility.
128. 
129. ## OBMM consistency model — why NC matters
130. 
131. From `obmm/doc/libobmm.md` and `obmm/doc/obmm_set_ownership.md`:
132. 
133. - For **cacheable** OBMM mappings, at any moment all hosts touching a
134.   region must be in one of two states:
135.     a) all hosts are PROT_READ or PROT_NONE, OR
136.     b) exactly one host has writers; all other hosts must be PROT_NONE.
137. - A receive-FIFO model (writer on the sending host, reader on the
138.   receiving host, on the SAME region) violates this: it would require
139.   one host to write while another host reads simultaneously.
140. - Therefore the obmm transport CANNOT use cacheable mappings for the
141.   FIFO region without expensive ownership flips per message.
142. - NC (O_SYNC) mappings are exempt: per the doc, "用户无需关心一致性
143.   模型，所有的用户均具备读写权限". This is why decision (1) above
144.   is mandatory, not optional.
145. 
146. ## Implications for the transport design
147. 
148. These follow from the facts above and should be treated as defaults; ask
149. the user before deviating:
150. 
151. - **Memory registration** (`uct_md_ops_t::mem_reg` / `mem_dereg`) does not
152.   need to call libobmm. The current placeholders
153.   (`uct_md_dummy_mem_reg` / `uct_md_dummy_mem_dereg`) are appropriate
154.   because the buffers used by am_short live inside the pre-imported
155.   peer region, not in arbitrary user buffers.
156. - **Address exchange** for am_short: `iface_addr` MUST carry
157.   `(exporter_dcna, exporter_deid, memid, slot_index, generation)`
158.   so the peer can (a) look up the already-mmap'd region in our MD's
159.   mapping table by exporter identity + memid, and (b) detect stale
160.   slot reuse via generation. Memid alone is unsafe and was rejected
161.   in plan-review. The current `uct_obmm_iface_addr_t = uint64_t`
162.   must be widened.
163. - **Reachability**: `iface_is_reachable_v2` matches on
164.   `(exporter_dcna, exporter_deid, memid)` against the MD's known
165.   exports + imports. Drop the `uct_sm_iface_is_reachable` (same-host)
166.   call — obmm is cross-node by construction.
167. - **Progress wiring**: `iface_progress_enable/disable` MUST call
168.   `uct_base_iface_progress_enable_cb(...)` /
169.   `uct_base_iface_progress_disable(...)`. The current
170.   `ucs_empty_function` stubs prevent UCP from ever polling the iface.
171. - **EP_CHECK**: do NOT advertise `UCT_IFACE_FLAG_EP_CHECK` in v1.
172.   The current skeleton sets it but `ep_check` only returns OK; no
173.   cross-node liveness check exists. PID-in-addr is not enough.
174. - **Ownership / `obmm_set_ownership`**: only call this if the UCT layer
175.   needs to flip read/write permission on a sub-range of the imported
176.   region; for a first am_short pass with a producer/consumer FIFO this
177.   is typically NOT needed. Ask before adding it.
178. 
179. ## What to ASK the user before writing code
180. 
181. Do not invent answers to any of these. Use the `ask_user` tool:
182. 
183. 1. Whether multiple obmm ifaces per process are expected, or strictly
184.    one peer per local iface (current assumption: 1 iface per process,
185.    pool holds many ifaces from many processes).
186. 2. What the wire `am_id` / header / payload alignment requirements are
187.    on the obmm hardware (e.g. 64 B cache line? 256 B?). Default plan
188.    aligns elements to 64 B; confirm before tuning.
189. 3. ~~Whether NC writes from one host become visible to remote loads
190.    without an explicit fabric-level barrier other than CPU
191.    `dmb`/`mfence`.~~ **RESOLVED in plan-review**: must use bus-domain
192.    fences (`ucs_memory_bus_*_fence`), not CPU-domain. CPU fences are
193.    inner-shareable only and don't reach cross-host NC.
194. 
195. ## Forbidden assumptions
196. 
197. - Do NOT assume libobmm performs its own synchronization — am_short
198.   ordering must be enforced by the transport (release / acquire fences,
199.   same as mm).
200. - Do NOT use cacheable mappings on the FIFO region. NC (`O_SYNC`)
201.   is mandatory; see "Locked-in design decisions".
202. - Do NOT call any `obmm_*` runtime API in the UCT transport unless this
203.   document is updated to allow it. In particular do NOT call
204.   `obmm_set_ownership` — its semantics conflict with the FIFO usage
205.   pattern.
206. - Do NOT use `ucs_memory_cpu_*_fence()` on the obmm data path. They
207.   are inner-shareable / compiler-only and do not cover cross-host NC
208.   visibility. Use `ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()` /
209.   `ucs_memory_bus_load_fence()` (sfence/lfence on x86,
210.   `dmb oshst`/`dmb oshld` on arm64). The mm transport gets away with
211.   CPU fences only because mm peers share an inner-shareable cache
212.   domain; obmm peers do not.
213. 
214. ## Why cacheable + manual cache management was rejected
215. 
216. Asked and answered during plan-review. Do not re-litigate without new
217. information about the obmm fabric.
218. 
219. 1. **OBMM cacheable consistency is enforced at the page-table level**,
220.    not at the cache level. `obmm/doc/libobmm.md:196-211` and
221.    `obmm/doc/obmm_set_ownership.md` require that at any moment either
222.    all hosts touching a region are PROT_READ/PROT_NONE, or exactly
223.    one host has writers and all other hosts are PROT_NONE. Even a
224.    correctly `clflush`-ed write from host A is not legal to read on
225.    host B until ownership is flipped via the `obmm_set_ownership()`
226.    syscall. That is one syscall per message — incompatible with
227.    `am_short` latency goals.
228. 2. **arm64 user-space lacks `dc ivac`** (invalidate by VA to PoC, EL0
229.    typically only exposes `dc civac` = clean+invalidate). A reader-side
230.    "discard cache, then load" sequence would have to clean+invalidate
231.    on every poll, doubling the writer-side cost.
232. 3. **UCX has no precedent** for cross-host cacheable shared memory with
233.    manual coherence on a hot data path. `ucs_arch_clear_cache` exists
234.    (x86: `mfence; clflush; mfence` per line; arm64: `dc cvau` +
235.    `ic ivau`) but is used only for instruction-cache coherence
236.    (JIT / code patching), never for transport data. All cross-host
237.    UCX transports either use a NIC (NIC handles coherence) or rely
238.    on a HW-coherent fabric. Inventing a new pattern here would carry
239.    risk far above what NC mapping costs.
240. 4. **Bulk-flip ownership** (writer holds write, batches N messages,
241.    flips, reader batches N reads) is a possible future path for
242.    `put/get` bulk transfers but trades latency for throughput and
243.    defeats AM short's purpose. Out of scope for v1.
244. 
245. NC (`O_SYNC`) avoids all four issues at the cost of uncached load/store
246. performance, which the project owner has accepted.
247.
````

28.  * other's (exporter_dcna, exporter_deid). */
29. typedef struct uct_obmm_device_addr {
30.     uint64_t exporter_dcna;
31.     uint64_t exporter_deid_hi;
32.     uint64_t exporter_deid_lo;
33. } uct_obmm_device_addr_t;
34. 
35. 
36. /* Wire-format iface address: identifies the FIFO slot inside the region
37.  * named by the device address, plus enough geometry for the peer to
38.  * validate compatibility before trusting any pointer math. */
39. typedef struct uct_obmm_iface_addr {
40.     uint32_t slot_index;
41.     uint32_t generation;
42.     uint32_t pid;
43.     uint32_t fifo_size;
44.     uint32_t fifo_elem_size;
45.     uint32_t bcopy_seg_size;  /* v2: per-elem bcopy desc size; locks
46.                                   max_bcopy and slot_stride. v1 wrote 0
47.                                   here (named `reserved`); slot geometry
48.                                   checks prevent v1↔v2 mixing. */
49. } uct_obmm_iface_addr_t;
50. 
51. 
52. typedef struct uct_obmm_iface_common_config {
53.     uct_iface_config_t     super;
54.     double                 bandwidth; /* Memory bandwidth in bytes per second */
55. } uct_obmm_iface_common_config_t;
56. 
57. 
58. typedef struct uct_obmm_iface_config {
59.     uct_obmm_iface_common_config_t super;
60.     unsigned                       fifo_size;       /* FIFO ring depth (power of 2) */
61.     unsigned                       fifo_elem_size;  /* bytes per element (incl. hdr) */
62.     unsigned                       bcopy_seg_size;  /* v2: bytes per bcopy desc */
63.     size_t                         fifo_max_poll;   /* RX completions per progress() */
64. } uct_obmm_iface_config_t;
65. 
66. 
67. typedef struct uct_obmm_iface {
68.     uct_base_iface_t         super;
69.     struct {
70.         double               bandwidth; /* Memory bandwidth in bytes per second */
71.     } config;
72. 
73.     /* Local receive state -- our own slot inside the local export region. */
74.     uct_obmm_pool_t          pool;            /* attached local export pool */
75.     uct_obmm_region_t       *region;          /* points into md->regions[]  */
76.     void                    *recv_slot;       /* base of our slot bytes     */
77.     uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t     *recv_ctl;        /* head/tail in our slot      */
78.     void                    *recv_elems;      /* fifo[] in our slot         */
79.     void                    *recv_descs;      /* v2: bcopy desc[] in slot   */
80.     uint32_t                 slot_index;      /* our slot index in pool     */
81.     uint32_t                 generation;      /* our slot generation token  */
82.     uint64_t                 read_index;      /* monotonic RX cursor        */
83. 
84.     /* Geometry, cached from config. fifo_size MUST be power of 2. */
85.     unsigned                 fifo_size;
86.     unsigned                 fifo_mask;       /* fifo_size - 1              */
87.     unsigned                 fifo_elem_size;
88.     unsigned                 bcopy_seg_size;  /* v2: == max_bcopy           */
89.     size_t                   fifo_max_poll;
90. 
91.     /* Pending send arbiter (mirrors mm). pending_add queues UCP requests
92.      * here when peer FIFO is full; iface_progress dispatches them after
93.      * draining receives so any tail advance becomes immediately visible
94.      * to retries. Without this, UCP busy-spins inside ucp_do_am_bcopy_*
95.      * on UCS_ERR_BUSY from a no-op pending_add. */
96.     ucs_arbiter_t            arbiter;
97. } uct_obmm_iface_t;
98. 
99. 
100. extern ucs_config_field_t uct_obmm_iface_config_table[];
101. 
102. ucs_status_t
103. uct_obmm_iface_query_tl_devices(uct_md_h md,
104.                                 uct_tl_device_resource_t **tl_devices_p,
105.                                 unsigned *num_tl_devices_p);
106. 
107. UCS_CLASS_DECLARE_NEW_FUNC(uct_obmm_iface_t, uct_iface_t, uct_md_h, uct_worker_h,
108.                            const uct_iface_params_t*, const uct_iface_config_t*);
109. 
110. #endif

70. 
71. ### Slot stride
72. 
73. ```
74. slot_stride = align_up(
75.     sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t) +
76.     fifo_size * elem_size +
77.     fifo_size * seg_size,
78.     cacheline)
79. ```
80. 
81. The pool's `slot_count` (compile-time `UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT = 64`)
82. **times** `slot_stride` MUST fit in `region->length` (128 MiB minus pool
83.  header overhead). Defaults are picked to favor short-path coverage over
84.  maximum local process count; callers may shrink (not grow) `seg_size` /
85.  `fifo_size` if they need more slots.
86. 
87. Default budget check:
88. ```
89. fifo_size       =     64
90. elem_size       =   4160   (UCT max_short = 4144 total bytes)
91. seg_size        =  16384   (max_bcopy = 16384)
92. ctl + slot data = 128 + 64*(4160+16384) = ~1284 KiB / slot
93. slot_count      =     64
94. total           = ~ 80 MiB / 128 MiB                     ✓
95. ```
96. These defaults keep bcopy at a 16KiB power-of-two while moving the effective
97. UCP eager-short boundary above common 2048-byte and 4096-byte payloads.
98. A 4096-byte payload plus the 8-byte UCT short header needs 4104 bytes, so
99. `max_short` has to exceed 4096 if the goal is to keep 4096-byte payloads on
100. the short path.
101. 
102. If a user bumps `seg_size` to 32768, total grows to ~144 MiB and pool
103. attach fails with a clear error pointing at the geometry knobs.
104. 
105. When the last local iface on an export exits, UCX resets the entire local
106. export region to zero before another attach may re-initialize the pool.
107. 
108. ---
109.

248. 
249. All under `UCX_OBMM_*` prefix.
250. 
251. | knob                      | default | meaning                          |
252. |---------------------------|---------|----------------------------------|
253. | FIFO_SIZE                 |    64   | ring depth (power of 2)          |
254. | FIFO_ELEM_SIZE            |  4160   | bytes per FIFO elem (incl. 16B hdr) → UCT max_short = 4144 total bytes |
255. | BCOPY_SEG_SIZE   (v2 NEW) | 16384   | bytes per paired desc → max_bcopy |
256. | FIFO_MAX_POLL             |    16   | RX completions per progress()     |
257. | MEMIDS        (optional)  |   ""    | comma-separated explicit shmdev memids (for example `1,2`); when set, obmm queries only these memids instead of scanning all shmdevs. Regardless of whether this knob is set, discovery is fail-fast: any discovered/requested shmdev that is missing, unusable, or yields an invalid export/import topology fails md_open |
258. 
259. Validation at iface init:
260. - `FIFO_SIZE` > 0, power of 2
261. - `FIFO_ELEM_SIZE` > sizeof(elem_hdr) and `(elem_size - hdr) <= UINT16_MAX`
262. - `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE` > 0 and `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE <= UINT16_MAX`
263. - `slot_count * slot_stride + pool_overhead <= region->length`
264.

7. #ifndef UCT_OBMM_FIFO_H_
8. #define UCT_OBMM_FIFO_H_
9. 
10. #include <ucs/arch/cpu.h>
11. #include <ucs/sys/compiler.h>
12. #include <ucs/sys/compiler_def.h>
13. #include <ucs/sys/ptr_arith.h>
14. 
15. #include <stdint.h>
16. 
17. 
18. /* Element flags carried in the shared FIFO element header. */
19. enum {
20.     /* Toggled every FIFO wraparound; receiver uses this to detect a freshly
21.      * written element without taking a tail/head delta lock. */
22.     UCT_OBMM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_OWNER = UCS_BIT(0),
23. 
24.     /* Set by senders that wrote via am_bcopy (pack_cb output stored in the
25.      * payload area starting at elem+1, with NO 8-byte am_short header
26.      * prefix). When clear, the element was written via am_short and
27.      * &elem->header + length covers the [hdr][payload] buffer. */
28.     UCT_OBMM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_BCOPY = UCS_BIT(1)
29. };
30. 
31. 
32. /* Per-slot FIFO control header. Lives at offset 0 of every allocated slot in
33.  * the obmm pool. Producers serialize `head` reservation with a token lock:
34.  * on target aarch64 NC mappings, cross-node CAS updates memory but its return
35.  * value is not a reliable ownership result. Consumers read/write `tail` to
36.  * release space. Control fields are accessed via non-cacheable mappings,
37.  * therefore all updates must be paired with bus fences
38.  * (ucs_memory_bus_*_fence), not CPU fences. */
39. typedef struct uct_obmm_fifo_ctl {
40.     /* 1st cacheline: producer-touched */
41.     volatile uint64_t head;
42.     volatile uint64_t lock;
43.     UCS_CACHELINE_PADDING(uint64_t, uint64_t);
44. 
45.     /* 2nd cacheline: consumer-touched */
46.     volatile uint64_t tail;
47.     UCS_CACHELINE_PADDING(uint64_t);
48. } UCS_V_ALIGNED(UCS_SYS_CACHE_LINE_SIZE) uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t;
49. 
50. 
51. /* FIFO element header. The element body (am short header + payload) follows
52.  * immediately. Total element stride is iface->config.fifo_elem_size, which
53.  * the iface chooses so that header+payload <= elem_size. */
54. typedef struct uct_obmm_fifo_element {
55.     uint8_t  flags;       /* UCT_OBMM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_xx */
56.     uint8_t  am_id;       /* active message id */
57.     uint16_t length;      /* payload length (excluding am_short header) */
58.     uint32_t generation;  /* owner-slot generation token; receiver discards
59.                              elements whose generation doesn't match the
60.                              slot's current meta.generation */
61.     uint64_t header;      /* am_short 64-bit header */
62.     /* payload[length] follows here */
63. } UCS_S_PACKED uct_obmm_fifo_element_t;
64. 
65.

110. ## FIFO element layout
111. 
112. `uct_obmm_fifo_element_t` (16 bytes, packed) is unchanged from v1:
113. 
114. | field      | bytes | notes                                          |
115. |------------|-------|------------------------------------------------|
116. | flags      |   1   | OWNER bit + BCOPY bit                          |
117. | am_id      |   1   |                                                |
118. | length     |   2   | u16 — payload bytes (excl. am_short hdr)       |
119. | generation |   4   | slot generation token at TX time               |
120. | header     |   8   | am_short user-visible 8B header (unused bcopy) |
121. 
122. **am_short payload** still lives inline at `elem + 1` in the FIFO area.
123. Wire format and `max_short = elem_size - 16` are unchanged.
124. 
125. **am_bcopy payload** (NEW in v2) lives in the paired `desc[N]` instead
126. of inside the FIFO element body. The element body is unused for bcopy;
127. on bcopy the sender writes:
128. - `elem->flags  = OWNER | BCOPY`
129. - `elem->am_id  = id`
130. - `elem->length = pack_cb_returned_length`     (≤ seg_size, so ≤ u16max)
131. - `elem->generation = ep->expected_generation`
132. - `elem->header = 0` (unused)
133. 
134. Receiver, on seeing FLAG_BCOPY, computes
135. `desc[N] = slot_descs + (idx & mask) * seg_size` and calls
136. `uct_iface_invoke_am(am_id, desc[N], length, 0)`.
137. 
138. Because `desc[N]` is bound 1:1 to `elem[N]`, no extra metadata is
139. exchanged in the FIFO element to locate the desc.
140. 
141. ### `length` field width
142. 
143. `elem->length` stays `uint16_t`, capping `seg_size` at 65535. We reject
144. larger `seg_size` at iface init. If a future `seg_size > 64KiB` is
145. needed, widen `length` to `uint32_t` and update the compatibility checks.
146. 
147. ---
148. 
149. ## Sender side (`obmm_ep`)
150. 
151. Both `am_short` and `am_bcopy` reserve a slot identically:
152. 
153. ```
154. 1. load head from peer_ctl->head
155. 2. if (head - cached_tail) >= fifo_size:
````

````
40. 
41. Inside the 128 MiB exported region:
42. 
43. ```
44. +-------------------------------------------------------+ offset 0
45. | uct_obmm_pool_hdr_t (magic, state, geometry)          |
46. +-------------------------------------------------------+
47. | alloc_bitmap[bitmap_words]                            |
48. +-------------------------------------------------------+
49. | slot_meta[slot_count]  (gen, owner_pid, starttime, …) |
50. +-------------------------------------------------------+ hdr->slot_array_offset
51. | slot[0]:                                              |
52. |   uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t  (head + tail, padded)          |
53. |   fifo_elem[fifo_size]  (elem_size each)              |
54. |   bcopy_desc[fifo_size] (seg_size each)   <-- NEW v2  |
55. +-------------------------------------------------------+
56. | slot[1]: …                                            |
57. …
58. ```
59. 
60. **Key invariant (v2)**: every FIFO element `elem[N]` (N = `idx & mask`)
61. has a paired `desc[N]` of `seg_size` bytes in the same slot. Lifetime of
62. `desc[N]` is **identical** to lifetime of `elem[N]` — both are released
63. together when the receiver bumps tail past index N, and both are
64. overwritten together by the sender that claims index N+fifo_size.
65. 
66. This eliminates the cross-host desc free-list problem: there is no
67. separate desc allocator, no per-desc CAS, and no risk of the desc pool
68. running dry while FIFO slots remain available. The FIFO already has
69. exactly the right backpressure semantics.
70.
````

</details>

```
1) **Yes, it fits.**  
`slot_stride = align_up(128 + 64*32792 + 64*16384, 64) = 3,147,392`; pool overhead is `slot_offset = 832`; total is `832 + 32*3,147,392 = 100,717,376`, leaving **33,500,352 bytes (~31.95 MiB)** slack in 128 MiB. The `uint16` caps still pass. (`ucx\src\uct\obmm\base\obmm_fifo.h:71-79`, `ucx\src\uct\obmm\base\obmm_pool.c:63-75`, `ucx\src\uct\obmm\base\obmm_pool.h:40-66`, `ucx\src\uct\obmm\base\obmm_iface.c:345-363`)

2) **One material assumption is wrong:** “power-of-two business sizes” is **not** generally true at UCP level.  
For AM short, it does line up here: UCP subtracts its 8-byte `ucp_am_hdr_t`, so `32776 -> 32768` payload. But for bcopy, UCP uses `max_bcopy - only_hdr_size`, and AM bcopy `only_hdr_size` is at least 8 bytes, so `16384` means **16376-byte payload**, not 16 KiB. (`ucx\src\uct\api\uct.h:1094-1101`, `ucx\src\ucp\core\ucp_am.h:51-89`, `ucx\src\ucp\core\ucp_ep.c:2435-2463,2870-2878`, `ucx\src\ucp\core\ucp_request.c:602-619`, `ucx\src\ucp\core\ucp_am.c:1738-1755`)

3) **Definitely update beyond raw defaults:**  
- slot-budget/rationale text in `ucx\src\uct\obmm\DESIGN.md:81-103`  
- config table in `ucx\src\uct\obmm\DESIGN.md:251-263`  
- verification text mentioning default seg size in `ucx\src\uct\obmm\DESIGN.md:324-335`  
- slot-count comment in `ucx\src\uct\obmm\base\obmm_iface.h:18-22`  
- config descriptions in `ucx\src\uct\obmm\base\obmm_iface.c:46-60`  
Also fix the misleading “shrink seg_size/fifo_size if they need more slots” wording; runtime knobs do **not** increase `slot_count`. (`DESIGN.md:81-85`)

4) **Subtle notes to call out:**  
- This is a real **compatibility/capacity** change: mixed old/new geometries will fail reachability, even though the struct layout is unchanged. (`obmm_iface.c:185-197`)  
- The cap becomes **32 attached ifaces/slots**, not strictly “32 processes,” if a process can open more than one iface. (`obmm_iface.h:18-22`)  
- `ucx_info` will show UCT totals (`max_short=32776`, `max_bcopy=16384`), not the UCP payload thresholds.

### 💬 Copilot

- **Fits, internally consistent.** `slot_stride=3,147,392`, `slot_offset=832`, `required=100,717,376`, so it leaves **33,500,352 B (~31.95 MiB)** slack in 128 MiB. `max_short=32776` and `max_bcopy=16384` both stay under the `uint16` guards. A 32 KiB bcopy with the same 32 KiB short geometry would overflow by **54,080 B**.

- **Material bad assumption:** `am.max_bcopy` is a **total** UCT size, not business payload. So `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE=16384` gives UCP single-bcopy payload ≈ **16376 B** (and AM-reply short is also below 32 KiB). Only plain request/tag eager-short cleanly lands at **32768 B** payload.

- **Definitely update:**  
  `ucx\src\uct\obmm\DESIGN.md:81-103, 251-263, 324-335`;  
  `ucx\src\uct\obmm\base\obmm_iface.h:18-22`;  
  `ucx\src\uct\obmm\base\obmm_iface.c:46-60`.  
  Especially fix the misleading “shrink seg_size/fifo_size if they need more slots” wording.

- **Subtle notes to mention:** this is a **compatibility/capacity** retune: mixed old/new geometries will fail pool attach / reachability; and the cap is **32 attached ifaces/slots**, not necessarily 32 processes.

251. | knob                      | default | meaning                          |
252. |---------------------------|---------|----------------------------------|
253. | FIFO_SIZE                 |    64   | ring depth (power of 2)          |
254. | FIFO_ELEM_SIZE            |  4160   | bytes per FIFO elem (incl. 16B hdr) → UCT max_short = 4144 total bytes |
255. | BCOPY_SEG_SIZE   (v2 NEW) | 16384   | bytes per paired desc → max_bcopy |
256. | FIFO_MAX_POLL             |    16   | RX completions per progress()     |
257. | MEMIDS        (optional)  |   ""    | comma-separated explicit shmdev memids (for example `1,2`); when set, obmm queries only these memids instead of scanning all shmdevs. Regardless of whether this knob is set, discovery is fail-fast: any discovered/requested shmdev that is missing, unusable, or yields an invalid export/import topology fails md_open |
258. 
259. Validation at iface init:
260. - `FIFO_SIZE` > 0, power of 2
261. - `FIFO_ELEM_SIZE` > sizeof(elem_hdr) and `(elem_size - hdr) <= UINT16_MAX`
262. - `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE` > 0 and `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE <= UINT16_MAX`
263. - `slot_count * slot_stride + pool_overhead <= region->length`
264. 
265. ---
266. 
267. ## Future scope (not in v2)
268. 
269. - `am_zcopy`: requires UCT MD memory-handle plumbing (`mem_reg`,
270.   `mkey_pack`, `mem_attach`). Currently obmm has no MD-level
271.   registration — every peer access is via the pre-existing 128 MiB
272.   region. Out of scope until libobmm-aware md is added.
273. - `put_bcopy / get_bcopy`: blocked by the same MD plumbing; UCP RMA
274.   cannot be served by the FIFO-only data path.
275. - Real pending arbiter: needed only if profiling shows BUSY-retry
276.   storms.
277. - Multi-region per node, NUMA-aware slot placement.
278. - Variable-size desc allocator (mm-style mpool) to cover medium-size
279.   messages without burning seg_size per FIFO depth.
280. 
281. ---
282. 
283. ## Receive-side fence ordering (full bus fence at tail release)
284. 
285. `ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()` on aarch64 is `dmb oshst` — store→store
286. only. It does NOT order prior loads against subsequent stores. The
287. receiver's lifetime invariant requires:
288. 
289. ```
290. loads from desc[N]  HAPPENS-BEFORE  store to recv_ctl->tail = N+1
291. ```
292. 
293. Otherwise a sender that observes the new tail can reuse `desc[N]` while
294. the receiver core still has outstanding loads in flight from the old
295. lap's payload. We therefore use `uct_obmm_bus_full_fence()` (defined
296. locally in `obmm_fifo.h`: `dmb osh` on aarch64, `mfence` on x86,
297. `sync` on ppc64, `fence iorw,iorw` on rv64) before the tail store, not
298. the bus_store fence.
299. 
300. Why a local helper rather than adding `ucs_memory_bus_fence()` for all
301. archs in `ucs/arch/`: AGENTS.md restricts changes to
302. `ucx/src/uct/obmm/`. If/when the helper proves useful elsewhere, it can
303. be promoted to ucs/arch — but that is a separate ask.
304. 
305. ## Receive-buffer semantics for AM handler
306. 
307. `invoke_am(..., desc, length, 0)` — the trailing `0` (no
308. `UCT_CB_PARAM_FLAG_DESC`) means the data pointer is valid **only for the
309. duration of the callback**. The handler MUST NOT retain it; UCP knows
310. this contract and copies into its own buffer when persistence is
311. needed.
312. 
313. This is by design: the desc lifetime is bound 1:1 to the FIFO element
314. slot, so as soon as the receiver advances `tail` past N, the sender is
315. free to overwrite `desc[N]` on the next lap. There is no separate desc
316. allocator to support post-callback retention.
317. 
318. If a future need arises to support `UCT_CB_PARAM_FLAG_DESC`-style
319. returnable descriptors (e.g. for AM zcopy or large-message rendezvous
320. without copy), it requires a real per-iface mpool of receive
321. descriptors that the upper layer can hold and release explicitly —
322. mirroring `uct_mm_recv_desc_t`. Out of scope for v2.
323.

224. static unsigned uct_obmm_iface_progress(uct_iface_h tl_iface)
225. {
226.     uct_obmm_iface_t        *iface = ucs_derived_of(tl_iface, uct_obmm_iface_t);
227.     unsigned                 polled = 0;
228.     uct_obmm_fifo_element_t *elem;
229.     uint8_t                  flags;
230.     uint8_t                  expected_owner;
231.     size_t                   max_poll = iface->fifo_max_poll;
232. 
233.     while (polled < max_poll) {
234.         elem = uct_obmm_slot_elem(iface->recv_elems, iface->read_index,
235.                                   iface->fifo_mask, iface->fifo_elem_size);
236. 
237.         /* Owner bit alternates each lap of the ring; pass 0 expects 1, pass
238.          * 1 expects 0, etc. Combined with zero-fill on slot allocation, this
239.          * means an unwritten slot reads as flags==0 and is correctly skipped
240.          * on the very first lap. */
241.         expected_owner = ((iface->read_index / iface->fifo_size) & 1u) ?
242.                          0u : UCT_OBMM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_OWNER;
243. 
244.         flags = elem->flags;
245.         if ((flags & UCT_OBMM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_OWNER) != expected_owner) {
246.             break;
247.         }
248. 
249.         ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
250. 
251.         if (elem->generation != iface->generation) {
252.             /* Stale write from a previous slot owner (we were torn down and
253.              * re-allocated this slot). Drop silently. */
254.             ucs_trace_data("obmm: drop stale elem (gen=%u expected=%u) "
255.                            "at idx=%lu", elem->generation, iface->generation,
256.                            (unsigned long)iface->read_index);
257.         } else if (flags & UCT_OBMM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_BCOPY) {
258.             /* am_bcopy: payload is in the paired desc[N], not in the FIFO
259.              * element body. The bus_load_fence above orders this load
260.              * with respect to the sender's bus_store_fence + flag write. */
261.             void *desc = uct_obmm_slot_desc(iface->recv_descs,
262.                                             iface->read_index,
263.                                             iface->fifo_mask,
264.                                             iface->bcopy_seg_size);
265.             uct_iface_invoke_am(&iface->super, elem->am_id,
266.                                 desc, elem->length, 0);
267.         } else {
268.             /* am_short: contiguous [header(8B)][payload] starting at
269.              * &elem->header. elem->length already includes the 8B header. */
270.             uct_iface_invoke_am(&iface->super, elem->am_id,
271.                                 &elem->header, elem->length, 0);
272.         }
273. 
274.         iface->read_index++;
275.         polled++;
276.     }
277. 
278.     if (polled > 0) {
279.         /* Full bus fence: orders the AM handler's LOADS from desc[]/elem
280.          * payload BEFORE the STORE that publishes the new tail. A plain
281.          * bus_store_fence (e.g. dmb oshst on aarch64) only orders
282.          * store→store, which would let a sender observe the advanced
283.          * tail and overwrite desc[N] while we still have outstanding
284.          * loads in flight. See obmm_fifo.h:uct_obmm_bus_full_fence. */
285.         uct_obmm_bus_full_fence();
286.         iface->recv_ctl->tail = iface->read_index;
287.     }
288. 
289.     /* Drain any UCP requests waiting on TX backpressure. The peer-side
290.      * tail advance we just published may also have freed slots that *our*
291.      * pending eps have been waiting for; dispatch with a fresh head/tail
292.      * snapshot so retries see the latest state. Without this dispatch,
293.      * UCS_ERR_BUSY-only pending_add caused a livelock under symmetric
294.      * bidirectional load (osu_bibw at size==BCOPY_SEG_SIZE). */
295.     ucs_arbiter_dispatch(&iface->arbiter, 1, uct_obmm_ep_process_pending,
296.                          &polled);
297. 
298.     return polled;
299. }
300.

303. {
304.     (void)flags;
305.     ucs_memory_cpu_fence();
306.     UCT_TL_IFACE_STAT_FENCE(ucs_derived_of(tl_iface, uct_base_iface_t));
307.     return UCS_OK;
308. }

320. static UCS_CLASS_INIT_FUNC(uct_obmm_iface_t, uct_md_h tl_md, uct_worker_h worker,
321.                            const uct_iface_params_t *params,
322.                            const uct_iface_config_t *tl_config)
323. {
324.     uct_obmm_iface_config_t *config = ucs_derived_of(tl_config,
325.                                                      uct_obmm_iface_config_t);
326.     uct_obmm_md_t           *md     = ucs_derived_of(tl_md, uct_obmm_md_t);
327.     uct_obmm_region_t       *region;
328.     size_t                   stride;
329.     size_t                   required;
330.     ucs_status_t             status;
331. 
332.     if (config->fifo_size == 0) {
333.         ucs_error("obmm: FIFO_SIZE must be > 0");
334.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
335.     }
336.     if (!ucs_is_pow2(config->fifo_size)) {
337.         ucs_error("obmm: FIFO_SIZE (%u) must be a power of 2",
338.                   config->fifo_size);
339.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
340.     }
341.     if (config->fifo_elem_size <= sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_element_t)) {
342.         ucs_error("obmm: FIFO_ELEM_SIZE (%u) must be > %zu",
343.                   config->fifo_elem_size, sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_element_t));
344.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
345.     }
346.     /* elem->length is uint16_t; reject geometries whose advertised
347.      * max_short / max_bcopy would not fit in that field. */
348.     if ((config->fifo_elem_size - sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_element_t)) >
349.         UINT16_MAX) {
350.         ucs_error("obmm: FIFO_ELEM_SIZE (%u) too large; payload area must fit "
351.                   "in uint16 (max %zu)",
352.                   config->fifo_elem_size,
353.                   (size_t)UINT16_MAX + sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_element_t));
354.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
355.     }
356.     if (config->bcopy_seg_size == 0) {
357.         ucs_error("obmm: BCOPY_SEG_SIZE must be > 0");
358.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
359.     }
360.     if (config->bcopy_seg_size > UINT16_MAX) {
361.         ucs_error("obmm: BCOPY_SEG_SIZE (%u) too large; max_bcopy must fit "
362.                   "in uint16 (max %u)",
363.                   config->bcopy_seg_size, (unsigned)UINT16_MAX);
364.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
365.     }
366. 
367.     region = uct_obmm_md_export_region(md);
368.     if (region == NULL) {
369.         ucs_error("obmm: cannot create iface; this MD has no local export "
370.                   "region");
371.         return UCS_ERR_NO_DEVICE;
372.     }
373. 
374.     /* Compute slot stride as size_t, then validate it fits in u32 (the
375.      * pool header field is u32) AND that the total region budget covers
376.      * slot_count slots. Failing here is preferred over silently capping
377.      * BCOPY_SEG_SIZE — UCP would happily make protocol decisions based
378.      * on a quietly reduced max_bcopy. */
379.     stride = uct_obmm_slot_stride(config->fifo_size, config->fifo_elem_size,
380.                                   config->bcopy_seg_size);
381.     if (stride > UINT32_MAX) {
382.         ucs_error("obmm: slot stride %zu exceeds uint32_t (fifo_size=%u "
383.                   "elem=%u seg=%u); reduce one of the geometry knobs",
384.                   stride, config->fifo_size, config->fifo_elem_size,
385.                   config->bcopy_seg_size);
386.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
387.     }
388.     required = uct_obmm_pool_required_size(UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT,
389.                                            (uint32_t)stride);
390.     if (required > region->length) {
391.         ucs_error("obmm: geometry does not fit in region: "
392.                   "fifo_size=%u elem_size=%u seg_size=%u stride=%zu "
393.                   "slot_count=%u required=%zu region=%zu. "
394.                   "Reduce UCX_OBMM_BCOPY_SEG_SIZE or UCX_OBMM_FIFO_SIZE.",
395.                   config->fifo_size, config->fifo_elem_size,
396.                   config->bcopy_seg_size, stride,
397.                   UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT, required, region->length);
398.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
399.     }

34. /* In-region pool header. Lives at offset 0 of the local export region. All
35.  * fields are written via non-cacheable mappings: state transitions must be
36.  * paired with ucs_memory_bus_store_fence so peers (potentially on another
37.  * host) see the geometry before the READY transition. During cleanup, INITING
38.  * is only a transient coordination state; once reset completes, the shared
39.  * region is fully zero again. */
40. typedef struct uct_obmm_pool_hdr {
41.     uint64_t magic;             /* UCT_OBMM_POOL_MAGIC */
42.     uint32_t state;             /* UCT_OBMM_POOL_STATE_xx, atomic */
43.     uint32_t slot_count;
44.     uint32_t slot_size;
45.     uint64_t slot_array_offset; /* offset (from region base) of slot 0 */
46.     uint32_t bitmap_words;      /* number of u64 words in alloc bitmap */
47.     uint32_t initializer_pid;   /* pid that owned the INITING transition */
48.     uint64_t initializer_starttime;
49.     /* followed by:
50.      *   uint64_t alloc_bitmap[bitmap_words];
51.      *   uct_obmm_slot_meta_t slot_meta[slot_count];
52.      */
53. } uct_obmm_pool_hdr_t;
54. 
55. 
56. /* Per-slot ownership metadata. Stored adjacent to the bitmap, separate from
57.  * the slot's actual FIFO contents. */
58. typedef struct uct_obmm_slot_meta {
59.     uint32_t state;            /* UCT_OBMM_SLOT_STATE_xx */
60.     uint32_t generation;       /* monotonically increasing; bumped on free,
61.                                   scavenge, and when readers must discard
62.                                   in-flight stale elements */
63.     uint32_t owner_pid;
64.     uint32_t reserved;
65.     uint64_t owner_starttime;  /* /proc/<pid>/stat field 22, for liveness */
66. } uct_obmm_slot_meta_t;
67. 
68. 
69. /* Convenience accessor populated by uct_obmm_pool_attach. Pointers point
70.  * into the mapped region; nothing is owned by this struct. */
71. typedef struct uct_obmm_pool {
72.     void                  *base;     /* region base (pool hdr) */
73.     size_t                 length;   /* mapped region size */
74.     uct_obmm_pool_hdr_t   *hdr;
75.     volatile uint64_t     *bitmap;
76.     uct_obmm_slot_meta_t  *meta;
77.     void                  *slots;    /* base + hdr->slot_array_offset */
78.     uint32_t               slot_count;
79.     uint32_t               slot_size;
80. } uct_obmm_pool_t;

66. /* Compute slot stride: control header + fifo_size * elem_size + (v2)
67.  * fifo_size * bcopy_seg_size, cacheline aligned so that adjacent slots
68.  * don't share a line. Returned as size_t; callers must validate the
69.  * result fits in the uint32_t pool_hdr->slot_size field before passing
70.  * to pool_attach. */
71. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE size_t
72. uct_obmm_slot_stride(unsigned fifo_size, unsigned fifo_elem_size,
73.                      unsigned bcopy_seg_size)
74. {
75.     return ucs_align_up(sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t) +
76.                         ((size_t)fifo_size * fifo_elem_size) +
77.                         ((size_t)fifo_size * bcopy_seg_size),
78.                         UCS_SYS_CACHE_LINE_SIZE);
79. }

### 💬 Copilot

**已经改成只支持 32 个本地 slot/attach 了**，并把默认几何调成：

- `UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT = 32`
- `FIFO_ELEM_SIZE = 32792` → `max_short = 32776` total bytes，也就是 **32768B 业务 payload + 8B short header**
- `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE = 16384` → **raw UCT `max_bcopy = 16KiB`**

这套配置明显偏向 `short`，而且按你刚确认的口径，把 **bcopy 的原始 UCT 上限** 对齐成了 2 的幂。总占用现在约 **96 MiB / 128 MiB**，还能留出余量；如果再把 `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE` 提到 `32768`，就会超出 region。文档也同步改了，明确了一个重要点：**short 的 32KiB 是业务 payload 尺寸，而 bcopy 的 16KiB 是 raw UCT cap；上层 UCP/MPI 的单次业务 payload 会因协议头略小一点。**

<sub>⏱️ 381m 39s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

**你可以把“原始 UCT 上限”理解成：obmm 传输层对 UCP 宣布的单次调用预算，不是纯业务 payload。**  
在我们这边，`max_bcopy` 直接等于 `bcopy_seg_size`，也就是 `iface_query()` 里上报给 UCP 的 `attr-\>cap.am.max_bcopy`；UCP 再把这块预算分成“自己的协议头 + 业务数据”一起塞进一次 `uct_ep_am_bcopy()` 里。代码上就是：

- obmm 上报：`max_short = fifo_elem_size - elem_hdr`，`max_bcopy = bcopy_seg_size`  
  `ucx\src\uct\obmm\base\obmm_iface.c:103-106`
- UCP bcopy 打包时要求：`payload + UCP_hdr \<= max_bcopy`  
  `ucx\src\ucp\tag\eager_snd.c:20-35`
- 多片 bcopy 的 first/middle 片都会先扣掉自己的 UCP 头再放业务数据  
  `ucx\src\ucp\tag\eager_snd.c:61-76,100-112`, `ucx\src\ucp\tag\eager.h:29-50`

所以我前面说的意思是：

- **short** 这次可以精确做到 **32768B 业务 payload**
- **bcopy** 现在做到的是 **16384B 单片 UCT 预算**
- 真正单片业务 payload 会是 **16384 - UCP头大小**

---

**`short \> bcopy` 本身没有功能性问题。**  
UCT 并没有要求 `max_bcopy \>= max_short`，这两个 cap 是独立的；UCP 的选择顺序是：

1. `length \<= max_short` → 走 **short**
2. 否则，如果还在 eager/bcopy 范围内 → 走 **bcopy**
3. 如果一片 bcopy 装不下 → 走 **bcopy_multi**
4. 再大就可能转 **zcopy / rndv**

这段逻辑就在  
`ucx\src\ucp\core\ucp_request.c:602-619`

而 tag eager 协议表也很清楚：只有

- `contig_short`
- `bcopy_single`
- `bcopy_multi`
- `zcopy_single`
- `zcopy_multi`

没有什么 “multi-short” 路径。  
`ucx\src\ucp\tag\eager_snd.c:117-186`

---

**所以大消息不会被分片成多个 short；如果还在 eager 范围内，它会分片成多个 bcopy。**  
这一点你担心得对：**如果把 bcopy 设得太小，会有性能问题**，虽然不是正确性问题。

影响主要是：

- 更早从 **single bcopy** 退化成 **multi bcopy**
- 每片都要带额外 UCP 头
- 片数变多，发送/接收调度次数变多
- FIFO/desc 压力更大，延迟曲线更容易出现台阶

也就是说，**bcopy 太小会让“超过 short 但还没到 zcopy/rndv”的那一段消息更难看。**

---

**放到我们现在这组参数上，真实含义是：**

- `0 ~ 32768B` 业务 payload：优先走 **short**
- `\>32768B` 后：**不会拆成 short**，而是看 UCP 阈值走 **single/multi bcopy** 或直接转 **zcopy/rndv**
- 因为现在 `bcopy` 单片预算只有 `16384`，所以一旦消息大于 short，上层若还停留在 eager/bcopy 区间，基本就会很快进入 **multi-bcopy**

所以如果你的主要关注点是：

- **32KiB 以内极致延迟**：现在这组偏向 short 是合理的
- **32KiB 往上那一段也想平滑**：那 `bcopy=16KiB` 可能偏小，后面值得继续往上抬，或者重新平衡 short/bcopy

一句话概括：

**short 比 bcopy 大没问题；真正的问题不是“会不会错”，而是“超过 short 之后会不会太早掉进 multi-bcopy”。**

---

70. 
71. ### Slot stride
72. 
73. ```
74. slot_stride = align_up(
75.     sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t) +
76.     fifo_size * elem_size +
77.     fifo_size * seg_size,
78.     cacheline)
79. ```
80. 
81. The pool's `slot_count` (compile-time `UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT = 32`)
82. **times** `slot_stride` MUST fit in `region->length` (128 MiB minus pool
83.  header overhead). Defaults are picked to favor short-path coverage over
84.  maximum local process count; lowering `seg_size` and/or `fifo_size`
85.  reduces per-slot footprint, but the supported local attach count remains
86.  the compile-time `slot_count`.
87. 
88. Default budget check:
89. ```
90. fifo_size       =     64
91. elem_size       =  32792   (UCT max_short = 32776 total bytes)
92. seg_size        =  16384   (max_bcopy = 16384)
93. ctl + slot data = 128 + 64*(32792+16384) = ~3074 KiB / slot
94. slot_count      =     32
95. total           = ~ 96 MiB / 128 MiB                     ✓
96. ```
97. These defaults bias the transport toward short: `FIFO_ELEM_SIZE=32792`
98. makes `max_short = 32776`, so a 32768-byte business payload plus the 8-byte
99. UCT short header fits exactly on the short path. `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE=16384`
100. keeps the raw UCT bcopy limit on a 16KiB power-of-two; upper-layer business
101. payload per bcopy fragment is slightly smaller because UCP eager bcopy also
102. packs protocol headers into that segment.
103. 
104. If a user bumps `seg_size` to 32768 while keeping the 32KiB short geometry,
105. the pool overruns the 128 MiB region by 54080 bytes and attach fails with a
106. clear error pointing at the geometry knobs.
107. 
108. When the last local iface on an export exits, UCX resets the entire local
109. export region to zero before another attach may re-initialize the pool.
110.
````

250. ## Configuration knobs
251. 
252. All under `UCX_OBMM_*` prefix.
253. 
254. | knob                      | default | meaning                          |
255. |---------------------------|---------|----------------------------------|
256. | FIFO_SIZE                 |    64   | ring depth (power of 2)          |
257. | FIFO_ELEM_SIZE            | 32792   | bytes per FIFO elem (incl. 16B hdr) → UCT max_short = 32776 total bytes (32768B payload + 8B short hdr) |
258. | BCOPY_SEG_SIZE   (v2 NEW) | 16384   | bytes per paired desc → raw UCT max_bcopy |
259. | FIFO_MAX_POLL             |    16   | RX completions per progress()     |
260. | MEMIDS        (optional)  |   ""    | comma-separated explicit shmdev memids (for example `1,2`); when set, obmm queries only these memids instead of scanning all shmdevs. Regardless of whether this knob is set, discovery is fail-fast: any discovered/requested shmdev that is missing, unusable, or yields an invalid export/import topology fails md_open |
261. 
262. Validation at iface init:
263. - `FIFO_SIZE` > 0, power of 2
264. - `FIFO_ELEM_SIZE` > sizeof(elem_hdr) and `(elem_size - hdr) <= UINT16_MAX`
265. - `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE` > 0 and `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE <= UINT16_MAX`
266. - `slot_count * slot_stride + pool_overhead <= region->length`
267. 
268. ---
269. 
270. ## Future scope (not in v2)
271. 
272. - `am_zcopy`: requires UCT MD memory-handle plumbing (`mem_reg`,
273.   `mkey_pack`, `mem_attach`). Currently obmm has no MD-level
274.   registration — every peer access is via the pre-existing 128 MiB
275.   region. Out of scope until libobmm-aware md is added.
276. - `put_bcopy / get_bcopy`: blocked by the same MD plumbing; UCP RMA
277.   cannot be served by the FIFO-only data path.
278. - Real pending arbiter: needed only if profiling shows BUSY-retry
279.   storms.
280. - Multi-region per node, NUMA-aware slot placement.
281. - Variable-size desc allocator (mm-style mpool) to cover medium-size
282.   messages without burning seg_size per FIFO depth.
283. 
284. ---
285. 
286. ## Receive-side fence ordering (full bus fence at tail release)
287. 
288. `ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()` on aarch64 is `dmb oshst` — store→store
289. only. It does NOT order prior loads against subsequent stores. The
290. receiver's lifetime invariant requires:
291. 
292. ```
293. loads from desc[N]  HAPPENS-BEFORE  store to recv_ctl->tail = N+1
294. ```
295. 
296. Otherwise a sender that observes the new tail can reuse `desc[N]` while
297. the receiver core still has outstanding loads in flight from the old
298. lap's payload. We therefore use `uct_obmm_bus_full_fence()` (defined
299. locally in `obmm_fifo.h`: `dmb osh` on aarch64, `mfence` on x86,
300. `sync` on ppc64, `fence iorw,iorw` on rv64) before the tail store, not
301. the bus_store fence.
302. 
303. Why a local helper rather than adding `ucs_memory_bus_fence()` for all
304. archs in `ucs/arch/`: AGENTS.md restricts changes to
305. `ucx/src/uct/obmm/`. If/when the helper proves useful elsewhere, it can
306. be promoted to ucs/arch — but that is a separate ask.
307. 
308. ## Receive-buffer semantics for AM handler
309. 
310. `invoke_am(..., desc, length, 0)` — the trailing `0` (no
311. `UCT_CB_PARAM_FLAG_DESC`) means the data pointer is valid **only for the
312. duration of the callback**. The handler MUST NOT retain it; UCP knows
313. this contract and copies into its own buffer when persistence is
314. needed.
315. 
316. This is by design: the desc lifetime is bound 1:1 to the FIFO element
317. slot, so as soon as the receiver advances `tail` past N, the sender is
318. free to overwrite `desc[N]` on the next lap. There is no separate desc
319. allocator to support post-callback retention.
320. 
321. If a future need arises to support `UCT_CB_PARAM_FLAG_DESC`-style
322. returnable descriptors (e.g. for AM zcopy or large-message rendezvous
323. without copy), it requires a real per-iface mpool of receive
324. descriptors that the upper layer can hold and release explicitly —
325. mirroring `uct_mm_recv_desc_t`. Out of scope for v2.
326. 
327. ## Verification (no hardware)
328. 
329. Per `.github/skills/ucx-build-verify/SKILL.md`:
330. 
331. 1. Build via `task` agent: `./autogen.sh && ./contrib/configure-devel
332.    && make -j && make install`.
333. 2. `ucx_info -d -t obmm` → confirm `am_short` and `am_bcopy` lines:
334.    `max_short` should report 32776 total bytes (enough for 32768B payload +
335.    8B short header), and `max_bcopy` should reflect raw `seg_size`
336.    (default 16384).
337. 3. `ucx_info -c | grep OBMM` → confirm new `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE` entry.
338. 4. `nm -D libuct.so | grep uct_obmm_ep_am_bcopy` → exists.
339. 5. Hardware-required checks (cross-node MPI, sweep sizes through
340.    `> max_short` and `> max_bcopy`) deferred to user-driven runs on
````

18. /* Element flags carried in the shared FIFO element header. */
19. enum {
20.     /* Toggled every FIFO wraparound; receiver uses this to detect a freshly
21.      * written element without taking a tail/head delta lock. */
22.     UCT_OBMM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_OWNER = UCS_BIT(0),
23. 
24.     /* Set by senders that wrote via am_bcopy (pack_cb output stored in the
25.      * payload area starting at elem+1, with NO 8-byte am_short header
26.      * prefix). When clear, the element was written via am_short and
27.      * &elem->header + length covers the [hdr][payload] buffer. */
28.     UCT_OBMM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_BCOPY = UCS_BIT(1)
29. };
30. 
31. 
32. /* Per-slot FIFO control header. Lives at offset 0 of every allocated slot in
33.  * the obmm pool. Producers serialize `head` reservation with a token lock:
34.  * on target aarch64 NC mappings, cross-node CAS updates memory but its return
35.  * value is not a reliable ownership result. Consumers read/write `tail` to
36.  * release space. Control fields are accessed via non-cacheable mappings,
37.  * therefore all updates must be paired with bus fences
38.  * (ucs_memory_bus_*_fence), not CPU fences. */
39. typedef struct uct_obmm_fifo_ctl {
40.     /* 1st cacheline: producer-touched */
41.     volatile uint64_t head;
42.     volatile uint64_t lock;
43.     UCS_CACHELINE_PADDING(uint64_t, uint64_t);
44. 
45.     /* 2nd cacheline: consumer-touched */
46.     volatile uint64_t tail;
47.     UCS_CACHELINE_PADDING(uint64_t);
48. } UCS_V_ALIGNED(UCS_SYS_CACHE_LINE_SIZE) uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t;
49. 
50. 
51. /* FIFO element header. The element body (am short header + payload) follows
52.  * immediately. Total element stride is iface->config.fifo_elem_size, which
53.  * the iface chooses so that header+payload <= elem_size. */
54. typedef struct uct_obmm_fifo_element {
55.     uint8_t  flags;       /* UCT_OBMM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_xx */
56.     uint8_t  am_id;       /* active message id */
57.     uint16_t length;      /* payload length (excluding am_short header) */
58.     uint32_t generation;  /* owner-slot generation token; receiver discards
59.                              elements whose generation doesn't match the
60.                              slot's current meta.generation */
61.     uint64_t header;      /* am_short 64-bit header */
62.     /* payload[length] follows here */
63. } UCS_S_PACKED uct_obmm_fifo_element_t;

66. /* Compute slot stride: control header + fifo_size * elem_size + (v2)
67.  * fifo_size * bcopy_seg_size, cacheline aligned so that adjacent slots
68.  * don't share a line. Returned as size_t; callers must validate the
69.  * result fits in the uint32_t pool_hdr->slot_size field before passing
70.  * to pool_attach. */
71. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE size_t
72. uct_obmm_slot_stride(unsigned fifo_size, unsigned fifo_elem_size,
73.                      unsigned bcopy_seg_size)
74. {
75.     return ucs_align_up(sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t) +
76.                         ((size_t)fifo_size * fifo_elem_size) +
77.                         ((size_t)fifo_size * bcopy_seg_size),
78.                         UCS_SYS_CACHE_LINE_SIZE);
79. }
80. 
81. 
82. /* Get FIFO control header pointer from a slot base pointer. */
83. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t*
84. uct_obmm_slot_ctl(void *slot_base)
85. {
86.     return (uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t*)slot_base;
87. }
88. 
89. 
90. /* Get FIFO elements array pointer from a slot base pointer. */
91. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE void*
92. uct_obmm_slot_elems(void *slot_base)
93. {
94.     return UCS_PTR_BYTE_OFFSET(slot_base, sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t));
95. }
96. 
97. 
98. /* Get bcopy desc array pointer from a slot base pointer. The desc area
99.  * lives immediately after the FIFO element array. Each desc is
100.  * `bcopy_seg_size` bytes; index N is paired 1:1 with FIFO element N. */
101. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE void*
102. uct_obmm_slot_descs(void *slot_base, unsigned fifo_size,
103.                     unsigned fifo_elem_size)
104. {
105.     return UCS_PTR_BYTE_OFFSET(slot_base,
106.                                sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t) +
107.                                ((size_t)fifo_size * fifo_elem_size));
108. }
109. 
110. 
111. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE uct_obmm_fifo_element_t*
112. uct_obmm_slot_elem(void *elems, uint64_t index, unsigned mask,
113.                    unsigned elem_size)
114. {
115.     return (uct_obmm_fifo_element_t*)
116.            UCS_PTR_BYTE_OFFSET(elems, (size_t)(index & mask) * elem_size);
117. }
118. 
119. 
120. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE void*
121. uct_obmm_slot_desc(void *descs, uint64_t index, unsigned mask,
122.                    unsigned seg_size)
123. {
124.     return UCS_PTR_BYTE_OFFSET(descs, (size_t)(index & mask) * seg_size);
125. }
126. 
127. 
128. /* Full bus-domain fence: orders ALL prior memory accesses (loads and
129.  * stores) before ALL subsequent memory accesses, in the outer-shareable /
130.  * device domain that includes cross-host obmm peers.
131.  *
132.  * Why we need this in addition to ucs_memory_bus_{store,load}_fence:
133.  * the receiver must order its desc[N] LOADS (issued during the AM
134.  * handler) before the STORE that publishes the new tail. On ARM64,
135.  * ucs_memory_bus_store_fence() is `dmb oshst` (store→store only) and
136.  * does not order prior loads. Without this load→store barrier, a sender
137.  * could observe the advanced tail and overwrite desc[N] while the
138.  * receiver still has outstanding loads from the previous lap's payload.
139.  *
140.  * Defined locally in obmm rather than added to ucs/arch to keep the
```

220. 
221. ## Capabilities (`iface_query`)
222. 
223. | flag                            | v1 | v2 | notes                       |
224. |---------------------------------|----|----|-----------------------------|
225. | AM_SHORT                        |  ✓ |  ✓ | max = elem_size - 16        |
226. | AM_BCOPY                        |  ✓ |  ✓ | v1: = max_short (cramped); v2: = seg_size |
227. | PENDING                         |  ✓ |  ✓ | returns BUSY only           |
228. | CONNECT_TO_IFACE                |  ✓ |  ✓ |                             |
229. | CB_SYNC                         |  ✓ |  ✓ |                             |
230. | INTER_NODE                      |  ✓ |  ✓ | required for cross-host UCT (otherwise OMPI's NET_ONLY filter strips us — see ucp_worker.c:2962) |
231. 
232. **Not advertised** in v1/v2: PUT/GET (any), ATOMIC, AM_ZCOPY, EP_CHECK,
233. AM_DUP, ERRHANDLE_PEER. Adding any of these requires a separate design
234. note.
235. 
236. ---
237. 
238. ## Wire-format compat
239. 
240. `uct_obmm_iface_addr_t` carries `(slot_index, generation, pid,
241. fifo_size, fifo_elem_size, bcopy_seg_size)`. v2 **adds** `bcopy_seg_size`
242. (replaces v1's `reserved` u32 → no struct-size change). Two ifaces are
243. mutually reachable iff all three geometry fields match — guarded in
244. `is_reachable_v2`. Pool compatibility is enforced by the shared pool
245. geometry checks in `pool_attach`/`pool_open`; the shared region does not
246. persist a separate pool version word or filler replacement field.
```

### 3) Subtle Compatibility/Protocol Caveats

**A. Wire-format compatibility (`ucx/src/uct/obmm/DESIGN.md:238-246`, `ucx/src/uct/obmm/base/obmm_iface.c:186-198`, `ucx/src/uct/obmm/base/obmm_ep.c:87-97`):**
- **v2 geometry lock**: `uct_obmm_iface_addr_t` carries `(fifo_size, fifo_elem_size, bcopy_seg_size)` on the wire (lines 39–49 in `obmm_iface.h`). Two ifaces are reachable **iff all three match** (enforced in `is_reachable_v2` and `ep_create`).
- **Implication**: Changing the **defaults** does NOT break wire compatibility — it only changes what **new** ifaces advertise. However, if **both** sides of a two-node setup do not apply the retune **simultaneously**, the geometry mismatch will cause `is_reachable_v2` to return 0 with an `"incompatible OBMM geometry"` info_str (`obmm_iface.c:190`).
- **Deployment strategy**: In a cluster with pre-existing obmm regions initialized under the old geometry, **new ifaces with the proposed defaults will NOT be reachable** to old ifaces until the old region is reset (requires last iface exit → region zero). If backward-compatible coexistence is needed, users must **override** `UCX_OBMM_FIFO_ELEM_SIZE` and `UCX_OBMM_BCOPY_SEG_SIZE` to match the already-initialized pool geometry.

**B. Pool state and region reset (`ucx/src/uct/obmm/DESIGN.md:108-110`, `ucx/src/uct/obmm/base/obmm_pool.c:120-130`, `obmm_iface.c:367-399`):**
- The first iface to attach to a fresh (all-zero) region "wins" the geometry via pool init CAS (`pool.c:120`). Subsequent attaches see `READY` state and **must** present matching `(slot_count, slot_size)` or `pool_attach` fails with `UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM` (`pool.c:206-210`).
- `slot_size` = `uct_obmm_slot_stride(fifo_size, fifo_elem_size, bcopy_seg_size)`. Because the proposed retune **keeps slot_stride identical** (3,147,392 bytes), ifaces configured with the new defaults **would** match the pool header's `slot_size` field... **BUT** `is_reachable_v2` **also** checks `fifo_elem_size` and `bcopy_seg_size` individually (not just their combined stride), so the geometry mismatch still prevents connection (`obmm_iface.c:187-188`).
- **Subtle risk**: If the user mistakenly assumes "stride unchanged → compatible," they will hit the `is_reachable_v2` guard. The error message at `obmm_iface.c:190-196` is clear, but worth documenting that **all three geometry knobs must match**, not just the derived stride.

**C. UCP protocol selection edge case (`ucx/src/ucp/core/ucp_request.c:599-641`, `ucx/src/ucp/tag/eager_snd.c` per user context):**
- User stated: `"if length > max_bcopy-only_hdr_size then bcopy_multi"` and chose to `"treat the bcopy power-of-two target as the raw UCT cap, not exact upper-layer business payload."`
- **Current** OSU 32768B test: length=32768 → UCP eager short if header+payload ≤ max_short (current 32776 total) → **just fits** on short.
- **Proposed** OSU 32768B test: length=32768 → business payload alone exceeds new max_short (16392 total = 16384 payload + 8 hdr) → UCP selects **bcopy**. If the raw UCT max_bcopy (32768) is ≥ the **packed** UCP eager bcopy (business payload + UCP hdr), the test runs in a **single bcopy** fragment. If UCP hdr pushes it over, it fragments.
- **Material caveat**: The user's plan explicitly treats 32768 as the **raw UCT cap**, meaning a **32768-byte business payload** will NOT fit in one bcopy (it would need `32768 + sizeof(UCP eager bcopy hdr)` bytes). This is **intentional** per the user's statement, but confirm that OSU `osu_bw` with size=32768 will **fragment** into bcopy_multi (2 fragments: ~32760 + ~8) rather than a single bcopy. If the goal is "no fragmentation at 32768," the user would need `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE` slightly larger than 32768 + UCP hdr overhead.
- **Verification step**: After build, run `ucx_info -d -t obmm` to confirm `max_bcopy=32768`, then test with `osu_bw -m 32768:32768` and check whether it fragments. If fragmentation at exactly 32768 is acceptable (user's "power-of-two target is the raw cap" statement suggests yes), this is **not** an issue.

---

### Summary

**No material blocking issues.** The proposed geometry is **arithmetically sound**, **fits comfortably in 128 MiB**, and **achieves the stated rebalancing goal** (32768B OSU test moves from cramped SHORT to native BCOPY).

78. static int uct_obmm_proc_alive(uint32_t pid, uint64_t starttime)
79. {
80.     unsigned long live;
81. 
82.     if (pid == 0) {
83.         return 0;
84.     }
85. 
86.     live = ucs_sys_get_proc_create_time((pid_t)pid);
87.     if (live == 0ul) {
88.         /* /proc/<pid>/stat unreadable: pid does not exist any more */
89.         return 0;
90.     }
91. 
92.     return (uint64_t)live == starttime;
93. }

103. /* CAS-claim the INITING transition; if we lose, wait until READY (or
104.  * recover the slot if the prior initializer died mid-init). */
105. static ucs_status_t
106. uct_obmm_pool_init_or_wait(uct_obmm_pool_hdr_t *hdr, uint32_t slot_count,
107.                            uint32_t slot_size)
108. {
109.     unsigned long      self_starttime = ucs_sys_get_proc_create_time(getpid());
110.     uint32_t           prev;
111.     unsigned           spin;
112.     size_t             bitmap_words = uct_obmm_pool_bitmap_words(slot_count);
113.     size_t             slot_off     = uct_obmm_pool_slot_offset(slot_count);
114. 
115. retry:
116.     prev = ucs_atomic_cswap32(&hdr->state, UCT_OBMM_POOL_STATE_UNINIT,
117.                               UCT_OBMM_POOL_STATE_INITING);
118. 
119.     if (prev == UCT_OBMM_POOL_STATE_UNINIT) {
120.         /* We won: zero metadata, fill geometry, publish READY */
121.         memset((char*)hdr + sizeof(*hdr), 0,
122.                bitmap_words * sizeof(uint64_t) +
123.                (size_t)slot_count * sizeof(uct_obmm_slot_meta_t));
124. 
125.         hdr->magic                 = UCT_OBMM_POOL_MAGIC;
126.         hdr->slot_count            = slot_count;
127.         hdr->slot_size             = slot_size;
128.         hdr->slot_array_offset     = slot_off;
129.         hdr->bitmap_words          = (uint32_t)bitmap_words;
130.         hdr->initializer_pid       = (uint32_t)getpid();
131.         hdr->initializer_starttime = (uint64_t)self_starttime;
132. 
133.         ucs_memory_bus_store_fence();
134.         hdr->state = UCT_OBMM_POOL_STATE_READY;
135.         return UCS_OK;
136.     }
137. 
138.     if (prev == UCT_OBMM_POOL_STATE_READY) {
139.         ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
140.         return UCS_OK;
141.     }
142. 
143.     /* state == INITING : wait or recover */
144.     for (spin = 0; spin < UCT_OBMM_POOL_INIT_SPIN_LIMIT; ++spin) {
145.         ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
146.         if (hdr->state == UCT_OBMM_POOL_STATE_READY) {
147.             return UCS_OK;
148.         }
149.         if (hdr->state == UCT_OBMM_POOL_STATE_UNINIT) {
150.             /* Some other rescuer reset; race for init */
151.             goto retry;
152.         }
153. 
154.         if ((spin & 0xfffu) == 0xfffu) {
155.             /* Periodically check if the initializer is alive. If not,
156.              * try to reset back to UNINIT so someone can re-init. */
157.             if (uct_obmm_pool_initializer_stamped(hdr) &&
158.                 !uct_obmm_proc_alive(hdr->initializer_pid,
159.                                      hdr->initializer_starttime)) {
160.                 ucs_warn("obmm: pool initializer pid=%u died; resetting "
161.                          "pool init state",
162.                          hdr->initializer_pid);
163.                 ucs_atomic_cswap32(&hdr->state, UCT_OBMM_POOL_STATE_INITING,
164.                                    UCT_OBMM_POOL_STATE_UNINIT);
165.                 goto retry;
166.             }
167.         }
168.     }
169. 
170.     ucs_error("obmm: timed out waiting for pool init to complete "
171.               "(initializer pid=%u)", hdr->initializer_pid);
172.     return UCS_ERR_TIMED_OUT;
173. }

194.     }
