358.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
359.     }
360.     if (config->bcopy_seg_size == 0) {
361.         ucs_error("obmm: BCOPY_SEG_SIZE must be > 0");
362.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
363.     }
364.     if (config->bcopy_seg_size > UINT16_MAX) {
365.         ucs_error("obmm: BCOPY_SEG_SIZE (%u) too large; max_bcopy must fit "
366.                   "in uint16 (max %u)",
367.                   config->bcopy_seg_size, (unsigned)UINT16_MAX);
368.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
369.     }
370. 
371.     region = uct_obmm_md_export_region(md);
372.     if (region == NULL) {
373.         ucs_error("obmm: cannot create iface; this MD has no local export "
374.                   "region");
375.         return UCS_ERR_NO_DEVICE;
376.     }
377. 
378.     /* Compute slot stride as size_t, then validate it fits in u32 (the
379.      * pool header field is u32) AND that the total region budget covers
380.      * slot_count slots. Failing here is preferred over silently capping
381.      * BCOPY_SEG_SIZE — UCP would happily make protocol decisions based
382.      * on a quietly reduced max_bcopy. */
383.     stride = uct_obmm_slot_stride(config->fifo_size, config->fifo_elem_size,
384.                                   config->bcopy_seg_size);
385.     if (stride > UINT32_MAX) {
386.         ucs_error("obmm: slot stride %zu exceeds uint32_t (fifo_size=%u "
387.                   "elem=%u seg=%u); reduce one of the geometry knobs",
388.                   stride, config->fifo_size, config->fifo_elem_size,
389.                   config->bcopy_seg_size);
390.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
391.     }
392.     required = uct_obmm_pool_required_size(UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT,
393.                                            (uint32_t)stride);
394.     if (required > region->length) {
395.         ucs_error("obmm: geometry does not fit in region: "
396.                   "fifo_size=%u elem_size=%u seg_size=%u stride=%zu "
397.                   "slot_count=%u required=%zu region=%zu. "
398.                   "Reduce UCX_OBMM_BCOPY_SEG_SIZE or UCX_OBMM_FIFO_SIZE.",
399.                   config->fifo_size, config->fifo_elem_size,
400.                   config->bcopy_seg_size, stride,
401.                   UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT, required, region->length);
402.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
403.     }
404. 
405.     UCT_CHECK_PARAM(params->field_mask & UCT_IFACE_PARAM_FIELD_OPEN_MODE,
406.                     "UCT_IFACE_PARAM_FIELD_OPEN_MODE is not defined");
407.     if (!(params->open_mode & UCT_IFACE_OPEN_MODE_DEVICE)) {

409.         return UCS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED;
410.     }
411. 
412.     UCS_CLASS_CALL_SUPER_INIT(uct_base_iface_t, &uct_obmm_iface_ops,
413.                               &uct_obmm_iface_internal_ops, tl_md, worker,

416.                                              UCT_IFACE_PARAM_FIELD_STATS_ROOT) ?
417.                                             params->stats_root : NULL)
418.                               UCS_STATS_ARG(params->mode.device.dev_name));

420.     self->region         = region;
421.     self->config.bandwidth = config->super.bandwidth;
422.     self->fifo_size      = config->fifo_size;
423.     self->fifo_mask      = config->fifo_size - 1u;
424.     self->fifo_elem_size = config->fifo_elem_size;
425.     self->bcopy_seg_size = config->bcopy_seg_size;
426.     self->fifo_max_poll  = (config->fifo_max_poll == 0) ? 1 :
427.                            config->fifo_max_poll;
428.     self->read_index     = 0;
429. 
430.     status = uct_obmm_pool_attach(region->base, region->length,
431.                                   UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT,
432.                                   (uint32_t)stride, &self->pool);
433.     if (status != UCS_OK) {
434.         ucs_error("obmm: pool attach failed: %s", ucs_status_string(status));
435.         return status;
436.     }
437. 
438.     status = uct_obmm_pool_alloc_slot(&self->pool, &self->slot_index,
439.                                       &self->recv_slot, &self->generation);
440.     if (status != UCS_OK) {
441.         ucs_error("obmm: failed to allocate FIFO slot: %s",
442.                   ucs_status_string(status));
443.         return status;
444.     }
445. 
446.     self->recv_ctl   = uct_obmm_slot_ctl(self->recv_slot);
447.     self->recv_elems = uct_obmm_slot_elems(self->recv_slot);
448.     self->recv_descs = uct_obmm_slot_descs(self->recv_slot, self->fifo_size,
449.                                            self->fifo_elem_size);
450.     self->recv_ctl->lock = 0;
451. 
452.     ucs_arbiter_init(&self->arbiter);
453. 
454.     /* recv_slot was zeroed by pool_alloc_slot, so head/tail/all element
455.      * flags are zero. read_index starts at 0, expected owner bit on the
456.      * first lap is 1; uninitialized zero correctly reads as "not yet
457.      * written". */
458. 
459.     ucs_debug("obmm: iface %p attached to region %p slot=%u gen=%u "
460.               "fifo_size=%u elem_size=%u seg_size=%u stride=%zu",
461.               self, region->base, self->slot_index, self->generation,
462.               self->fifo_size, self->fifo_elem_size, self->bcopy_seg_size,
463.               stride);
464.     return UCS_OK;
465. }
466. 
467. 
468. static UCS_CLASS_CLEANUP_FUNC(uct_obmm_iface_t)
469. {
470.     uct_base_iface_progress_disable(&self->super.super,
471.                                     UCT_PROGRESS_SEND | UCT_PROGRESS_RECV);
472.     if ((self->pool.hdr != NULL) &&
473.         uct_obmm_pool_free_slot(&self->pool, self->slot_index)) {
474.         uct_obmm_pool_reset(&self->pool);
475.     }
476.     /* All eps were destroyed before iface cleanup (UCX framework
477.      * contract; mm relies on the same), so the arbiter is empty. */
478.     ucs_arbiter_cleanup(&self->arbiter);
479. }
480.

297. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE ucs_status_t
298. uct_obmm_ep_reserve_slot(uct_obmm_ep_t *ep, uint64_t *head_p)
299. {
300.     uint64_t head;
301. 
302.     if (!uct_obmm_ep_try_lock_head(ep)) {
303.         UCS_STATS_UPDATE_COUNTER(ep->super.stats, UCT_EP_STAT_NO_RES, 1);
304.         return UCS_ERR_NO_RESOURCE;
305.     }
306. 
307.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
308.     head = ep->peer_ctl->head;
309. 
310.     if ((head - ep->cached_tail) >= ep->fifo_size) {
311.         ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
312.         ep->cached_tail = ep->peer_ctl->tail;
313.         if ((head - ep->cached_tail) >= ep->fifo_size) {
314.             UCS_STATS_UPDATE_COUNTER(ep->super.stats, UCT_EP_STAT_NO_RES, 1);
315.             uct_obmm_ep_unlock_head(ep);
316.             return UCS_ERR_NO_RESOURCE;
317.         }
318.     }
319. 
320.     uct_obmm_bus_full_fence();
321.     ep->peer_ctl->head = head + 1;
322.     uct_obmm_ep_unlock_head(ep);
323. 
324.     *head_p = head;
325.     return UCS_OK;
326. }

396. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE int
397. uct_obmm_ep_has_tx_resource(uct_obmm_ep_t *ep)
398. {
399.     uint64_t head;
400. 
401.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
402.     if (ep->peer_ctl->lock != 0) {
403.         return 0;
404.     }
405. 
406.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
407.     head = ep->peer_ctl->head;
408.     if ((head - ep->cached_tail) < ep->fifo_size) {
409.         return 1;
410.     }
411.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
412.     ep->cached_tail = ep->peer_ctl->tail;

417. ucs_status_t uct_obmm_ep_pending_add(uct_ep_h tl_ep, uct_pending_req_t *n,
418.                                      unsigned flags)
419. {
420.     uct_obmm_ep_t    *ep    = ucs_derived_of(tl_ep, uct_obmm_ep_t);
421.     uct_obmm_iface_t *iface = ucs_derived_of(tl_ep->iface, uct_obmm_iface_t);
422. 
423.     (void)flags;
424. 
425.     /* obmm NO_RESOURCE can mean either FIFO-full or transient head-lock
426.      * contention. Queue unconditionally rather than returning BUSY for an
427.      * immediate retry, otherwise multi-producer contention can devolve into a
428.      * retry storm instead of making forward progress through the iface arbiter. */
429. 
430.     UCS_STATIC_ASSERT(sizeof(uct_pending_req_priv_arb_t) <=
431.                       UCT_PENDING_REQ_PRIV_LEN);
432.     uct_pending_req_arb_group_push(&ep->arb_group, n);
433.     ucs_arbiter_group_schedule(&iface->arbiter, &ep->arb_group);
434.     UCT_TL_EP_STAT_PEND(&ep->super);
435. 
436.     return UCS_OK;
437. }

440. ucs_arbiter_cb_result_t
441. uct_obmm_ep_process_pending(ucs_arbiter_t *arbiter, ucs_arbiter_group_t *group,
442.                             ucs_arbiter_elem_t *elem, void *arg)
443. {
444.     uct_obmm_ep_t     *ep    = ucs_container_of(group, uct_obmm_ep_t, arb_group);
445.     unsigned          *count = (unsigned*)arg;
446.     uct_pending_req_t *req;
447.     ucs_status_t       status;
448. 
449.     /* Refresh cached tail so the request callback's am_short/am_bcopy sees
450.      * the freshest peer state and is not falsely starved. */
451.     if (!uct_obmm_ep_has_tx_resource(ep)) {
452.         return UCS_ARBITER_CB_RESULT_RESCHED_GROUP;
453.     }
454. 
455.     req    = ucs_container_of(elem, uct_pending_req_t, priv);
456.     status = req->func(req);
457. 
458.     if (status == UCS_OK) {
459.         ++(*count);
460.         return UCS_ARBITER_CB_RESULT_REMOVE_ELEM;
461.     } else if (status == UCS_INPROGRESS) {
462.         ++(*count);
463.         return UCS_ARBITER_CB_RESULT_NEXT_GROUP;
464.     }
465. 
466.     /* NO_RESOURCE (or any other transient): keep the request and try
467.      * again the next time iface_progress runs. */
468.     return UCS_ARBITER_CB_RESULT_RESCHED_GROUP;
469. }

231.     unsigned                 polled = 0;
232.     uct_obmm_fifo_element_t *elem;

234.     uint8_t                  expected_owner;

239.                                   iface->fifo_mask, iface->fifo_elem_size);
240. 
241.         /* Owner bit alternates each lap of the ring; pass 0 expects 1, pass
242.          * 1 expects 0, etc. Combined with zero-fill on slot allocation, this
243.          * means an unwritten slot reads as flags==0 and is correctly skipped
244.          * on the very first lap. */
245.         expected_owner = ((iface->read_index / iface->fifo_size) & 1u) ?

249.         if ((flags & UCT_OBMM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_OWNER) != expected_owner) {

264.              * with respect to the sender's bus_store_fence + flag write. */

266.                                             iface->read_index,

268.                                             iface->bcopy_seg_size);

124.     - the remaining hang is more consistent with multi-producer head-lock
125.       contention being treated as `BUSY` immediate retry, creating retry storms,

127.   - fix applied:
128.     - `obmm_ep_pending_add()` now always queues instead of returning `BUSY`
129.       after a `NO_RESOURCE` send failure
130.     - `uct_obmm_ep_has_tx_resource()` is now a conservative best-effort check
131.       for `process_pending()`: it requires both FIFO space and an unlocked peer
132.       head lock before retrying a pending request
133.     - temporary lock/stale diagnostics were removed after this behavior change
134.

250.     self->expected_generation = iaddr->generation;
251.     self->fifo_size           = iaddr->fifo_size;
252.     self->fifo_mask           = iaddr->fifo_size - 1u;
253.     self->fifo_elem_size      = iaddr->fifo_elem_size;
254.     self->bcopy_seg_size      = iaddr->bcopy_seg_size;
255.     self->peer_dcna           = daddr->exporter_dcna;
256.     self->peer_deid_hi        = daddr->exporter_deid_hi;
257.     self->peer_deid_lo        = daddr->exporter_deid_lo;
258.     self->peer_slot_index     = iaddr->slot_index;
259.     self->peer_pid            = iaddr->pid;
260.     self->lock_token          = uct_obmm_ep_make_lock_token(iface, self);
261.     self->trace_reserve_no_resource_count = 0;
262.     self->trace_pending_queue_count       = 0;
263.     self->trace_pending_resched_count     = 0;
264.     self->trace_send_with_pending_count   = 0;
265.     return UCS_OK;

268. static UCS_CLASS_CLEANUP_FUNC(uct_obmm_ep_t)
269. {
270.     /* Drain any UCP requests still parked on this ep's arbiter group
271.      * before the iface tears down its arbiter. mm follows the same
272.      * order (mm_ep.c:217). */
273.     uct_obmm_ep_pending_purge(&self->super.super, NULL, NULL);
274.     /* Peer pool memory is owned by the MD; nothing else to release. */

279. UCS_CLASS_DEFINE_DELETE_FUNC(uct_obmm_ep_t, uct_ep_t);

282. int uct_obmm_ep_is_connected(const uct_ep_h tl_ep,
283.                              const uct_ep_is_connected_params_t *params)
284. {
285.     const uct_obmm_ep_t          *ep = ucs_derived_of(tl_ep, uct_obmm_ep_t);
286.     const uct_obmm_device_addr_t *daddr;
287.     const uct_obmm_iface_addr_t  *iaddr;
288. 
289.     if (!uct_base_ep_is_connected(tl_ep, params)) {
290.         return 0;
291.     }
292. 
293.     daddr = (const uct_obmm_device_addr_t*)params->device_addr;
294.     iaddr = (const uct_obmm_iface_addr_t*)params->iface_addr;
295.     if ((daddr == NULL) || (iaddr == NULL)) {

302.            (iaddr->slot_index == ep->peer_slot_index) &&
303.            (iaddr->generation == ep->expected_generation);

307. ucs_status_t uct_obmm_ep_am_short(uct_ep_h tl_ep, uint8_t id, uint64_t header,
308.                                   const void *payload, unsigned length)
309. {
310.     uct_obmm_ep_t           *ep    = ucs_derived_of(tl_ep, uct_obmm_ep_t);
311.     uct_obmm_iface_t        *iface = ucs_derived_of(tl_ep->iface,
312.                                                     uct_obmm_iface_t);
313.     size_t                   payload_total = sizeof(header) + length;
314.     uct_obmm_fifo_element_t *elem;
315.     uint64_t                 head;
316.     uint8_t                  owner_bit;
317. 
318.     UCT_CHECK_AM_ID(id);
319.     UCT_CHECK_LENGTH(payload_total, 0,
320.                      ep->fifo_elem_size - sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_element_t),
321.                      "am_short");
322. 
323.     if (ucs_unlikely(!ucs_arbiter_group_is_empty(&ep->arb_group))) {
324.         ++ep->trace_send_with_pending_count;
325.         if (uct_obmm_trace_should_log(ep->trace_send_with_pending_count)) {
326.             uct_obmm_ep_trace_state(ep, "send while pending",
327.                                     ep->trace_send_with_pending_count,
328.                                     "am_short entry", NULL);
329.         }
330.     }
331. 
332.     if (uct_obmm_ep_reserve_slot(ep, &head) != UCS_OK) {
333.         return UCS_ERR_NO_RESOURCE;
334.     }
335. 
336.     elem = uct_obmm_slot_elem(ep->peer_elems, head, ep->fifo_mask,
337.                               ep->fifo_elem_size);
338. 
339.     elem->am_id      = id;
340.     elem->length     = (uint16_t)payload_total;
341.     elem->generation = ep->expected_generation;
342.     elem->header     = header;
343.     if (length > 0) {
344.         memcpy(elem + 1, payload, length);
345.     }
346. 
347.     /* Publish: the OWNER bit toggles each wraparound. The receiver expects
348.      * bit==1 on even passes and bit==0 on odd passes (and vice versa) so
349.      * that uninitialized memory (zero) reads as "not yet written" on the
350.      * first pass. */
351.     owner_bit = ((head / ep->fifo_size) & 1u) ? 0u : UCT_OBMM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_OWNER;
352. 
353.     ucs_memory_bus_store_fence();
354.     elem->flags = owner_bit;
355. 
356.     UCT_TL_EP_STAT_OP(&ep->super, AM, SHORT, payload_total);
357.     uct_iface_trace_am(&iface->super, UCT_AM_TRACE_TYPE_SEND, id,
358.                        &header, payload_total, "TX: AM_SHORT");
359.     return UCS_OK;
360. }
361. 
362. 
363. /* Reserve one slot in the peer's FIFO, returning the head index that was
364.  * claimed. Multi-producer reservation is serialized with a token lock because
365.  * on target NC/aarch64 mappings, CAS updates memory but its return value is
366.  * not a reliable ownership result. */
367. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE ucs_status_t
368. uct_obmm_ep_reserve_slot(uct_obmm_ep_t *ep, uint64_t *head_p)
369. {
370.     uint64_t head;
371. 
372.     if (!uct_obmm_ep_try_lock_head(ep)) {
373.         ++ep->trace_reserve_no_resource_count;
374.         if (uct_obmm_trace_should_log(ep->trace_reserve_no_resource_count)) {
375.             uct_obmm_ep_trace_state(ep, "reserve stalled",
376.                                     ep->trace_reserve_no_resource_count,
377.                                     "head lock busy", NULL);
378.         }
379.         UCS_STATS_UPDATE_COUNTER(ep->super.stats, UCT_EP_STAT_NO_RES, 1);
380.         return UCS_ERR_NO_RESOURCE;
381.     }
382. 
383.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
384.     head = ep->peer_ctl->head;
385. 
386.     if ((head - ep->cached_tail) >= ep->fifo_size) {
387.         ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
388.         ep->cached_tail = ep->peer_ctl->tail;
389.         if ((head - ep->cached_tail) >= ep->fifo_size) {
390.             ++ep->trace_reserve_no_resource_count;
391.             if (uct_obmm_trace_should_log(ep->trace_reserve_no_resource_count)) {
392.                 uct_obmm_ep_trace_state(ep, "reserve stalled",
393.                                         ep->trace_reserve_no_resource_count,
394.                                         "peer fifo full", NULL);
395.             }
396.             UCS_STATS_UPDATE_COUNTER(ep->super.stats, UCT_EP_STAT_NO_RES, 1);
397.             uct_obmm_ep_unlock_head(ep);
398.             return UCS_ERR_NO_RESOURCE;
399.         }
400.     }
401. 
402.     uct_obmm_bus_full_fence();
403.     ep->peer_ctl->head = head + 1;
404.     uct_obmm_ep_unlock_head(ep);
405. 
406.     uct_obmm_ep_trace_recovered(ep, "reserve recovered",
407.                                 ep->trace_reserve_no_resource_count, NULL);
408.     ep->trace_reserve_no_resource_count = 0;
409. 
410.     *head_p = head;
411.     return UCS_OK;
412. }
413.

415. ssize_t uct_obmm_ep_am_bcopy(uct_ep_h tl_ep, uint8_t id,
416.                              uct_pack_callback_t pack_cb, void *arg,
417.                              unsigned flags)
418. {
419.     uct_obmm_ep_t           *ep    = ucs_derived_of(tl_ep, uct_obmm_ep_t);
420.     uct_obmm_iface_t        *iface = ucs_derived_of(tl_ep->iface,
421.                                                     uct_obmm_iface_t);
422.     uct_obmm_fifo_element_t *elem;
423.     void                    *desc;
424.     uint64_t                 head;
425.     size_t                   length;
426.     uint8_t                  owner_bit;
427.     ucs_status_t             status;
428. 
429.     /* flags (UCT_SEND_FLAG_PEER_CHECK etc.) are ignored: this transport
430.      * does not advertise EP_CHECK / keepalive in v1. */
431.     (void)flags;
432. 
433.     UCT_CHECK_AM_ID(id);
434. 
435.     if (ucs_unlikely(!ucs_arbiter_group_is_empty(&ep->arb_group))) {
436.         ++ep->trace_send_with_pending_count;
437.         if (uct_obmm_trace_should_log(ep->trace_send_with_pending_count)) {
438.             uct_obmm_ep_trace_state(ep, "send while pending",
439.                                     ep->trace_send_with_pending_count,
440.                                     "am_bcopy entry", NULL);
441.         }
442.     }
443. 
444.     status = uct_obmm_ep_reserve_slot(ep, &head);
445.     if (status != UCS_OK) {
446.         return status;
447.     }
448. 
449.     elem = uct_obmm_slot_elem(ep->peer_elems, head, ep->fifo_mask,
450.                               ep->fifo_elem_size);
451.     desc = uct_obmm_slot_desc(ep->peer_descs, head, ep->fifo_mask,
452.                               ep->bcopy_seg_size);
453. 
454.     /* pack_cb writes pack_cb_ret bytes directly into the paired desc[N]
455.      * area. UCP guarantees pack_cb_ret <= cap.am.max_bcopy, which we set
456.      * to bcopy_seg_size. The asserts catch buggy direct UCT users in
457.      * debug builds; production safety relies on the iface cap contract. */
458.     length = pack_cb(desc, arg);
459.     ucs_assertv(length <= ep->bcopy_seg_size,
460.                 "obmm: pack_cb returned %zu > bcopy_seg_size=%u",
461.                 length, ep->bcopy_seg_size);
462.     ucs_assertv(length <= UINT16_MAX,
463.                 "obmm: pack_cb returned %zu > UINT16_MAX", length);
464. 
465.     elem->am_id      = id;
466.     elem->length     = (uint16_t)length;
467.     elem->generation = ep->expected_generation;
468.     elem->header     = 0; /* unused for bcopy */
469. 
470.     owner_bit = ((head / ep->fifo_size) & 1u) ? 0u :
471.                                                 UCT_OBMM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_OWNER;
472. 
473.     /* Release barrier: orders the desc[N] payload writes AND elem header
474.      * writes BEFORE the flags publish. Receiver pairs with bus_load_fence
475.      * after observing the flags byte. */
476.     ucs_memory_bus_store_fence();
477.     elem->flags = owner_bit | UCT_OBMM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_BCOPY;
478. 
479.     UCT_TL_EP_STAT_OP(&ep->super, AM, BCOPY, length);
480.     uct_iface_trace_am(&iface->super, UCT_AM_TRACE_TYPE_SEND, id,
481.                        desc, length, "TX: AM_BCOPY");
482.     return (ssize_t)length;
483. }

489.  * us after this check, callers must still tolerate reserve_slot() returning

7. #ifndef UCT_OBMM_FIFO_H_

9. 
10. #include <ucs/arch/cpu.h>
11. #include <ucs/sys/compiler.h>
12. #include <ucs/sys/compiler_def.h>
13. #include <ucs/sys/ptr_arith.h>

17. 
18. /* Element flags carried in the shared FIFO element header. */
19. enum {
20.     /* Toggled every FIFO wraparound; receiver uses this to detect a freshly
21.      * written element without taking a tail/head delta lock. */
22.     UCT_OBMM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_OWNER = UCS_BIT(0),
23. 
24.     /* Set by senders that wrote via am_bcopy (pack_cb output stored in the
25.      * payload area starting at elem+1, with NO 8-byte am_short header
26.      * prefix). When clear, the element was written via am_short and
27.      * &elem->header + length covers the [hdr][payload] buffer. */
28.     UCT_OBMM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_BCOPY = UCS_BIT(1)
29. };
30. 
31. 
32. /* Per-slot FIFO control header. Lives at offset 0 of every allocated slot in
33.  * the obmm pool. Producers serialize `head` reservation with a token lock:
34.  * on target aarch64 NC mappings, cross-node CAS updates memory but its return
35.  * value is not a reliable ownership result. Consumers read/write `tail` to
36.  * release space. Control fields are accessed via non-cacheable mappings,
37.  * therefore all updates must be paired with bus fences
38.  * (ucs_memory_bus_*_fence), not CPU fences. */
39. typedef struct uct_obmm_fifo_ctl {
40.     /* 1st cacheline: producer-touched */
41.     volatile uint64_t head;
42.     volatile uint64_t lock;
43.     UCS_CACHELINE_PADDING(uint64_t, uint64_t);
44. 
45.     /* 2nd cacheline: consumer-touched */
46.     volatile uint64_t tail;
47.     UCS_CACHELINE_PADDING(uint64_t);
48. } UCS_V_ALIGNED(UCS_SYS_CACHE_LINE_SIZE) uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t;
49. 
50. 
51. /* FIFO element header. The element body (am short header + payload) follows
52.  * immediately. Total element stride is iface->config.fifo_elem_size, which
53.  * the iface chooses so that header+payload <= elem_size. */
54. typedef struct uct_obmm_fifo_element {
55.     uint8_t  flags;       /* UCT_OBMM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_xx */
56.     uint8_t  am_id;       /* active message id */
57.     uint16_t length;      /* payload length (excluding am_short header) */
58.     uint32_t generation;  /* owner-slot generation token; receiver discards
59.                              elements whose generation doesn't match the
60.                              slot's current meta.generation */
61.     uint64_t header;      /* am_short 64-bit header */
62.     /* payload[length] follows here */
63. } UCS_S_PACKED uct_obmm_fifo_element_t;
64. 
65. 
66. /* Compute slot stride: control header + fifo_size * elem_size + (v2)
67.  * fifo_size * bcopy_seg_size, cacheline aligned so that adjacent slots
68.  * don't share a line. Returned as size_t; callers must validate the
69.  * result fits in the uint32_t pool_hdr->slot_size field before passing
70.  * to pool_attach. */
71. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE size_t
72. uct_obmm_slot_stride(unsigned fifo_size, unsigned fifo_elem_size,
73.                      unsigned bcopy_seg_size)
74. {
75.     return ucs_align_up(sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t) +
76.                         ((size_t)fifo_size * fifo_elem_size) +
77.                         ((size_t)fifo_size * bcopy_seg_size),
78.                         UCS_SYS_CACHE_LINE_SIZE);
79. }
80. 
81. 
82. /* Get FIFO control header pointer from a slot base pointer. */
83. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t*
84. uct_obmm_slot_ctl(void *slot_base)
85. {
86.     return (uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t*)slot_base;
87. }
88. 
89. 
90. /* Get FIFO elements array pointer from a slot base pointer. */
91. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE void*
92. uct_obmm_slot_elems(void *slot_base)
93. {
94.     return UCS_PTR_BYTE_OFFSET(slot_base, sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t));
95. }
96. 
97. 
98. /* Get bcopy desc array pointer from a slot base pointer. The desc area
99.  * lives immediately after the FIFO element array. Each desc is
100.  * `bcopy_seg_size` bytes; index N is paired 1:1 with FIFO element N. */
101. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE void*
102. uct_obmm_slot_descs(void *slot_base, unsigned fifo_size,
103.                     unsigned fifo_elem_size)
104. {
105.     return UCS_PTR_BYTE_OFFSET(slot_base,
106.                                sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t) +
107.                                ((size_t)fifo_size * fifo_elem_size));
108. }
109. 
110. 
111. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE uct_obmm_fifo_element_t*
112. uct_obmm_slot_elem(void *elems, uint64_t index, unsigned mask,
113.                    unsigned elem_size)
114. {
115.     return (uct_obmm_fifo_element_t*)
116.            UCS_PTR_BYTE_OFFSET(elems, (size_t)(index & mask) * elem_size);
117. }
118. 
119. 
120. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE void*
121. uct_obmm_slot_desc(void *descs, uint64_t index, unsigned mask,
122.                    unsigned seg_size)
123. {
124.     return UCS_PTR_BYTE_OFFSET(descs, (size_t)(index & mask) * seg_size);
125. }
126. 
127. 
128. /* Full bus-domain fence: orders ALL prior memory accesses (loads and
129.  * stores) before ALL subsequent memory accesses, in the outer-shareable /
130.  * device domain that includes cross-host obmm peers.
131.  *
132.  * Why we need this in addition to ucs_memory_bus_{store,load}_fence:
133.  * the receiver must order its desc[N] LOADS (issued during the AM
134.  * handler) before the STORE that publishes the new tail. On ARM64,
135.  * ucs_memory_bus_store_fence() is `dmb oshst` (store→store only) and
136.  * does not order prior loads. Without this load→store barrier, a sender
137.  * could observe the advanced tail and overwrite desc[N] while the
138.  * receiver still has outstanding loads from the previous lap's payload.
139.  *
140.  * Defined locally in obmm rather than added to ucs/arch to keep the
141.  * change inside ucx/src/uct/obmm/ per AGENTS.md. */
142. #if defined(__aarch64__)
143. #define uct_obmm_bus_full_fence() __asm__ __volatile__("dmb osh" ::: "memory")
144. #elif defined(__x86_64__) || defined(__i386__)
145. #define uct_obmm_bus_full_fence() __asm__ __volatile__("mfence" ::: "memory")
146. #elif defined(__powerpc64__)
147. #define uct_obmm_bus_full_fence() __asm__ __volatile__("sync" ::: "memory")
148. #elif defined(__riscv) && (__riscv_xlen == 64)
149. #define uct_obmm_bus_full_fence() \
150.     __asm__ __volatile__("fence iorw, iorw" ::: "memory")
151. #else
152. /* Fallback: combine store + load fences. Not strictly load→store on all
153.  * archs but better than nothing; build will warn so the porter notices. */
154. #warning "obmm: no full bus fence for this arch; receiver tail release ordering may be weak"
155. #define uct_obmm_bus_full_fence() do { \
156.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();        \
157.     ucs_memory_bus_store_fence();       \
158. } while (0)
159. #endif
160. 
161. #endif
162.

486. /* Conservative best-effort check for whether a pending request is worth

491. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE int
492. uct_obmm_ep_has_tx_resource(uct_obmm_ep_t *ep)
493. {
494.     uint64_t head;
495. 
496.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
497.     if (ep->peer_ctl->lock != 0) {
498.         return 0;
499.     }
500. 
501.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();

504.         return 1;
505.     }
506.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
507.     ep->cached_tail = ep->peer_ctl->tail;
508.     return (head - ep->cached_tail) < ep->fifo_size;
509. }

### 💬 Copilot

Based on my review of the uncommitted diagnostic changes in the obmm transport files, I've found one significant issue:

## Issue: Race condition in diagnostic counter reads within trace function
**File:** ucx/src/uct/obmm/base/obmm_ep.c:73-112
**Severity:** Medium
**Problem:** The `uct_obmm_ep_trace_reason` function is called from `uct_obmm_ep_trace_state` with locally-read values of `head`, `tail`, and `lock`, but it uses `ep-\>cached_tail` from the ep structure. This creates a temporal inconsistency where the function compares a stale `cached_tail` against fresh `head`/`tail` values read at a different point in time.

Specifically:
- Lines 97-100: `uct_obmm_ep_trace_state` reads fresh `head`, `tail`, `lock` after a memory fence
- Line 107: Calls `uct_obmm_ep_trace_reason(ep, head, tail, lock)` with these fresh values
- Line 81: Inside `uct_obmm_ep_trace_reason`, the condition `(head - ep-\>cached_tail) \>= ep-\>fifo_size` compares fresh `head` against stale `ep-\>cached_tail`

This means the "fifo-full" vs "state-race" classification in the diagnostic output may be incorrect, as it's mixing snapshot data from different time points. Since this is a diagnostic path, it won't cause functional incorrectness, but it could severely mislead debugging efforts during the hang investigation.

**Evidence:** 
1. The `cached_tail` is only updated in `uct_obmm_ep_reserve_slot` (line 388) or `uct_obmm_ep_has_tx_resource` (line 507), not at the time `trace_state` is called
2. All three values `head`, `tail`, `lock` are read fresh in `trace_state`, but `cached_tail` is read from ep struct at an unknown prior time
3. This temporal inconsistency could cause the trace to report "state-race" when the real reason was "fifo-full" (or vice versa)

**Suggested fix:** 
Pass `ep-\>cached_tail` as a parameter to `uct_obmm_ep_trace_reason`, or better yet, read it fresh inside `uct_obmm_ep_trace_state` after the same memory fence and pass it along. This ensures all the diagnostic snapshot data comes from the same point in time:

```c
static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE void
uct_obmm_ep_trace_state(uct_obmm_ep_t *ep, const char *stage, uint64_t count,
                        const char *detail, const uct_pending_req_t *req)
{
    uint64_t head;
    uint64_t tail;
    uint64_t lock;
    uint64_t cached_tail;

    ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
    head = ep-\>peer_ctl-\>head;
    tail = ep-\>peer_ctl-\>tail;
    lock = ep-\>peer_ctl-\>lock;
    cached_tail = ep-\>cached_tail;  // read at same snapshot point

    ucs_warn("obmm: %s x%llu ep=%p req=%p peer(pid=%u slot=%u gen=%u) "
             "reason=%s detail=%s lock=0x%llx token=0x%llx head=%llu "
             "cached_tail=%llu tail=%llu group_empty=%d",
             stage, (unsigned long long)count, ep, req, ep-\>peer_pid,
             ep-\>peer_slot_index, ep-\>expected_generation,
             uct_obmm_ep_trace_reason(ep, head, tail, lock, cached_tail), detail,
             ...
}
```

And update `uct_obmm_ep_trace_reason` signature to take `cached_tail` as a parameter instead of reading from `ep-\>cached_tail`.

---

No other significant correctness, compile, or concurrency issues found in the reviewed changes. The diagnostic counters are accessed only from the progress/send paths which UCT guarantees are single-threaded per endpoint, so no additional synchronization is needed for the counter increments.

### 💬 Copilot

**日志已经加上了，而且这次只做了诊断，不改行为。** 现在 obmm 会把“卡住发生在哪一段”拆成几类限频告警，覆盖了发送、占槽、pending、arbiter、接收 progress 全链路。

关键日志点在：
- `send while pending`：EP 已有 pending 时，新的直发还在继续进来
- `reserve stalled` / `reserve recovered`：卡在 `reserve_slot()`，并区分 `lock-busy` / `fifo-full`
- `pending queued`：请求进入 pending
- `pending stalled` / `pending callback stalled` / `pending recovered`：arbiter 已经在跑，但仍不前进，或后来恢复
- `iface idle with pending` / `iface pending recovered`：iface 侧 `progress()` 没收包、但 arbiter 还非空

这些日志都做了**2 的幂次限频**，只会在第 1/2/4/8/... 次打印，避免像上次那样刷屏。改动在：
`ucx\src\uct\obmm\base\obmm_ep.c`
`ucx\src\uct\obmm\base\obmm_ep.h`
`ucx\src\uct\obmm\base\obmm_iface.c`
`ucx\src\uct\obmm\base\obmm_iface.h`

你现在直接用原来的跨节点 4 进程复现场景再跑一轮，就能从第一批 `obmm:` WARN 看出来到底是：
**卡在直发占槽前、卡在 pending 重试里、还是 iface progress 根本没把局面推进下去。**

32. /* Per-slot FIFO control header. Lives at offset 0 of every allocated slot in
33.  * the obmm pool. Producers serialize `head` reservation with a token lock:
34.  * on target aarch64 NC mappings, cross-node CAS updates memory but its return
35.  * value is not a reliable ownership result. Consumers read/write `tail` to
36.  * release space. Control fields are accessed via non-cacheable mappings,
37.  * therefore all updates must be paired with bus fences
38.  * (ucs_memory_bus_*_fence), not CPU fences. */
39. typedef struct uct_obmm_fifo_ctl {
40.     /* 1st cacheline: producer-touched */
41.     volatile uint64_t head;
42.     volatile uint64_t lock;
43.     UCS_CACHELINE_PADDING(uint64_t, uint64_t);
44. 
45.     /* 2nd cacheline: consumer-touched */
46.     volatile uint64_t tail;
47.     UCS_CACHELINE_PADDING(uint64_t);
48. } UCS_V_ALIGNED(UCS_SYS_CACHE_LINE_SIZE) uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t;
```

10. 
11. # OBMM API and Test Environment
12. 
13. This skill is the **single source of truth** for what the agent may assume
14. about libobmm and the deployment topology. If something is not stated here,
15. the agent must ASK the user instead of inventing it.
16. 
17. ## libobmm public API (from `obmm/src/libobmm/libobmm.h`)
18. 
19. ```c

23.

27.                         unsigned long flags);
28. 
29. mem_id obmm_export_useraddr(int pid, void *va, size_t length,
30.                             unsigned long flags, struct obmm_mem_desc *desc);
31. 
32. mem_id obmm_import(const struct obmm_mem_desc *desc, unsigned long flags,
33.                    int base_dist, int *numa);

43. 
44. Key data structures:
45. 
46. - `struct obmm_mem_desc { addr; length; seid[16]; deid[16]; tokenid; scna;
47.   dcna; priv_len; priv[]; }` — the descriptor returned by export and
48.   consumed by import.
49. - `struct obmm_preimport_info { pa; length; base_dist; numa_id; seid; deid;
50.   scna; dcna; priv_len; priv[]; }`
51. - `mem_id` is `uint64_t`; `OBMM_INVALID_MEMID == 0`.
52. 
53. ## Test environment — IMMUTABLE FACTS
54. 
55. These were stated by the project owner. The transport implementation MUST
56. be designed against exactly this topology:
57. 
58. 1. **Two nodes**, node 0 and node 1.
59. 2. Each node has **already exported a 128 MiB memory region** to the other
60.    side, before any UCX / MPI process starts.
61. 3. Each node has **already imported** the peer's 128 MiB region.
62. 4. The export / import / preimport / unimport / unexport lifecycle is
63.    handled outside the UCX transport — **the obmm UCT transport must NOT
64.    call** `obmm_export`, `obmm_unexport`, `obmm_import`, `obmm_unimport`,
65.    `obmm_preimport`, or `obmm_unpreimport` at runtime.
66. 5. Inside UCT, access to the local and peer regions is done with
67.    **`open("/dev/obmm_shmdev${memid}", O_RDWR | O_SYNC)` + `mmap`**
68.    (NC mapping; see "Locked-in design decisions" below).
69.    The local export memid and peer import memid are discovered by
70.    scanning `/sys/devices/obmm/obmm_shmdev*/` and inspecting whether
71.    each contains an `export_info/` or `import_info/` subdirectory.
72. 6. **No hardware is available** in the development environment. Do not
73.    attempt to run `mpirun`, real `ucx_perftest`, or any test that requires
74.    the obmm device. Validation is limited to:
75.      - `make` / `make install` succeeding,
76.      - `ucx_info -d` listing the obmm component, md, and tl,
77.      - `ucx_info -c` showing OBMM_* env vars,
78.      - static review against this skill and `uct-transport-patterns`.
79. 
80. ## Locked-in design decisions (do not change without re-asking)
81. 
82. These were explicitly decided with the project owner during the v1
83. am_short plan review. They override any conflicting suggestion the
84. agent may otherwise default to (notably the mm transport's behavior).
85. 
86. 1. **NC mapping for the data path.** Open shmdev with
87.    `O_RDWR | O_SYNC` and mmap with `MAP_SHARED`. This puts the FIFO
88.    region into a non-cacheable mapping, which:
89.      - bypasses the OBMM cacheable consistency model (writers and
90.        readers from any host coexist),
91.      - removes the need to ever call `obmm_set_ownership` from the
92.        transport.
93. 2. **Cross-node atomic RMW on NC is guaranteed.** The project owner
94.    has stated that the obmm fabric supports atomic FAA / CAS on NC
95.    mappings across nodes. The transport may therefore use mm-style
96.    multi-producer FIFOs (FAA on a shared head) without redesigning
97.    for SPSC.
98. 3. **UCT owns the in-region layout.** The 128 MiB exported region is
99.    zero-filled at platform export time. The transport places its own
100.    header (state / version / slot bitmap / slot_meta / fixed-size
101.    slots) at the start of the region. A two-phase init is used:
102.    `state` transitions UNINIT→INITING (CAS) → fill geometry → bus
103.    fence → store READY. Losers spin on READY then bus-load fence.
104.    Single-magic init is racy (geometry not yet visible) and must
105.    not be used.
106. 4. **Topology**: per node there is exactly 1 export region and 1
107.    import region (the peer node's export). Discovered via
108.    `/sys/devices/obmm/obmm_shmdev*/{export_info,import_info}`.
109.    Reachability and mapping table keys are
110.    `(exporter_dcna, exporter_deid, memid)` from sysfs — NOT memid
111.    alone (collision-prone).
112. 5. **Self-loopback inside one node** is supported: same-node processes
113.    communicate by both mapping the local export region (the imported
114.    "peer region" entry simply will not exist in the single-node case,
115.    or will equal the local one — handle both).
116. 6. **Slot lifecycle uses generation tokens.** Each slot has
117.    `(owner_pid, owner_starttime, generation, state)` in slot_meta.
118.    `iface_addr` and every FIFO elem carry `generation`; receiver
119.    discards mismatches. Destroy = mark DEAD → bus fence → bump
120.    generation → clear bit. Crash recovery: scan bitmap, validate
121.    `/proc/<pid>/stat starttime`, reclaim. PID alone is insufficient
122.    (PID reuse).
123. 7. **Cross-node memory ordering uses BUS-domain fences.**
124.    `ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()` / `ucs_memory_bus_load_fence()`
125.    (sfence/lfence on x86, `dmb oshst`/`dmb oshld` on arm64). The
126.    CPU-domain fences mm uses (`ucs_memory_cpu_*_fence`) are
127.    inner-shareable only and DO NOT cover cross-host NC visibility.
128. 
129. ## OBMM consistency model — why NC matters
130. 
131. From `obmm/doc/libobmm.md` and `obmm/doc/obmm_set_ownership.md`:
132. 
133. - For **cacheable** OBMM mappings, at any moment all hosts touching a
134.   region must be in one of two states:
135.     a) all hosts are PROT_READ or PROT_NONE, OR
136.     b) exactly one host has writers; all other hosts must be PROT_NONE.
137. - A receive-FIFO model (writer on the sending host, reader on the
138.   receiving host, on the SAME region) violates this: it would require
139.   one host to write while another host reads simultaneously.
140. - Therefore the obmm transport CANNOT use cacheable mappings for the
141.   FIFO region without expensive ownership flips per message.
142. - NC (O_SYNC) mappings are exempt: per the doc, "用户无需关心一致性
143.   模型，所有的用户均具备读写权限". This is why decision (1) above
144.   is mandatory, not optional.
145. 
146. ## Implications for the transport design
147. 
148. These follow from the facts above and should be treated as defaults; ask
149. the user before deviating:
150. 
151. - **Memory registration** (`uct_md_ops_t::mem_reg` / `mem_dereg`) does not
152.   need to call libobmm. The current placeholders
153.   (`uct_md_dummy_mem_reg` / `uct_md_dummy_mem_dereg`) are appropriate
154.   because the buffers used by am_short live inside the pre-imported
155.   peer region, not in arbitrary user buffers.
156. - **Address exchange** for am_short: `iface_addr` MUST carry
157.   `(exporter_dcna, exporter_deid, memid, slot_index, generation)`
158.   so the peer can (a) look up the already-mmap'd region in our MD's
159.   mapping table by exporter identity + memid, and (b) detect stale
160.   slot reuse via generation. Memid alone is unsafe and was rejected
161.   in plan-review. The current `uct_obmm_iface_addr_t = uint64_t`
162.   must be widened.
163. - **Reachability**: `iface_is_reachable_v2` matches on
164.   `(exporter_dcna, exporter_deid, memid)` against the MD's known
165.   exports + imports. Drop the `uct_sm_iface_is_reachable` (same-host)
166.   call — obmm is cross-node by construction.
167. - **Progress wiring**: `iface_progress_enable/disable` MUST call
168.   `uct_base_iface_progress_enable_cb(...)` /
169.   `uct_base_iface_progress_disable(...)`. The current
170.   `ucs_empty_function` stubs prevent UCP from ever polling the iface.
171. - **EP_CHECK**: do NOT advertise `UCT_IFACE_FLAG_EP_CHECK` in v1.
172.   The current skeleton sets it but `ep_check` only returns OK; no
173.   cross-node liveness check exists. PID-in-addr is not enough.
174. - **Ownership / `obmm_set_ownership`**: only call this if the UCT layer
175.   needs to flip read/write permission on a sub-range of the imported
176.   region; for a first am_short pass with a producer/consumer FIFO this
177.   is typically NOT needed. Ask before adding it.
178. 
179. ## What to ASK the user before writing code
180. 
181. Do not invent answers to any of these. Use the `ask_user` tool:
182. 
183. 1. Whether multiple obmm ifaces per process are expected, or strictly
184.    one peer per local iface (current assumption: 1 iface per process,
185.    pool holds many ifaces from many processes).
186. 2. What the wire `am_id` / header / payload alignment requirements are
187.    on the obmm hardware (e.g. 64 B cache line? 256 B?). Default plan
188.    aligns elements to 64 B; confirm before tuning.
189. 3. ~~Whether NC writes from one host become visible to remote loads
190.    without an explicit fabric-level barrier other than CPU
191.    `dmb`/`mfence`.~~ **RESOLVED in plan-review**: must use bus-domain
192.    fences (`ucs_memory_bus_*_fence`), not CPU-domain. CPU fences are
193.    inner-shareable only and don't reach cross-host NC.
194. 
195. ## Forbidden assumptions
196. 
197. - Do NOT assume libobmm performs its own synchronization — am_short
198.   ordering must be enforced by the transport (release / acquire fences,
199.   same as mm).
200. - Do NOT use cacheable mappings on the FIFO region. NC (`O_SYNC`)
201.   is mandatory; see "Locked-in design decisions".
202. - Do NOT call any `obmm_*` runtime API in the UCT transport unless this
203.   document is updated to allow it. In particular do NOT call
204.   `obmm_set_ownership` — its semantics conflict with the FIFO usage
205.   pattern.
206. - Do NOT use `ucs_memory_cpu_*_fence()` on the obmm data path. They
207.   are inner-shareable / compiler-only and do not cover cross-host NC
208.   visibility. Use `ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()` /
209.   `ucs_memory_bus_load_fence()` (sfence/lfence on x86,
210.   `dmb oshst`/`dmb oshld` on arm64). The mm transport gets away with
211.   CPU fences only because mm peers share an inner-shareable cache
212.   domain; obmm peers do not.
213. 
214. ## Why cacheable + manual cache management was rejected
215. 
216. Asked and answered during plan-review. Do not re-litigate without new
217. information about the obmm fabric.
218. 
219. 1. **OBMM cacheable consistency is enforced at the page-table level**,
220.    not at the cache level. `obmm/doc/libobmm.md:196-211` and
221.    `obmm/doc/obmm_set_ownership.md` require that at any moment either
222.    all hosts touching a region are PROT_READ/PROT_NONE, or exactly
223.    one host has writers and all other hosts are PROT_NONE. Even a
224.    correctly `clflush`-ed write from host A is not legal to read on
225.    host B until ownership is flipped via the `obmm_set_ownership()`
226.    syscall. That is one syscall per message — incompatible with
227.    `am_short` latency goals.
228. 2. **arm64 user-space lacks `dc ivac`** (invalidate by VA to PoC, EL0
229.    typically only exposes `dc civac` = clean+invalidate). A reader-side
230.    "discard cache, then load" sequence would have to clean+invalidate
231.    on every poll, doubling the writer-side cost.
232. 3. **UCX has no precedent** for cross-host cacheable shared memory with
233.    manual coherence on a hot data path. `ucs_arch_clear_cache` exists
234.    (x86: `mfence; clflush; mfence` per line; arm64: `dc cvau` +
235.    `ic ivau`) but is used only for instruction-cache coherence
236.    (JIT / code patching), never for transport data. All cross-host
237.    UCX transports either use a NIC (NIC handles coherence) or rely
238.    on a HW-coherent fabric. Inventing a new pattern here would carry
239.    risk far above what NC mapping costs.
240. 4. **Bulk-flip ownership** (writer holds write, batches N messages,
241.    flips, reader batches N reads) is a possible future path for
242.    `put/get` bulk transfers but trades latency for throughput and
243.    defeats AM short's purpose. Out of scope for v1.
244. 
245. NC (`O_SYNC`) avoids all four issues at the cost of uncached load/store
246. performance, which the project owner has accepted.
247.
````

1. /*
2.  * obmm_atomic_probe.c
3.  *
4.  * Minimal NC-mapping atomic probe for obmm shmdev pages.
5.  *
6.  * Purpose:
7.  *   1. Reproduce the current 64-bit shared lock protocol outside UCX
8.  *   2. Check whether 64-bit FAA return values are self-consistent on NC
9.  *
10.  * Build:
11.  *   gcc -O2 -std=gnu11 -o obmm_atomic_probe obmm_atomic_probe.c

13.  * Typical use:
14.  *   1. Pick an offset that is not used by UCX. By default this tool uses the
15.  *      last page of the 128 MiB obmm region.
16.  *   2. Make sure no UCX/MPI job is touching the same probe page.
17.  *   3. Clear once:
18.  *        ./obmm_atomic_probe --dev /dev/obmm_shmdevX --mode clear
19.  *   4. Run the same mode concurrently on the two nodes against two device
20.  *      paths that map the SAME underlying obmm region:
21.  *        ./obmm_atomic_probe --dev /dev/obmm_shmdevX --mode lock64 --iters 2000000
22.  *        ./obmm_atomic_probe --dev /dev/obmm_shmdevY --mode lock64 --iters 2000000

25.  *        ./obmm_atomic_probe --dev /dev/obmm_shmdevY --mode faa64 --iters 2000000

102. #endif
103. }
104. 
105. static inline void probe_bus_full_fence(void)
106. {
107. #if defined(__aarch64__)
108.     __asm__ __volatile__("dmb osh" ::: "memory");
109. #elif defined(__x86_64__) || defined(__i386__)
110.     __asm__ __volatile__("mfence" ::: "memory");
111. #elif defined(__powerpc64__)
112.     __asm__ __volatile__("sync" ::: "memory");
113. #elif defined(__riscv) && (__riscv_xlen == 64)
114.     __asm__ __volatile__("fence iorw, iorw" ::: "memory");
115. #else
116.     __sync_synchronize();
117. #endif
118. }
119. 
120. static inline uint64_t probe_atomic_cswap64(volatile uint64_t *ptr,
121.                                             uint64_t oldval, uint64_t newval)
122. {
123.     return __sync_val_compare_and_swap(ptr, oldval, newval);
124. }
125. 
126. static inline uint64_t probe_atomic_fetch_add64(volatile uint64_t *ptr,
127.                                                 uint64_t add)
128. {
129.     return __sync_fetch_and_add(ptr, add);
130. }
131. 
132. static uint64_t probe_mix64(uint64_t x)
133. {
134.     x ^= x >> 30;
135.     x *= UINT64_C(0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9);
136.     x ^= x >> 27;
137.     x *= UINT64_C(0x94d049bb133111eb);
138.     x ^= x >> 31;
139.     return x;
140. }

142. static uint64_t probe_default_token(void)
143. {
144.     char hostname[256];
145.     uint64_t seed = (uint64_t)getpid();
146.     size_t i;
147. 
148.     if (gethostname(hostname, sizeof(hostname)) != 0) {
149.         strncpy(hostname, "unknown-host", sizeof(hostname));
150.         hostname[sizeof(hostname) - 1] = '\0';
151.     }
152. 
153.     for (i = 0; hostname[i] != '\0'; ++i) {
154.         seed = probe_mix64(seed ^ (unsigned char)hostname[i]);
155.     }
156. 
157.     seed = probe_mix64(seed ^ (uint64_t)time(NULL));
158.     return (seed == 0) ? UINT64_C(1) : seed;
159. }

180. static int probe_parse_u64(const char *str, uint64_t *value_p)
181. {
182.     char *endptr = NULL;
183.     unsigned long long value;
184. 
185.     errno = 0;
186.     value = strtoull(str, &endptr, 0);
187.     if ((errno != 0) || (endptr == str) || ((endptr != NULL) && (*endptr != '\0'))) {
188.         return -1;
189.     }
190. 
191.     *value_p = (uint64_t)value;
192.     return 0;

196. {

198.     int mode_set = 0;
199. 
200.     memset(args, 0, sizeof(*args));

223.                 return -1;
224.             }
225.             mode_set = 1;
226.         } else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--offset")) {
227.             if ((++i >= argc) || (probe_parse_u64(argv[i], &args->offset) != 0)) {
228.                 return -1;
229.             }
230.         } else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--iters")) {

232.                 return -1;
233.             }
234.         } else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--token")) {
235.             if ((++i >= argc) || (probe_parse_u64(argv[i], &args->token) != 0)) {
236.                 return -1;
237.             }
238.         } else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--hold-loops")) {
239.             if ((++i >= argc) || (probe_parse_u64(argv[i], &args->hold_loops) != 0)) {
240.                 return -1;
241.             }
242.         } else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--anomaly-limit")) {
243.             if ((++i >= argc) || (probe_parse_u64(argv[i], &args->anomaly_limit) != 0)) {
244.                 return -1;
245.             }
246.         } else {
247.             return -1;
248.         }
249.     }
250. 
251.     if (args->dev_path == NULL) {
252.         return -1;
253.     }
254.     if (!mode_set) {

261. static int probe_map(const probe_args_t *args, mapped_probe_t *mapped)
262. {
263.     long page_size;
264.     off_t map_offset;
265.     size_t delta;
266. 
267.     memset(mapped, 0, sizeof(*mapped));
268.     mapped->fd = -1;
269. 
270.     page_size = sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE);
271.     if (page_size <= 0) {
272.         fprintf(stderr, "failed to get page size\n");
273.         return -1;
274.     }
275. 
276.     map_offset = (off_t)(args->offset & ~((uint64_t)page_size - 1));
277.     delta      = (size_t)(args->offset - (uint64_t)map_offset);
278. 
279.     mapped->fd = open(args->dev_path, O_RDWR | O_SYNC);
280.     if (mapped->fd < 0) {
281.         perror("open");
282.         return -1;
283.     }
284. 
285.     mapped->map_length = (size_t)page_size;
286.     mapped->map_base   = mmap(NULL, mapped->map_length, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE,
287.                               MAP_SHARED, mapped->fd, map_offset);
288.     if (mapped->map_base == MAP_FAILED) {
289.         perror("mmap");
290.         close(mapped->fd);
291.         mapped->fd = -1;
292.         return -1;
293.     }
294. 
295.     if ((delta + sizeof(probe_page_t)) > mapped->map_length) {
296.         fprintf(stderr, "probe structure does not fit in mapped page\n");
297.         munmap(mapped->map_base, mapped->map_length);
298.         close(mapped->fd);
299.         mapped->map_base = NULL;
300.         mapped->fd       = -1;
301.         return -1;
302.     }
303. 
304.     mapped->page = (probe_page_t *)((char *)mapped->map_base + delta);
305.     return 0;
306. }
307. 
308. static void probe_unmap(mapped_probe_t *mapped)
309. {
310.     if (mapped->map_base != NULL) {
311.         munmap(mapped->map_base, mapped->map_length);
312.     }
313.     if (mapped->fd >= 0) {
314.         close(mapped->fd);
315.     }
316. }

322.     mapped->page->faa_word  = 0;
323.     mapped->page->reserved  = 0;

326.            args->dev_path, args->offset);

329. static void probe_log_lock_anomaly(const char *kind, uint64_t iter,
330.                                    uint64_t observed, uint64_t token,
331.                                    uint64_t head, uint64_t limit,
332.                                    uint64_t *count_p)
333. {
334.     if (*count_p >= limit) {
335.         return;
336.     }
337. 
338.     ++(*count_p);
339.     printf("lock64 anomaly[%s]: iter=%" PRIu64 " observed=0x%016" PRIx64
340.            " token=0x%016" PRIx64 " head=%" PRIu64 "\n",
341.            kind, iter, observed, token, head);
342. }
343. 
344. static void probe_run_lock64(mapped_probe_t *mapped, const probe_args_t *args)
345. {
346.     uint64_t i;
347.     uint64_t lock_busy = 0;
348.     uint64_t acquired = 0;
349.     uint64_t owner_mismatch = 0;
350.     uint64_t readback_nonzero = 0;
351.     uint64_t anomaly_lines = 0;
352. 
353.     printf("lock64 start: dev=%s offset=%" PRIu64 " token=0x%016" PRIx64
354.            " iters=%" PRIu64 " hold_loops=%" PRIu64 "\n",
355.            args->dev_path, args->offset, args->token, args->iters,
356.            args->hold_loops);
357. 
358.     for (i = 0; i < args->iters; ++i) {
359.         uint64_t head;
360.         uint64_t observed;
361.         uint64_t spin;
362. 
363.         probe_bus_load_fence();
364.         if (mapped->page->lock_word != 0) {
365.             ++lock_busy;
366.             continue;
367.         }
368. 
369.         (void)probe_atomic_cswap64(&mapped->page->lock_word, 0, args->token);
370.         probe_bus_full_fence();
371.         if (mapped->page->lock_word != args->token) {
372.             ++lock_busy;
373.             continue;
374.         }
375. 
376.         ++acquired;
377. 
378.         probe_bus_load_fence();
379.         head = mapped->page->head_word;
380.         probe_bus_full_fence();
381.         mapped->page->head_word = head + 1;
382. 
383.         for (spin = 0; spin < args->hold_loops; ++spin) {
384.             __asm__ __volatile__("" ::: "memory");
385.         }
386. 
387.         probe_bus_load_fence();
388.         observed = mapped->page->lock_word;
389.         if (observed != args->token) {
390.             ++owner_mismatch;
391.             probe_log_lock_anomaly("owner_mismatch", i, observed, args->token,
392.                                    head, args->anomaly_limit, &anomaly_lines);
393.         }
394. 
395.         probe_bus_store_fence();
396.         mapped->page->lock_word = 0;
397.         probe_bus_full_fence();
398.         observed = mapped->page->lock_word;
399.         if (observed != 0) {
400.             ++readback_nonzero;
401.             probe_log_lock_anomaly("unlock_readback_nonzero", i, observed,
402.                                    args->token, head, args->anomaly_limit,
403.                                    &anomaly_lines);
404.         }
405.     }
406. 
407.     printf("lock64 summary: token=0x%016" PRIx64 " acquired=%" PRIu64
408.            " busy=%" PRIu64 " owner_mismatch=%" PRIu64
409.            " unlock_readback_nonzero=%" PRIu64
410.            " final_lock=0x%016" PRIx64 " final_head=%" PRIu64 "\n",
411.            args->token, acquired, lock_busy, owner_mismatch,
412.            readback_nonzero, mapped->page->lock_word, mapped->page->head_word);
413. }
414. 
415. static void probe_log_faa_anomaly(const char *kind, uint64_t iter, uint64_t oldv,
416.                                   uint64_t after, uint64_t prev_old,
417.                                   uint64_t limit, uint64_t *count_p)
418. {
419.     if (*count_p >= limit) {
420.         return;
421.     }
422. 
423.     ++(*count_p);
424.     printf("faa64 anomaly[%s]: iter=%" PRIu64 " old=%" PRIu64
425.            " after=%" PRIu64 " prev_old=%" PRIu64 "\n",
426.            kind, iter, oldv, after, prev_old);
427. }
428. 
429. static void probe_run_faa64(mapped_probe_t *mapped, const probe_args_t *args)
430. {
431.     uint64_t i;
432.     uint64_t oldv;
433.     uint64_t after;
434.     uint64_t prev_old = 0;
435.     uint64_t monotonic_fail = 0;
436.     uint64_t readback_fail = 0;
437.     uint64_t anomaly_lines = 0;
438.     uint64_t min_delta = UINT64_MAX;
439.     uint64_t max_delta = 0;
440.     int have_prev = 0;
441. 
442.     printf("faa64 start: dev=%s offset=%" PRIu64 " iters=%" PRIu64 "\n",
443.            args->dev_path, args->offset, args->iters);
444. 
445.     for (i = 0; i < args->iters; ++i) {
446.         oldv = probe_atomic_fetch_add64(&mapped->page->faa_word, 1);
447.         probe_bus_full_fence();
448.         after = mapped->page->faa_word;
449. 
450.         if (have_prev) {
451.             uint64_t delta = oldv - prev_old;
452. 
453.             if (oldv <= prev_old) {
454.                 ++monotonic_fail;
455.                 probe_log_faa_anomaly("non_monotonic_old", i, oldv, after,
456.                                       prev_old, args->anomaly_limit,
457.                                       &anomaly_lines);
458.             } else {
459.                 if (delta < min_delta) {
460.                     min_delta = delta;
461.                 }
462.                 if (delta > max_delta) {
463.                     max_delta = delta;
464.                 }
465.             }
466.         } else {
467.             have_prev = 1;
468.         }
469. 
470.         if (after < (oldv + 1)) {
471.             ++readback_fail;
472.             probe_log_faa_anomaly("readback_lt_old_plus_1", i, oldv, after,
473.                                   prev_old, args->anomaly_limit,
474.                                   &anomaly_lines);
475.         }
476. 
477.         prev_old = oldv;
478.     }
479. 
480.     if (min_delta == UINT64_MAX) {
481.         min_delta = 0;
482.     }
483. 
484.     printf("faa64 summary: ops=%" PRIu64 " monotonic_fail=%" PRIu64
485.            " readback_fail=%" PRIu64 " min_delta=%" PRIu64
486.            " max_delta=%" PRIu64 " final_counter=%" PRIu64 "\n",
487.            args->iters, monotonic_fail, readback_fail, min_delta, max_delta,
488.            mapped->page->faa_word);
489. }
490. 
491. int main(int argc, char **argv)
492. {
493.     probe_args_t  args;
494.     mapped_probe_t mapped;
495. 
496.     if (probe_parse_args(argc, argv, &args) != 0) {
497.         probe_usage(argv[0]);
498.         return 1;
499.     }
500. 
501.     if (probe_map(&args, &mapped) != 0) {
502.         return 1;
503.     }
504. 
505.     switch (args.mode) {
506.     case PROBE_MODE_CLEAR:
507.         probe_clear(&mapped, &args);
508.         break;
509.     case PROBE_MODE_LOCK64:
510.         probe_run_lock64(&mapped, &args);
511.         break;
512.     case PROBE_MODE_FAA64:
513.         probe_run_faa64(&mapped, &args);
514.         break;
515.     default:
516.         probe_usage(argv[0]);
517.         probe_unmap(&mapped);
518.         return 1;
519.     }
520. 
521.     probe_unmap(&mapped);
522.     return 0;
523. }

## Issue: Incorrect fence placement allows lock-word corruption during critical section
**File:** obmm_atomic_probe.c:369-374
**Severity:** Critical
**Problem:** The lock acquisition uses a CAS followed by a full fence, then reads the lock_word back to confirm acquisition. However, the CAS instruction (`__sync_val_compare_and_swap`) itself does not guarantee ordering with the subsequent load on line 371. On weakly-ordered architectures (ARM, RISC-V, Power), another thread's write could become visible between the CAS and the readback, causing a false "lock not acquired" signal even though this thread successfully won the CAS race. This breaks the lock protocol's correctness assumption.

**Evidence:** 
- Line 369: CAS returns the old value but doesn't guarantee the write is globally visible
- Line 370: Full fence after CAS
- Line 371: Load of lock_word - on ARM/RISC-V this load can be reordered or see stale cache data despite the fence if the CAS hasn't propagated
- The `__sync_*` builtins provide acquire/release semantics but the exact ordering between CAS completion and subsequent NC-mapped loads on ARM is underspecified for O_SYNC mappings

**Suggested fix:** Insert a load fence before line 371, or rely solely on the CAS return value instead of reading back the lock_word. The readback pattern assumes a sequentially-consistent memory model that O_SYNC NC mappings may not provide.

---

## Issue: Unlocked lock-word read creates race condition
**File:** obmm_atomic_probe.c:363-367
**Severity:** High
**Problem:** The code reads `lock_word` with a plain volatile load (line 364) without any atomic operation, then decides whether to attempt CAS based on that stale value. On NC mappings with weak ordering, this read could see a cached or reordered value. More critically, even if the read sees 0, another thread could acquire the lock between line 364 and line 369, making the "skip if busy" optimization ineffective. While this doesn't violate safety (the CAS is still atomic), the `lock_busy` counter will significantly undercount actual contention, making the diagnostic output misleading for the stated purpose of detecting anomalies.

**Evidence:**
- Line 364: Plain load with only a preceding load fence
- No atomic operation protects this read
- If lock_word is non-zero due to reordering or cache effects on NC, the thread skips the CAS but increments `lock_busy` as if contention occurred
- For a diagnostic tool meant to surface anomalies, this creates false negatives

**Suggested fix:** Either remove the pre-check (always attempt CAS) or clearly document that `lock_busy` counts "observed non-zero" not "actual contention". For anomaly detection, eliminating the pre-check would give cleaner results.

**Problem:** The code reads `head_word`, increments it, and writes back without checking for overflow. While unlikely in practice, this is a diagnostic tool meant to detect anomalies - if overflow occurs, the final `head_word` value in the summary will be incorrect and misleading when comparing multi-node results to verify all locks were counted.

**Evidence:** Line 381 writes `head + 1` with no bounds check; `head` is uint64_t and will wrap silently

**Suggested fix:** Check for `UINT64_MAX` and either saturate, warn, or abort. For a probe tool, logging the wrap would improve diagnosability.

If the NC mapping allows store-to-load reordering or has a slow writeback, another thread could have done a successful CAS on the same lock_word between our acquisition check (line 371) and this verification read (line 388), causing a false `owner_mismatch` error. This would be a false positive anomaly, making the diagnostic output unreliable.

**Evidence:**
- Lines 369-374: Lock acquisition sequence
- Line 387: Load fence doesn't prevent concurrent stores on weakly-ordered NC memory
- Line 388: Plain volatile load could see a concurrent write
- This is exactly the kind of anomaly the tool is meant to detect, but we can't distinguish between a real hardware bug and a tool-induced race

**Suggested fix:** This may be intentional to detect if the hardware violates expected semantics. If so, document this clearly. If not, the check should be removed or restructured to avoid false positives.

Based on my static analysis of `obmm_atomic_probe.c`, I found several critical correctness and safety issues:

## Issue: CAS return value discarded - cannot distinguish lock acquisition from failure
**File:** obmm_atomic_probe.c:369-374
**Severity:** Critical
**Problem:** The CAS operation at line 369 discards its return value with `(void)`, then attempts to verify lock acquisition by reading back `lock_word` at line 371. This is unreliable because:
1. **False failure detection**: If the CAS succeeds (this thread acquired the lock), another thread could acquire+release the lock between lines 370-371, causing the readback to see 0 instead of `token`. The thread incorrectly thinks it failed and skips its critical section.
2. **Cannot distinguish anomalies from races**: Without the CAS return value, you cannot tell whether seeing a non-token value means (a) the CAS failed normally, or (b) the CAS succeeded but hardware corruption occurred.
3. **For anomaly detection**: To detect if the hardware violated atomicity, you need to know the CAS succeeded, THEN check if the readback is corrupted. Current code cannot make this distinction.

**Evidence:** `__sync_val_compare_and_swap` returns the old value (0 on success, non-zero on failure). The code needs this to interpret the readback correctly.

**Suggested fix:** 
```c
uint64_t old = probe_atomic_cswap64(&mapped-\>page-\>lock_word, 0, args-\>token);
probe_bus_full_fence();
if (old != 0) {
    ++lock_busy;  // CAS failed - expected
    continue;
}
// CAS succeeded, now check for anomalies
uint64_t readback = mapped-\>page-\>lock_word;
if (readback != args-\>token) {
    // Real anomaly: CAS succeeded but readback is wrong!
    ++owner_mismatch;
    probe_log_lock_anomaly("cas_succeeded_readback_mismatch", ...);
    continue;
}
++acquired;
```

---

## Issue: Integer overflow in offset calculation can cause out-of-bounds memory access
**File:** obmm_atomic_probe.c:276-277, 295-301, 304
**Severity:** High
**Problem:** 
1. Line 276: `args-\>offset` (uint64_t) is cast to `off_t` (typically signed long) without bounds checking. On 32-bit systems or when `off_t` is 32-bit, offsets \> 2GB will overflow.
2. Line 277: `delta = args-\>offset - map_offset` computes the difference between a uint64_t and a possibly-negative or truncated `off_t`, risking underflow if types mismatch.
3. Line 295: Checks if `delta + sizeof(probe_page_t)` fits in the mapped page, but if `delta` wrapped due to line 277, this check passes incorrectly.
4. Line 304: Uses `delta` to compute the probe page pointer - if delta is wrong, this accesses out-of-bounds memory, likely causing a segfault or corrupting unrelated data.

**Evidence:** No validation that `args-\>offset \< OBMM_PROBE_REGION_BYTES` (128MB). User could pass `--offset 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`.

**Suggested fix:** Add validation in `probe_parse_args` or `probe_map`:
```c
if (args-\>offset \>= OBMM_PROBE_REGION_BYTES) {
    fprintf(stderr, "offset %" PRIu64 " exceeds region size\n", args-\>offset);
    return -1;
}
```

---

## Issue: Pre-acquisition lock_word read creates misleading diagnostics
**File:** obmm_atomic_probe.c:363-367
**Severity:** Medium
**Problem:** The code reads `lock_word` with a plain volatile load (line 364) before attempting CAS (line 369). On NC mappings with weakly-ordered memory, this read can see stale cached data or reordered values. If the read incorrectly sees non-zero (due to cache effects), the code skips the CAS and increments `lock_busy`, reporting false contention. For a diagnostic tool meant to detect hardware anomalies, this creates noise and false positives in the contention counter, making it harder to interpret results.

**Evidence:** Line 364 uses plain volatile load with only a preceding load fence; no atomic operation protects this read from reordering or stale data on NC.

**Suggested fix:** Remove the pre-check (lines 363-367) entirely. Always attempt the CAS and rely on its return value. This eliminates false readings and provides cleaner diagnostic data. The CAS is fast enough that the optimization is unnecessary for a diagnostic tool.

---

## Issue: Missing validation that opened device is actually a character device
**File:** obmm_atomic_probe.c:279-293
**Severity:** Medium
**Problem:** The code opens `args-\>dev_path` without verifying it's a character device file. If a user accidentally provides a regular file path, `open` succeeds, `O_SYNC` may be ignored or behave differently, and `mmap` succeeds but doesn't provide NC semantics. The tool would then run against cacheable memory, producing meaningless results - false negatives (no anomalies detected) or false positives (anomalies due to wrong memory type). For a hardware diagnostic tool, this silent failure mode is a severe diagnosability issue.

**Evidence:** No `fstat` check after line 279; any file path is accepted.

**Suggested fix:** After opening, verify the device type:
```c
struct stat st;
if (fstat(mapped-\>fd, &st) != 0 || !S_ISCHR(st.st_mode)) {
    fprintf(stderr, "error: %s is not a character device\n", args-\>dev_path);
    close(mapped-\>fd);
    return -1;
}
```

---

## Issue: Missing overflow check on head_word increment reduces diagnostic value
**File:** obmm_atomic_probe.c:378-381
**Severity:** Low
**Problem:** The code reads `head_word`, increments by 1, and writes back without checking for `UINT64_MAX`. If two processes run 2^64 total lock acquisitions (extremely unlikely but theoretically possible over days), `head_word` wraps to 0 silently. The final summary would report an incorrect count, making it impossible to verify that all lock acquisitions across both nodes were counted correctly - defeating one of the diagnostic goals.

**Evidence:** Line 381 writes `head + 1` with no bounds check.

**Suggested fix:** Add overflow detection:
```c
if (head == UINT64_MAX) {
    fprintf(stderr, "WARNING: head_word overflow at iter %" PRIu64 "\n", i);
    // Either saturate, abort, or continue with wrap - document behavior
}
mapped-\>page-\>head_word = head + 1;
```

267. static int probe_map(const probe_args_t *args, mapped_probe_t *mapped)
268. {
269.     long page_size;
270.     off_t map_offset;
271.     size_t delta;
272.     struct stat st;
273. 
274.     memset(mapped, 0, sizeof(*mapped));
275.     mapped->fd = -1;
276. 
277.     page_size = sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE);
278.     if (page_size <= 0) {
279.         fprintf(stderr, "failed to get page size\n");
280.         return -1;
281.     }
282. 
283.     map_offset = (off_t)(args->offset & ~((uint64_t)page_size - 1));
284.     delta      = (size_t)(args->offset - (uint64_t)map_offset);
285. 
286.     mapped->fd = open(args->dev_path, O_RDWR | O_SYNC);
287.     if (mapped->fd < 0) {
288.         perror("open");
289.         return -1;
290.     }
291.     if ((fstat(mapped->fd, &st) != 0) || !S_ISCHR(st.st_mode)) {
292.         fprintf(stderr, "%s is not a character device\n", args->dev_path);
293.         close(mapped->fd);
294.         mapped->fd = -1;
295.         return -1;
296.     }
297. 
298.     mapped->map_length = (size_t)page_size;
299.     mapped->map_base   = mmap(NULL, mapped->map_length, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE,
300.                               MAP_SHARED, mapped->fd, map_offset);
301.     if (mapped->map_base == MAP_FAILED) {
302.         perror("mmap");
303.         close(mapped->fd);
304.         mapped->fd = -1;
305.         return -1;
306.     }
307. 
308.     if ((delta + sizeof(probe_page_t)) > mapped->map_length) {
309.         fprintf(stderr, "probe structure does not fit in mapped page\n");
310.         munmap(mapped->map_base, mapped->map_length);
311.         close(mapped->fd);
312.         mapped->map_base = NULL;
313.         mapped->fd       = -1;
314.         return -1;
315.     }
316. 
317.     mapped->page = (probe_page_t *)((char *)mapped->map_base + delta);
318.     return 0;
319. }
320. 
321. static void probe_unmap(mapped_probe_t *mapped)
322. {
323.     if (mapped->map_base != NULL) {
324.         munmap(mapped->map_base, mapped->map_length);
325.     }
326.     if (mapped->fd >= 0) {
327.         close(mapped->fd);
328.     }
329. }

376.         uint64_t old;
377. 
378.         old = probe_atomic_cswap64(&mapped->page->lock_word, 0, args->token);

383.         }
384.

392.             probe_bus_store_fence();
393.             mapped->page->lock_word = 0;

395.             continue;
396.         }
397.

399. 
400.         probe_bus_load_fence();
401.         head = mapped->page->head_word;
402.         probe_bus_full_fence();

405.         for (spin = 0; spin < args->hold_loops; ++spin) {

410.         observed = mapped->page->lock_word;
411.         if (observed != args->token) {
412.             ++owner_mismatch;
413.             probe_log_lock_anomaly("owner_mismatch", i, observed, args->token,
414.                                    head, args->anomaly_limit, &anomaly_lines);
415.         }
416. 
417.         probe_bus_store_fence();
418.         mapped->page->lock_word = 0;
419.         probe_bus_full_fence();
420.         observed = mapped->page->lock_word;

<sub>⏱️ 2414m 23s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

**探针程序已经写好了：`obmm_atomic_probe.c`。** 它把问题从 UCX transport 里剥出来，分成两种模式：

- `lock64`：复现当前 64-bit shared lock 的 acquire/unlock 路径
- `faa64`：检查 64-bit FAA 返回值在本进程内是否单调自洽

最短用法：

```bash
gcc -O2 -std=gnu11 -o obmm_atomic_probe obmm_atomic_probe.c
./obmm_atomic_probe --dev /dev/obmm_shmdevX --mode clear
```

然后在**两个节点**上，针对**同一块底层 region** 的两个对应 device path，同时跑：

```bash
./obmm_atomic_probe --dev /dev/obmm_shmdevX --mode lock64 --iters 2000000
./obmm_atomic_probe --dev /dev/obmm_shmdevY --mode lock64 --iters 2000000
```

再跑：

```bash
./obmm_atomic_probe --dev /dev/obmm_shmdevX --mode faa64 --iters 2000000
./obmm_atomic_probe --dev /dev/obmm_shmdevY --mode faa64 --iters 2000000
```

默认探测页是 **128 MiB region 的最后一页**。跑的时候不要让 UCX/MPI 同时占这页。

你只需要回传这些短行，不用贴整段日志：
- `lock64 summary: ...`
- 任何 `lock64 anomaly[...]`
- `faa64 summary: ...`
- 任何 `faa64 anomaly[...]`

这样下一步就能判断：**是只有 lock word 坏，还是连 FAA 返回值也不可信。**

<sub>⏱️ 2546m 44s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

**已经足够定性了：根因不是 pending/arbiter，而是当前平台上 `O_SYNC` NC 映射里的 64-bit 原子 RMW 语义本身不可靠。** 所以 obmm **不能继续依赖 mm 式的共享 `head/lock` 多生产者方案**。

证据很硬：
- `lock64` 里同时出现了 `cas_succeeded_readback_mismatch` 和 `owner_mismatch`，说明 **CAS 成功后读回都可能不是自己写进去的 token**
- `faa64` 里有大量 `non_monotonic_old` 和 `readback_lt_old_plus_1`，而且 `final_counter=1768845 \< ops=2000000`，说明 **FAA 返回值和结果读回都不自洽**
- 这意味着问题不是“锁实现细节有 bug”，而是**把这块 NC 共享内存当成正常可依赖的 64-bit 原子共享状态**这件事本身就站不住

下一步不该再修现在这把锁了，**该改协议**：去掉跨节点共享 `lock/head` 的 CAS/FAA 依赖，改成**单写者可证明正确**的路径，比如每个 sender 对 receiver 用独立 SPSC 队列/邮箱，由 receiver 轮询。只要热路径里不再依赖跨节点共享 64-bit 原子状态，这类卡死才有根上消掉的可能。
