429.                   ucs_status_string(status));
430.         return status;
431.     }
432. 
433.     for (bank = 0; bank < UCT_OBMM_MAILBOX_BANK_COUNT; ++bank) {
434.         for (slot = 0; slot < UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT; ++slot) {

438.                                             self->bcopy_seg_size);

440.         }

444.     ucs_arbiter_init(&self->arbiter);
445. 
446.     ucs_debug("obmm: iface %p attached to region %p slot=%u gen=%u "
447.               "fifo_size=%u elem_size=%u seg_size=%u stride=%zu",
448.               self, region->base, self->slot_index, self->generation,
449.               self->fifo_size, self->fifo_elem_size, self->bcopy_seg_size,
450.               stride);
451.     return UCS_OK;
452. }

38. static UCS_F_NOINLINE ucs_status_t
39. uct_mm_ep_attach_remote_seg(uct_mm_ep_t *ep, uct_mm_seg_id_t seg_id,
40.                             size_t length, void **address_p)
41. {
42.     uct_mm_iface_t *iface = ucs_derived_of(ep->super.super.iface,
43.                                            uct_mm_iface_t);
44.     uct_mm_remote_seg_t *remote_seg;
45.     ucs_status_t status;
46.     khiter_t khiter;
47.     int khret;
48. 
49.     khiter = kh_put(uct_mm_remote_seg, &ep->remote_segs, seg_id, &khret);
50.     if (khret == UCS_KH_PUT_FAILED) {
51.         ucs_error("failed to add remote segment to mm ep hash");
52.         return UCS_ERR_NO_MEMORY;
53.     }
54. 
55.     /* we expect the key would either be
56.      * never used (BUCKET_EMPTY) or deleted (BUCKET_CLEAR) */
57.     ucs_assert_always((khret == UCS_KH_PUT_BUCKET_EMPTY) ||
58.                       (khret == UCS_KH_PUT_BUCKET_CLEAR));
59. 
60.     remote_seg = &kh_val(&ep->remote_segs, khiter);
61. 
62.     status = uct_mm_iface_mapper_call(iface, mem_attach, seg_id, length,
63.                                       ep->remote_iface_addr, remote_seg);
64.     if (status != UCS_OK) {
65.         kh_del(uct_mm_remote_seg, &ep->remote_segs, khiter);
66.         return status;
67.     }
68. 
69.     *address_p = remote_seg->address;
70.     ucs_debug("mm_ep %p: attached remote segment id 0x%"PRIx64" at %p cookie %p",
71.               ep, seg_id, remote_seg->address, remote_seg->cookie);
72.     return UCS_OK;

107. /* send a signal to remote interface using Unix-domain socket */
108. static void uct_mm_ep_signal_remote(uct_mm_ep_t *ep)
109. {
110.     uct_mm_iface_t *iface = ucs_derived_of(ep->super.super.iface, uct_mm_iface_t);
111.     char dummy = 0;
112.     int ret;
113. 
114.     ucs_trace("ep %p: signal remote", ep);
115. 
116.     for (;;) {
117.         ret = sendto(iface->signal_fd, &dummy, sizeof(dummy), 0,
118.                      (const struct sockaddr*)&ep->fifo_ctl->signal_sockaddr,
119.                      ep->fifo_ctl->signal_addrlen);
120.         if (ucs_unlikely(ret < 0)) {
121.             if (errno == EINTR) {
122.                 /* Interrupted system call - retry */
123.                 continue;
124.             }
125.             if ((errno == EAGAIN) || (errno == ECONNREFUSED)) {
126.                 /* If we failed to signal because buffer is full - ignore the error
127.                  * since it means the remote side would get a signal anyway.
128.                  * If the remote side is not there - ignore the error as well.
129.                  */
130.                 ucs_trace("failed to send wakeup signal: %m");
131.                 return;
132.             } else {
133.                 ucs_warn("failed to send wakeup signal: %m");
134.                 return;
135.             }
136.         } else {
137.             ucs_assert(ret == sizeof(dummy));
138.             ucs_trace("sent wakeup from socket %d to %s", iface->signal_fd,
139.                       ep->fifo_ctl->signal_sockaddr.sun_path);
140.             return;
141.         }
142.     }
143. }

158. static UCS_CLASS_INIT_FUNC(uct_mm_ep_t, const uct_ep_params_t *params)
159. {
160.     uct_mm_iface_t            *iface = ucs_derived_of(params->iface, uct_mm_iface_t);
161.     uct_mm_md_t               *md    = ucs_derived_of(iface->super.super.md, uct_mm_md_t);
162.     const uct_mm_iface_addr_t *addr  = (const void *)params->iface_addr;

169.     kh_init_inplace(uct_mm_remote_seg, &self->remote_segs);
170.     ucs_arbiter_group_init(&self->arb_group);
171. 
172.     /* save remote md address */
173.     if (md->iface_addr_len > 0) {
174.         self->remote_iface_addr = ucs_malloc(md->iface_addr_len, "mm_md_addr");
175.         if (self->remote_iface_addr == NULL) {
176.             status = UCS_ERR_NO_MEMORY;
177.             goto err;
178.         }
179. 
180.         memcpy(self->remote_iface_addr, addr + 1, md->iface_addr_len);
181.     } else {
182.         self->remote_iface_addr = NULL;
183.     }
184. 
185.     /* Attach the remote FIFO, use the same method as bcopy descriptors */
186.     status = uct_mm_ep_get_remote_seg(self, addr->fifo_seg_id,
187.                                       UCT_MM_GET_FIFO_SIZE(iface), &fifo_ptr);
188.     if (status != UCS_OK) {
189.         ucs_error("mm ep failed to connect to remote FIFO id 0x%"PRIx64": %s",
190.                   addr->fifo_seg_id, ucs_status_string(status));
191.         goto err_free_md_addr;
192.     }
193. 
194.     /* Initialize remote FIFO control structure */
195.     uct_mm_iface_set_fifo_ptrs(fifo_ptr, &self->fifo_ctl, &self->fifo_elems);
196.     self->cached_tail = self->fifo_ctl->tail;
197.     ucs_arbiter_elem_init(&self->arb_elem);
198. 
199.     status = uct_ep_keepalive_init(&self->keepalive, self->fifo_ctl->pid);
200.     if (status != UCS_OK) {
201.         goto err_free_segs;
202.     }
203. 
204.     ucs_debug("created mm ep %p, connected to remote FIFO id 0x%"PRIx64,

451.     }
452. 
453.     state_prev = ucs_atomic_cswap32(&pool->hdr->state, UCT_OBMM_POOL_STATE_READY,
454.                                     UCT_OBMM_POOL_STATE_INITING);
455.     if (state_prev != UCT_OBMM_POOL_STATE_READY) {
456.         return 0;
457.     }
458. 
459.     self_starttime = ucs_sys_get_proc_create_time(getpid());
460.     pool->hdr->initializer_pid       = (uint32_t)getpid();
461.     pool->hdr->initializer_starttime = (uint64_t)self_starttime;
462.     ucs_memory_bus_store_fence();
463. 
464.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
465.     if (!uct_obmm_pool_all_slots_free(pool)) {
466.         ucs_memory_bus_store_fence();
467.         pool->hdr->state = UCT_OBMM_POOL_STATE_READY;
468.         return 0;
469.     }
470. 
471.     return 1;
472. }

475. void uct_obmm_pool_reset(uct_obmm_pool_t *pool)
476. {
477.     uct_obmm_pool_hdr_t *hdr;
478.     char                *base;
479.     size_t               length;
480.     size_t               state_offset;
481.     size_t               state_end;
482.     size_t               init_pid_offset;
483.     size_t               init_start_offset;
484.     size_t               init_end;
485. 
486.     if ((pool == NULL) || (pool->hdr == NULL) || (pool->base == NULL)) {
487.         return;
488.     }
489. 
490.     hdr = pool->hdr;
491.     base   = (char*)pool->base;
492.     length = pool->length;
493. 
494.     state_offset      = offsetof(uct_obmm_pool_hdr_t, state);
495.     state_end         = state_offset + sizeof(hdr->state);
496.     init_pid_offset   = offsetof(uct_obmm_pool_hdr_t, initializer_pid);
497.     init_start_offset = offsetof(uct_obmm_pool_hdr_t, initializer_starttime);
498.     init_end          = init_start_offset + sizeof(hdr->initializer_starttime);
499. 
500.     if (state_offset > 0) {
501.         memset(base, 0, state_offset);
502.     }
503.     if (init_pid_offset > state_end) {
504.         memset(base + state_end, 0, init_pid_offset - state_end);
505.     }
506.     if (length > init_end) {
507.         memset(base + init_end, 0, length - init_end);
508.     }
509.     ucs_memory_bus_store_fence();
510. 
511.     hdr->initializer_pid       = 0;
512.     hdr->initializer_starttime = 0;
513.     ucs_memory_bus_store_fence();
514. 
515.     hdr->state = UCT_OBMM_POOL_STATE_UNINIT;
516.     ucs_memory_bus_store_fence();
517. 
518.     memset(pool, 0, sizeof(*pool));
519. }
520.

````
1. # obmm UCT transport — design notes
2. 
3. This file is the **single source of truth** for the on-region wire format
4. and the data-path semantics of the `obmm` UCT transport. Update it
5. **before** changing layout, capabilities, or sync rules. AGENTS.md
6. mandates retrieve-before-recall; this doc is the first thing to grep.
7. 
8. Status legend:
9. - **v1** = shipped, MPI cross-node smoke tests pass.
10. - **v2** = current target: complete `am_bcopy` (max_bcopy decoupled from
11.   FIFO element size, no per-message UCP fragmentation below seg_size).
12. 
13. ---
14. 
15. ## Locked-in environment facts
16. 
17. (Mirrors `.github/skills/obmm-api-and-env/SKILL.md`. Do NOT contradict
18. without re-checking that file.)
19. 
20. - Each node pre-exports **one 128 MiB region**; export/import is done
21.   outside UCX. UCT must NOT call `obmm_export/import/preimport/...`.
22. - Data-path mapping is **non-cacheable** (`open(... O_SYNC)` + mmap).
23.   `obmm_set_ownership` is forbidden and irrelevant.
24. - Cross-host atomic FAA/CAS on NC is supported (project-owner statement).
25. - Memory ordering uses **bus-domain fences**
26.   (`ucs_memory_bus_store_fence` / `ucs_memory_bus_load_fence`), NOT the
27.   CPU-domain `ucs_memory_cpu_*_fence` that mm uses. mm peers share an
28.   inner-shareable cache domain; obmm peers do not.
29. - Reachability is keyed on `(exporter_dcna, exporter_deid, memid)`,
30.   never memid alone.
31. - Two-phase pool init (UNINIT → INITING → READY via CAS) plus per-slot
32.   `(generation, owner_pid, owner_starttime)` for crash/PID-reuse safety.
33.   During teardown, INITING is reused only as a transient cleanup lock; after
34.   reset the shared region returns to literal all-zero memory.
35. - ARM64 is the production ISA. NC + bus fences are correct on aarch64.
36. 
37. ---
38. 
39. ## Region layout (v2)
40. 
41. Inside the 128 MiB exported region:
42. 
43. ```
44. +-------------------------------------------------------+ offset 0
45. | uct_obmm_pool_hdr_t (magic, state, geometry)          |
46. +-------------------------------------------------------+
47. | alloc_bitmap[bitmap_words]                            |
48. +-------------------------------------------------------+
49. | slot_meta[slot_count]  (gen, owner_pid, starttime, …) |
50. +-------------------------------------------------------+ hdr->slot_array_offset
51. | slot[0]:                                              |
52. |   uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t  (head + tail, padded)          |
53. |   fifo_elem[fifo_size]  (elem_size each)              |
54. |   bcopy_desc[fifo_size] (seg_size each)   <-- NEW v2  |
55. +-------------------------------------------------------+
56. | slot[1]: …                                            |
57. …
58. ```
59. 
60. **Key invariant (v2)**: every FIFO element `elem[N]` (N = `idx & mask`)
61. has a paired `desc[N]` of `seg_size` bytes in the same slot. Lifetime of
62. `desc[N]` is **identical** to lifetime of `elem[N]` — both are released
63. together when the receiver bumps tail past index N, and both are
64. overwritten together by the sender that claims index N+fifo_size.
65. 
66. This eliminates the cross-host desc free-list problem: there is no
67. separate desc allocator, no per-desc CAS, and no risk of the desc pool
68. running dry while FIFO slots remain available. The FIFO already has
69. exactly the right backpressure semantics.
70. 
71. ### Slot stride
72. 
73. ```
74. slot_stride = align_up(
75.     sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_ctl_t) +
76.     fifo_size * elem_size +
77.     fifo_size * seg_size,
78.     cacheline)
79. ```
80. 
81. The pool's `slot_count` (compile-time `UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT = 32`)
82. **times** `slot_stride` MUST fit in `region->length` (128 MiB minus pool
83.  header overhead). Defaults are picked to favor short-path coverage over
84.  maximum local process count; lowering `seg_size` and/or `fifo_size`
85.  reduces per-slot footprint, but the supported local attach count remains
86.  the compile-time `slot_count`.
87. 
88. Default budget check:
89. ```
90. fifo_size       =     64
91. elem_size       =  16448   (raw UCT max_short = 16432 total bytes)
92. seg_size        =  32768   (raw UCT max_bcopy = 32768)
93. ctl + slot data = 128 + 64*(16448+32768) = ~3076 KiB / slot
94. slot_count      =     32
95. total           = ~ 96 MiB / 128 MiB                     ✓
96. ```
97. These defaults are chosen from the measured OSU latency sweep rather than from
98. wire-format arithmetic alone. With Open MPI PML/UCX on this tree, ordinary
99. `MPI_Send` goes through `mca_pml_ucx_send_nbr()` into `ucp_tag_send_nbx()`,
100. and UCX defaults `PROTO_ENABLE=y`, so protocol v2 selects between eager short,
101. eager bcopy single/multi, and rendezvous using its own headers and cost model.
102. The best reasoning-backed configuration found so far is to keep both geometry
103. knobs 64-byte aligned, leave `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE=32768` for 32KiB-class raw bcopy
104. capacity, and reduce `FIFO_ELEM_SIZE` to `16448` so 16KiB-class payloads stay
105. comfortably on short without over-extending the short window into slower
106. 32KiB-class territory.
107. 
108. If a user also pushes the short geometry back to a 32768-byte payload
109. (`elem_size=32792`) while simultaneously stretches bcopy to `seg_size=32792`,
110. the pool overruns the 128 MiB region by 103232 bytes and attach fails with a
111. clear error pointing at the geometry knobs.
112. 
113. When the last local iface on an export exits, UCX resets the entire local
114. export region to zero before another attach may re-initialize the pool.
115. 
116. ---
117. 
118. ## FIFO element layout
119. 
120. `uct_obmm_fifo_element_t` (16 bytes, packed) is unchanged from v1:
121. 
122. | field      | bytes | notes                                          |
123. |------------|-------|------------------------------------------------|
124. | flags      |   1   | OWNER bit + BCOPY bit                          |
125. | am_id      |   1   |                                                |
126. | length     |   2   | u16 — payload bytes (excl. am_short hdr)       |
127. | generation |   4   | slot generation token at TX time               |
128. | header     |   8   | am_short user-visible 8B header (unused bcopy) |
129. 
130. **am_short payload** still lives inline at `elem + 1` in the FIFO area.
131. Wire format and `max_short = elem_size - 16` are unchanged.
132. 
133. **am_bcopy payload** (NEW in v2) lives in the paired `desc[N]` instead
134. of inside the FIFO element body. The element body is unused for bcopy;
135. on bcopy the sender writes:
136. - `elem->flags  = OWNER | BCOPY`
137. - `elem->am_id  = id`
138. - `elem->length = pack_cb_returned_length`     (≤ seg_size, so ≤ u16max)
139. - `elem->generation = ep->expected_generation`
140. - `elem->header = 0` (unused)
141. 
142. Receiver, on seeing FLAG_BCOPY, computes
143. `desc[N] = slot_descs + (idx & mask) * seg_size` and calls
144. `uct_iface_invoke_am(am_id, desc[N], length, 0)`.
145. 
146. Because `desc[N]` is bound 1:1 to `elem[N]`, no extra metadata is
147. exchanged in the FIFO element to locate the desc.
148. 
149. ### `length` field width
150. 
151. `elem->length` stays `uint16_t`, capping `seg_size` at 65535. We reject
152. larger `seg_size` at iface init. If a future `seg_size > 64KiB` is
153. needed, widen `length` to `uint32_t` and update the compatibility checks.
154. 
155. ---
156. 
157. ## Sender side (`obmm_ep`)
158. 
159. Both `am_short` and `am_bcopy` reserve a slot identically:
160. 
161. ```
162. 1. load head from peer_ctl->head
163. 2. if (head - cached_tail) >= fifo_size:
164.        bus_load_fence; refresh cached_tail; recheck;
165.        if still full: return UCS_ERR_NO_RESOURCE
166. 3. claim producer lock (`peer_ctl->lock`) with a unique token, then
167.    store head → head+1, then release the lock
168. 4. compute idx = head, N = idx & mask
169. 5. payload write:
170.      short: memcpy header+payload into elem[N]+1
171.      bcopy: pack_cb(desc[N], arg) -> length
172. 6. fill elem[N] header fields (am_id, length, generation, [header])
173. 7. ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()                          <- release barrier
174. 8. elem[N]->flags = OWNER_BIT_FOR_THIS_LAP | (BCOPY if bcopy)
175. ```
176. 
177. The OWNER bit alternates each lap of the ring (see `obmm_iface.c`
178. `uct_obmm_iface_progress` for why). Since `desc[N]` writes happen
179. **before** the bus_store_fence, they become visible to the peer at the
180. same time as the published flags byte.
181. 
182. The producer lock exists because on the validated target aarch64 NC
183. environment, cross-node CAS updates memory correctly but its return value
184. is not reliable enough to use as a head-claim ownership result. The token
185. lock converts reservation into: acquire lock by readback, re-check space,
186. plain-store new head, release lock.
187. 
188. ### Pending
189. 
190. `ep_pending_add` returns `UCS_ERR_BUSY` (UCP retries via its own
191. progress loop). Real arbiter is out of scope for v1/v2 — backpressure
192. is bounded because the receiver drains continuously.
193. 
194. ---
195. 
196. ## Receiver side (`obmm_iface_progress`)
197. 
198. ```
199. loop up to fifo_max_poll:
200.     elem = elem[read_index & mask]
201.     expected_owner = lap_parity(read_index)
202.     if (elem->flags & OWNER) != expected_owner: break       (no work)
203.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence()                              (acquire)
204.     if elem->generation != iface->generation:
205.         drop silently (slot was reused after our death+rebirth)
206.     elif elem->flags & BCOPY:
207.         desc = desc[read_index & mask]
208.         invoke_am(am_id, desc,  length, 0)
209.     else:
210.         invoke_am(am_id, &elem->header, length, 0)
211.     read_index++
212. if any progress:
213.     ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()
214.     recv_ctl->tail = read_index
215. ```
216. 
217. **Why the fence ordering is correct for bcopy too**: the
218. `ucs_memory_bus_load_fence()` issued after observing the flags byte
219. orders **all** subsequent loads in this iteration — including the
220. load of `desc[N]` performed inside the AM handler's memcpy. The handler
221. is `CB_SYNC` (synchronous), so the fence-acquire pairs with the
222. sender's `bus_store_fence` before publishing flags.
223. 
224. ---
225. 
226. ## Capabilities (`iface_query`)
227. 
228. | flag                            | v1 | v2 | notes                       |
229. |---------------------------------|----|----|-----------------------------|
230. | AM_SHORT                        |  ✓ |  ✓ | max = elem_size - 16        |
231. | AM_BCOPY                        |  ✓ |  ✓ | v1: = max_short (cramped); v2: = seg_size |
232. | PENDING                         |  ✓ |  ✓ | returns BUSY only           |
233. | CONNECT_TO_IFACE                |  ✓ |  ✓ |                             |
234. | CB_SYNC                         |  ✓ |  ✓ |                             |
235. | INTER_NODE                      |  ✓ |  ✓ | required for cross-host UCT (otherwise OMPI's NET_ONLY filter strips us — see ucp_worker.c:2962) |
236. 
237. **Not advertised** in v1/v2: PUT/GET (any), ATOMIC, AM_ZCOPY, EP_CHECK,
238. AM_DUP, ERRHANDLE_PEER. Adding any of these requires a separate design
239. note.
240. 
241. ---
242. 
243. ## Wire-format compat
244. 
245. `uct_obmm_iface_addr_t` carries `(slot_index, generation, pid,
246. fifo_size, fifo_elem_size, bcopy_seg_size)`. v2 **adds** `bcopy_seg_size`
247. (replaces v1's `reserved` u32 → no struct-size change). Two ifaces are
248. mutually reachable iff all three geometry fields match — guarded in
249. `is_reachable_v2`. Pool compatibility is enforced by the shared pool
250. geometry checks in `pool_attach`/`pool_open`; the shared region does not
251. persist a separate pool version word or filler replacement field.
252. 
253. ---
254. 
255. ## Configuration knobs
256. 
257. All under `UCX_OBMM_*` prefix.
258. 
259. | knob                      | default | meaning                          |
260. |---------------------------|---------|----------------------------------|
````

</details>

268. `BW` is a UCP-facing estimate, not a wire-format limit. UCP folds it into lane
269. selection and protocol cost modeling, so it should track sustained transport
270. throughput rather than a one-off peak number. Leaving `UCX_OBMM_BW` unset is
271. valid; obmm then uses the built-in default above.
272.

274. - `FIFO_SIZE` > 0, power of 2
275. - `FIFO_ELEM_SIZE` > sizeof(elem_hdr) and `(elem_size - hdr) <= UINT16_MAX`

277. - `slot_count * slot_stride + pool_overhead <= region->length`

279. ---
280. 
281. ## Future scope (not in v2)
282. 
283. - `am_zcopy`: requires UCT MD memory-handle plumbing (`mem_reg`,
284.   `mkey_pack`, `mem_attach`). Currently obmm has no MD-level
285.   registration — every peer access is via the pre-existing 128 MiB
286.   region. Out of scope until libobmm-aware md is added.
287. - `put_bcopy / get_bcopy`: blocked by the same MD plumbing; UCP RMA
288.   cannot be served by the FIFO-only data path.
289. - Real pending arbiter: needed only if profiling shows BUSY-retry
290.   storms.
291. - Multi-region per node, NUMA-aware slot placement.
292. - Variable-size desc allocator (mm-style mpool) to cover medium-size
293.   messages without burning seg_size per FIFO depth.
294. 
295. ---
296. 
297. ## Receive-side fence ordering (full bus fence at tail release)
298. 
299. `ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()` on aarch64 is `dmb oshst` — store→store
300. only. It does NOT order prior loads against subsequent stores. The
301. receiver's lifetime invariant requires:
302. 
303. ```
304. loads from desc[N]  HAPPENS-BEFORE  store to recv_ctl->tail = N+1
305. ```
306. 
307. Otherwise a sender that observes the new tail can reuse `desc[N]` while
308. the receiver core still has outstanding loads in flight from the old
309. lap's payload. We therefore use `uct_obmm_bus_full_fence()` (defined
310. locally in `obmm_fifo.h`: `dmb osh` on aarch64, `mfence` on x86,
311. `sync` on ppc64, `fence iorw,iorw` on rv64) before the tail store, not
312. the bus_store fence.
313. 
314. Why a local helper rather than adding `ucs_memory_bus_fence()` for all
315. archs in `ucs/arch/`: AGENTS.md restricts changes to
316. `ucx/src/uct/obmm/`. If/when the helper proves useful elsewhere, it can
317. be promoted to ucs/arch — but that is a separate ask.
318. 
319. ## Receive-buffer semantics for AM handler
320. 
321. `invoke_am(..., desc, length, 0)` — the trailing `0` (no
322. `UCT_CB_PARAM_FLAG_DESC`) means the data pointer is valid **only for the
323. duration of the callback**. The handler MUST NOT retain it; UCP knows
324. this contract and copies into its own buffer when persistence is
325. needed.
326. 
327. This is by design: the desc lifetime is bound 1:1 to the FIFO element
328. slot, so as soon as the receiver advances `tail` past N, the sender is
329. free to overwrite `desc[N]` on the next lap. There is no separate desc
330. allocator to support post-callback retention.
331. 
332. If a future need arises to support `UCT_CB_PARAM_FLAG_DESC`-style
333. returnable descriptors (e.g. for AM zcopy or large-message rendezvous
334. without copy), it requires a real per-iface mpool of receive
335. descriptors that the upper layer can hold and release explicitly —
336. mirroring `uct_mm_recv_desc_t`. Out of scope for v2.
337. 
338. ## Verification (no hardware)
339.

341. 
342. 1. Build via `task` agent: `./autogen.sh && ./contrib/configure-devel
343.    && make -j && make install`.
344. 2. `ucx_info -d -t obmm` → confirm `am_short` and `am_bcopy` lines:
345.    `max_short` should report 16432 total bytes and `max_bcopy` should reflect
346.    raw `seg_size` (default 32768).
347. 3. `ucx_info -c | grep OBMM` → confirm new `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE` entry.
348. 4. `nm -D libuct.so | grep uct_obmm_ep_am_bcopy` → exists.
349. 5. Hardware-required checks (cross-node MPI, sweep sizes through
350.    `> max_short` and `> max_bcopy`) deferred to user-driven runs on
351.    the real two-node setup.
352.
````

</details>

Now I have enough context to analyze the code for substantive issues. Let me trace through the critical flows:

## Issue: Missing fence before head publish in sender path
**File:** ucx/src/uct/obmm/base/obmm_ep.c:318-319 (am_short) and 368-369 (am_bcopy)
**Severity:** Critical
**Problem:** The sender publishes the new head value **before** incrementing its local `tx_index`, creating a potential visibility ordering bug. The sequence is:
```c
ucs_memory_bus_store_fence();     // line 317/367
ep->tx_index      = index + 1;    // line 318/368  ← local update
ep->tx_ctl->head  = ep->tx_index; // line 319/369  ← NC store visible to peer
```
The `bus_store_fence()` orders prior payload stores before the fence, but does **not** order the subsequent local `tx_index` write before the `ep->tx_ctl->head` NC store. On weakly-ordered architectures, the compiler or CPU could reorder the NC store to `head` before the local `tx_index` update. If a signal or context switch occurs between those two lines, or if the sender later calls `uct_obmm_ep_has_tx_resource()` from another thread/context, it could observe stale `tx_index` while the receiver has already seen the new `head`, violating the SPSC invariant.

**Evidence:** The old lock-based protocol avoided this by performing the head increment as part of the locked critical section with a full fence afterward. The new code eliminated the lock but must still ensure the local index update is visible before the NC head update reaches the peer.

**Suggested fix:** Add a second `ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()` between the `tx_index` update and the `head` store, or use a full fence (since the local write must be visible before the NC write):
```c
ucs_memory_bus_store_fence();     // order payload writes
ep->tx_index = index + 1;
uct_obmm_bus_full_fence();         // order tx_index write before head publish
ep->tx_ctl->head = ep->tx_index;
```

---

## Issue: RX lane tail ack missing generation check after element drop
**File:** ucx/src/uct/obmm/base/obmm_iface.c:249-267
**Severity:** High
**Problem:** When the receiver drops a stale element (line 249-260), it still advances `rx_index` and publishes the new `tail` (lines 262-266) **without** re-verifying that `lane->ctl->sender_generation` still matches `lane->sender_generation`. Between the initial generation check (line 236) and the tail publish (line 264), the sender slot could have been torn down and reallocated with a new generation. Publishing a tail update to a lane that now belongs to a different sender can cause that sender to believe space was freed when it wasn't, leading to slot reuse corruption.

**Evidence:** The receiver checks `sender_generation` at line 236 to decide whether to skip the lane, but after consuming/dropping an element, it publishes tail without re-checking. The DESIGN.md states that stale writes should be dropped "silently," but the tail publish is not silent—it signals the sender that space is available.

**Suggested fix:** Either re-check `sender_generation` before publishing tail, or move the tail publish inside the `if (elem->generation == iface->generation)` block so it only acknowledges valid elements. The safest approach:
```c
if (elem->generation == iface->generation) {
    /* invoke AM ... */
    lane->rx_index++;
    uct_obmm_bus_full_fence();
    lane->ctl->tail = lane->rx_index;
    ucs_memory_bus_store_fence();
    lane->ctl->tail_generation = lane->sender_generation;
    return 1;
}
/* stale element: don't ack, just continue to next lane */
return 0;
```

## Issue: EP cached_tail initialization race with concurrent receiver start
**File:** ucx/src/uct/obmm/base/obmm_ep.c:238-239
**Severity:** Medium
**Problem:** EP initialization reads `self->tx_ctl->tail_generation` and `self->tx_ctl->tail` without a bus load fence. If the matching receiver has already started consuming on this lane (another EP to the same peer could have registered the RX lane first), the sender could read stale cached values of `tail` and `tail_generation`, leading to an incorrect `cached_tail` that underestimates available space.

**Evidence:** Line 238-239 performs:
```c
self->cached_tail = (self->tx_ctl->tail_generation == iface->generation) ?
                    self->tx_ctl->tail : self->tx_index;
```
without a preceding `ucs_memory_bus_load_fence()`. The receiver writes `tail_generation` at line 266 of `obmm_iface.c` after a store fence, so the sender must use a load fence to pair with it.

**Suggested fix:** Add a bus load fence before the conditional read:
```c
ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
self->cached_tail = (self->tx_ctl->tail_generation == iface->generation) ?
                    self->tx_ctl->tail : self->tx_index;
```

---

## Issue: RX lane registration overwrites active lane without draining in-flight elements
**File:** ucx/src/uct/obmm/base/obmm_ep.c:44-70
**Severity:** High
**Problem:** If `uct_obmm_ep_register_rx_lane()` finds an existing lane that doesn't match the new EP's generation or peer identity (lines 47-52), it unconditionally overwrites the lane's control pointers, generation, and `rx_index` without checking if there are still unprocessed elements from the old sender. The old sender may have published elements that the receiver hasn't consumed yet. Overwriting `lane->sender_generation` and resetting `rx_index` causes those in-flight elements to be silently dropped, but the sender doesn't know this and may have already reported success to UCP.

**Evidence:** Lines 47-52 check if the lane is inactive **or** if identity/generation has changed, then unconditionally reinitialize. But the old sender could still have `head > tail` with pending elements. The receiver should drain those first or coordinate teardown.

**Suggested fix:** This is a deeper protocol issue. The safe fix requires either (a) ensuring the old sender is fully quiesced before the lane is reused (e.g., ref-counted teardown waits for tail to catch up), or (b) adding an epoch/barrier mechanism. As written, the protocol assumes lane reuse only happens after the old sender has exited, which may not be guaranteed if EPs are destroyed out of order. At minimum, add a warning or assertion if `lane->ctl->head != lane->rx_index` when overwriting.

---

## Issue: Potential uint32 wraparound in tx_index not handled for fifo_size > 1
**File:** ucx/src/uct/obmm/base/obmm_ep.c:106-120
**Severity:** Medium (latent, fifo_size=1 default avoids it)
**Problem:** `tx_index` and `rx_index` are `uint32_t` and increment monotonically. With fifo_size=1, wraparound happens at 4B sends, but if fifo_size increases, the distance check `(uint32_t)(ep->tx_index - ep->cached_tail) < ep->fifo_size` (line 112) relies on unsigned arithmetic wraparound. If `tx_index` wraps but `cached_tail` doesn't (or vice versa), the distance check can spuriously succeed or fail.

**Evidence:** The code uses `uint32_t` for indices but doesn't explicitly handle wraparound. UCX's mm transport uses `uint64_t` for similar monotonic indices to defer wraparound indefinitely. The default fifo_size=1 makes this unlikely to trigger in practice, but the code claims to support power-of-2 fifo_size up to the geometry budget.

**Suggested fix:** Either (a) change `tx_index`, `rx_index`, `head`, `tail` to `uint64_t` to match UCX convention and defer wraparound, or (b) add comments and assertions documenting that the unsigned wraparound arithmetic is intentional and tested. The wire format already uses `uint32_t generation` tokens, so extending indices to 64-bit wouldn't break compatibility.

---

No significant issues found in:
- Wire-format consistency (geometry fields are checked at EP create)
- Pending arbiter flow (correctly queues and dispatches every progress call)
- Stale element drops (generation check at line 249 correctly discards mismatched elements)
- Fence usage for payload writes (bus_store_fence before publish is correct)

<sub>⏱️ 2593m 23s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

**是的，就当前这套 mailbox 框架的设计来说，跨节点收发路径已经不依赖跨节点原子 RMW 了。**

更准确地说：

- **数据面不依赖**：`head/tail/sender_generation/tail_generation` 都是 **单写者** 字段，靠普通 load/store + bus fence 保序，不再用跨节点 `CAS/FAA` 去抢 head、加 tail、加锁。
- **还保留的原子不在跨节点收发路径里**：现在剩下的 CAS 主要还是 **本地 export region 的 pool/slot 生命周期管理**，用于本机多进程 attach / alloc / free / cleanup 的互斥，不是跨节点消息发送依赖的机制。

所以如果你问的是**“消息发送/接收这条主路径是否还建立在跨节点原子可用这个前提上”**，答案就是 **不再建立在这个前提上了**。

138. int ompi_coll_tuned_bcast_intra_do_this(void *buf, size_t count,
139.                                         struct ompi_datatype_t *dtype,
140.                                         int root,
141.                                         struct ompi_communicator_t *comm,
142.                                         mca_coll_base_module_t *module,
143.                                         int algorithm, int faninout, int segsize)
144. {
145.     OPAL_OUTPUT_VERBOSE((COLL_TUNED_TRACING_VERBOSE, ompi_coll_tuned_stream,
146.         "coll:tuned:bcast_intra_do_this algorithm %d topo faninout %d segsize %d",
147.         algorithm, faninout, segsize));
148. 
149.     switch (algorithm) {
150.     case (0):
151.         return ompi_coll_tuned_bcast_intra_dec_fixed( buf, count, dtype, root, comm, module );
152.     case (1):
153.         return ompi_coll_base_bcast_intra_basic_linear( buf, count, dtype, root, comm, module );
154.     case (2):
155.         return ompi_coll_base_bcast_intra_chain( buf, count, dtype, root, comm, module, segsize, faninout );
156.     case (3):
157.         return ompi_coll_base_bcast_intra_pipeline( buf, count, dtype, root, comm, module, segsize );
158.     case (4):
159.         return ompi_coll_base_bcast_intra_split_bintree( buf, count, dtype, root, comm, module, segsize );
160.     case (5):
161.         return ompi_coll_base_bcast_intra_bintree( buf, count, dtype, root, comm, module, segsize );
162.     case (6):
163.         return ompi_coll_base_bcast_intra_binomial( buf, count, dtype, root, comm, module, segsize );
164.     case (7):
165.         return ompi_coll_base_bcast_intra_knomial(buf, count, dtype, root, comm, module,
166.                                                   segsize, coll_tuned_bcast_knomial_radix);
167.     case (8):
168.         return ompi_coll_base_bcast_intra_scatter_allgather(buf, count, dtype, root, comm, module, segsize);
169.     case (9):
170.         return ompi_coll_base_bcast_intra_scatter_allgather_ring(buf, count, dtype, root, comm, module, segsize);
171.     } /* switch */
172.     OPAL_OUTPUT_VERBOSE((COLL_TUNED_TRACING_VERBOSE, ompi_coll_tuned_stream,
173.         "coll:tuned:bcast_intra_do_this attempt to select algorithm %d when only 0-%d is valid?",
174.         algorithm, ompi_coll_tuned_forced_max_algorithms[BCAST]));
175.     return (MPI_ERR_ARG);
176. }

31. /*
32.  * Some static helpers.
33.  */
34. static int pown( int fanout, int num )
35. {
36.     int j, p = 1;
37.     if( num < 0 ) return 0;
38.     if (1==num) return fanout;
39.     if (2==fanout) {
40.         return p<<num;
41.     }
42.     else {
43.         for( j = 0; j < num; j++ ) { p*= fanout; }
44.     }
45.     return p;
46. }
47. 
48. static int calculate_level( int fanout, int rank )
49. {
50.     int level, num;
51.     if( rank < 0 ) return -1;
52.     for( level = 0, num = 0; num <= rank; level++ ) {
53.         num += pown(fanout, level);
54.     }
55.     return level-1;
56. }
57. 
58. static int calculate_num_nodes_up_to_level( int fanout, int level )
59. {
60.     /* just use geometric progression formula for sum:
61.        a^0+a^1+...a^(n-1) = (a^n-1)/(a-1) */
62.     if (1 == fanout) {
63.         return level;
64.     }
65.     else {
66.         return ((pown(fanout,level) - 1)/(fanout - 1));
67.     }
68. }

73.  * An example for fanout = 2, comm_size = 7
74.  *
75.  *              0           <-- delta = 1 (fanout^0)
76.  *            /   \
77.  *           1     2        <-- delta = 2 (fanout^1)
78.  *          / \   / \
79.  *         3   5 4   6      <-- delta = 4 (fanout^2)
80.  */
81.

83. ompi_coll_base_topo_build_tree( int fanout,
84.                                  struct ompi_communicator_t* comm,

87.     int rank, size, schild, sparent, shiftedrank, i;

97.         return NULL;
98.     }
99.     if (fanout>MAXTREEFANOUT) {
100.         OPAL_OUTPUT((ompi_coll_base_framework.framework_output,"coll:base:topo_build_tree invalid fanout %d bigger than max %d", fanout, MAXTREEFANOUT));
101.         return NULL;
102.     }

105.      * Get size and rank of the process in this communicator

146.      */
147.     shiftedrank = rank - root;
148.     if( shiftedrank < 0 ) {
149.         shiftedrank += size;
150.     }
151. 
152.     /* calculate my level */
153.     level = calculate_level( fanout, shiftedrank );
154.     delta = pown( fanout, level );
155. 
156.     /* find my children */
157.     for( i = 0; i < fanout; i++ ) {
158.         schild = shiftedrank + delta * (i+1);
159.         if( schild < size ) {
160.             tree->tree_next[i] = (schild+root)%size;
161.             tree->tree_nextsize = tree->tree_nextsize + 1;
162.         } else {
163.             break;
164.         }
165.     }
166. 
167.     /* find my parent */
168.     slimit = calculate_num_nodes_up_to_level( fanout, level );
169.     sparent = shiftedrank;
170.     if( sparent < fanout ) {
171.         sparent = 0;
172.     } else {
173.         while( sparent >= slimit ) {
174.             sparent -= delta/fanout;
175.         }
176.     }
177.     tree->tree_prev = (sparent+root)%size;
178. 
179.     return tree;
180. }

182. /*
183.  * Constructs in-order binary tree which can be used for non-commutative reduce
184.  * operations.
185.  * Root of this tree is always rank (size-1) and fanout is 2.
186.  * Here are some of the examples of this tree:
187.  * size == 2     size == 3     size == 4                size == 9
188.  *      1             2             3                        8
189.  *     /             / \          /   \                    /   \
190.  *    0             1  0         2     1                  7     3
191.  *                                    /                 /  \   / \
192.  *                                   0                 6    5 2   1
193.  *                                                         /     /
194.  *                                                        4     0
195.  */
196. ompi_coll_tree_t*
197. ompi_coll_base_topo_build_in_order_bintree( struct ompi_communicator_t* comm )
198. {
199.     int rank, size, myrank, rightsize, delta, parent, lchild, rchild;
200.     ompi_coll_tree_t* tree;
201. 
202.     /*
203.      * Get size and rank of the process in this communicator
204.      */
205.     size = ompi_comm_size(comm);
206.     rank = ompi_comm_rank(comm);
207. 
208.     tree = (ompi_coll_tree_t*)malloc(COLL_TREE_SIZE(MAXTREEFANOUT));
209.     if (!tree) {
210.         OPAL_OUTPUT((ompi_coll_base_framework.framework_output,
211.                      "coll:base:topo_build_tree PANIC::out of memory"));
212.         return NULL;
213.     }
214. 
215.     tree->tree_root     = MPI_UNDEFINED;
216.     tree->tree_nextsize = MPI_UNDEFINED;
217. 
218.     /*
219.      * Initialize tree
220.      */
221.     tree->tree_fanout   = 2;
222.     tree->tree_bmtree   = 0;
223.     tree->tree_root     = size - 1;
224.     tree->tree_prev     = -1;
225.     tree->tree_nextsize = 0;
226.     tree->tree_next[0]  = -1;
227.     tree->tree_next[1]  = -1;
228.     OPAL_OUTPUT((ompi_coll_base_framework.framework_output,
229.                  "coll:base:topo_build_in_order_tree Building fo %d rt %d",
230.                  tree->tree_fanout, tree->tree_root));
231. 
232.     /*
233.      * Build the tree
234.      */
235.     myrank = rank;
236.     parent = size - 1;
237.     delta = 0;
238. 
239.     while ( 1 ) {
240.         /* Compute the size of the right subtree */
241.         rightsize = size >> 1;
242. 
243.         /* Determine the left and right child of this parent  */
244.         lchild = -1;
245.         rchild = -1;
246.         if (size - 1 > 0) {
247.             lchild = parent - 1;
248.             if (lchild > 0) {
249.                 rchild = rightsize - 1;
250.             }
251.         }
252. 
253.         /* The following cases are possible: myrank can be
254.            - a parent,
255.            - belong to the left subtree, or
256.            - belong to the right subtee
257.            Each of the cases need to be handled differently.
258.         */
259. 
260.         if (myrank == parent) {
261.             /* I am the parent:
262.                - compute real ranks of my children, and exit the loop. */
263.             if (lchild >= 0) tree->tree_next[0] = lchild + delta;
264.             if (rchild >= 0) tree->tree_next[1] = rchild + delta;
265.             break;
266.         }
267.         if (myrank > rchild) {
268.             /* I belong to the left subtree:
269.                - If I am the left child, compute real rank of my parent
270.                - Iterate down through tree:
271.                compute new size, shift ranks down, and update delta.
272.             */
273.             if (myrank == lchild) {
274.                 tree->tree_prev = parent + delta;
275.             }
276.             size = size - rightsize - 1;
277.             delta = delta + rightsize;
278.             myrank = myrank - rightsize;
279.             parent = size - 1;
280. 
281.         } else {
282.             /* I belong to the right subtree:
283.                - If I am the right child, compute real rank of my parent
284.                - Iterate down through tree:
285.                compute new size and parent,
286.                but the delta and rank do not need to change.
287.             */
288.             if (myrank == rchild) {
289.                 tree->tree_prev = parent + delta;
290.             }
291.             size = rightsize;
292.             parent = rchild;
293.         }
294.     }
295. 
296.     if (tree->tree_next[0] >= 0) { tree->tree_nextsize = 1; }
297.     if (tree->tree_next[1] >= 0) { tree->tree_nextsize += 1; }
298. 
299.     return tree;
300. }
301. 
302. int ompi_coll_base_topo_destroy_tree( ompi_coll_tree_t** tree )
303. {
304.     ompi_coll_tree_t *ptr;
305. 
306.     if ((!tree)||(!*tree)) {
307.         return OMPI_SUCCESS;
308.     }
309. 
310.     ptr = *tree;
311. 
312.     free (ptr);
313.     *tree = NULL;   /* mark tree as gone */
314. 
315.     return OMPI_SUCCESS;
316. }
317.

479. ompi_coll_base_topo_build_kmtree(struct ompi_communicator_t* comm,
480.                                  int root, int radix)
481. {
482.     OPAL_OUTPUT((ompi_coll_base_framework.framework_output,
483.                  "coll:base:topo:build_kmtree root %d, radix %d", root, radix));
484.     int comm_size = ompi_comm_size(comm);
485.     int rank = ompi_comm_rank(comm);
486. 
487.     /* nchilds <= (radix - 1) * \ceil(\log_{radix}(comm_size)) */
488.     int log_radix = 0;
489.     for (int i = 1; i < comm_size; i *= radix)
490.         log_radix++;
491.     int nchilds_max = (radix - 1) * log_radix;
492. 
493.     int vrank = (rank - root + comm_size) % comm_size;
494.     ompi_coll_tree_t *kmtree = malloc(COLL_TREE_SIZE(nchilds_max));
495.     if (NULL == kmtree) {
496.         OPAL_OUTPUT((ompi_coll_base_framework.framework_output,
497.                      "coll:base:topo:build_kmtree PANIC out of memory"));
498.         return NULL;
499.     }
500. 
501.     kmtree->tree_bmtree = 0;
502.     kmtree->tree_root = root;
503.     kmtree->tree_prev = MPI_PROC_NULL;
504.     kmtree->tree_nextsize = 0;
505. 
506.     /* Setup parent */
507.     int mask = 0x1;
508.     while (mask < comm_size) {
509.         if (vrank % (radix * mask)) {
510.             kmtree->tree_prev = vrank / (radix * mask) * (radix * mask);
511.             kmtree->tree_prev = (kmtree->tree_prev + root) % comm_size;
512.             break;
513.         }
514.         mask *= radix;
515.     }
516. 
517.     /* Setup childs */
518.     mask /= radix;
519.     int nchilds = 0;
520.     while (mask > 0) {
521.         for (int r = 1; r < radix; r++) {
522.             int child = vrank + mask * r;
523.             if (child < comm_size) {
524.                 child = (child + root) % comm_size;
525.                 kmtree->tree_next[nchilds] = child;
526.                 nchilds++;
527.             }
528.         }
529.         mask /= radix;
530.     }
531.     kmtree->tree_nextsize = nchilds;
532.     return kmtree;
533. }

### 💬 Copilot

我觉得已经有一个很强的方向了：**当前 receiver 只在本地 `ep_create` 时注册 inbound lane，但 bcast 的父子边很多是单向的，接收方可能先 `irecv`，却从未先创建到 parent 的本地 EP**。这样 sender 已经往它的 lane 里写了，receiver 仍然完全不 poll 这条 lane。先把这个方向用日志实锤。

226. uct_obmm_iface_progress_lane(uct_obmm_iface_t *iface, uct_obmm_rx_lane_t *lane)
227. {
228.     uct_obmm_fifo_element_t *elem;
229.     uint32_t                 head;
230. 
231.     if (!lane->active) {
232.         return 0;
233.     }
234. 
235.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
236.     if (lane->ctl->sender_generation != lane->sender_generation) {
237.         return 0;
238.     }
239. 
240.     head = lane->ctl->head;
241.     if (head == lane->rx_index) {
242.         return 0;
243.     }
244. 
245.     elem = uct_obmm_lane_elem(lane->elems, lane->rx_index, iface->fifo_mask,
246.                               iface->fifo_elem_size);
247.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
248. 
249.     if (elem->generation == iface->generation) {
250.         if (elem->flags & UCT_OBMM_MAILBOX_ELEM_FLAG_BCOPY) {
251.             void *desc = uct_obmm_lane_desc(lane->descs, lane->rx_index,
252.                                             iface->fifo_mask,
253.                                             iface->bcopy_seg_size);
254.             uct_iface_invoke_am(&iface->super, elem->am_id,
255.                                 desc, elem->length, 0);
256.         } else {
257.             uct_iface_invoke_am(&iface->super, elem->am_id,
258.                                 &elem->header, elem->length, 0);
259.         }
260.     }
261. 
262.     lane->rx_index++;
263.     uct_obmm_bus_full_fence();
264.     if (lane->ctl->sender_generation != lane->sender_generation) {
265.         return 1;
266.     }
267.     lane->ctl->tail = lane->rx_index;
268.     ucs_memory_bus_store_fence();
269.     if (lane->ctl->sender_generation != lane->sender_generation) {
270.         return 1;
271.     }
272.     lane->ctl->tail_generation = lane->sender_generation;
273.     return 1;
274. }
275. 
276. 
277. static unsigned uct_obmm_iface_progress(uct_iface_h tl_iface)
278. {
279.     uct_obmm_iface_t *iface = ucs_derived_of(tl_iface, uct_obmm_iface_t);
280.     unsigned          polled = 0;
281.     unsigned          total_lanes = UCT_OBMM_MAILBOX_BANK_COUNT *
282.                                     UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT;
283.     unsigned          scanned;
284. 
285.     for (scanned = 0; (scanned < total_lanes) && (polled < iface->fifo_max_poll);
286.          ++scanned) {
287.         unsigned           idx  = (iface->rx_lane_rr + scanned) % total_lanes;
288.         unsigned           bank = idx / UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT;
289.         unsigned           slot = idx % UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT;
290. 
291.         polled += uct_obmm_iface_progress_lane(iface,
292.                                                &iface->rx_lanes[bank][slot]);
293.     }
294. 
295.     iface->rx_lane_rr = (iface->rx_lane_rr + 1) % total_lanes;
296. 
297.     ucs_arbiter_dispatch(&iface->arbiter, 1, uct_obmm_ep_process_pending,
298.                          &polled);
299. 
300.     return polled;
301. }
302. 
303. 
304. static ucs_status_t uct_obmm_iface_fence(uct_iface_h tl_iface, unsigned flags)
305. {
306.     (void)flags;
307.     uct_obmm_bus_full_fence();
308.     UCT_TL_IFACE_STAT_FENCE(ucs_derived_of(tl_iface, uct_base_iface_t));
309.     return UCS_OK;
310. }
311. 
312. 
313. static ucs_status_t uct_obmm_ep_fence(uct_ep_h tl_ep, unsigned flags)
314. {
315.     (void)flags;
316.     uct_obmm_bus_full_fence();
317.     UCT_TL_EP_STAT_FENCE(ucs_derived_of(tl_ep, uct_base_ep_t));
318.     return UCS_OK;
319. }
320. 
321. 
322. static UCS_CLASS_INIT_FUNC(uct_obmm_iface_t, uct_md_h tl_md, uct_worker_h worker,
323.                            const uct_iface_params_t *params,
324.                            const uct_iface_config_t *tl_config)
325. {
326.     uct_obmm_iface_config_t *config = ucs_derived_of(tl_config,
327.                                                      uct_obmm_iface_config_t);
328.     uct_obmm_md_t           *md     = ucs_derived_of(tl_md, uct_obmm_md_t);
329.     uct_obmm_region_t       *region;
330.     size_t                   stride;
331.     size_t                   required;
332.     ucs_status_t             status;
333.     unsigned                 bank;
334.     unsigned                 slot;
335. 
336.     if (config->fifo_size == 0) {
337.         ucs_error("obmm: FIFO_SIZE must be > 0");
338.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
339.     }
340.     if (!ucs_is_pow2(config->fifo_size)) {
341.         ucs_error("obmm: FIFO_SIZE (%u) must be a power of 2",
342.                   config->fifo_size);
343.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
344.     }
345.     if (config->fifo_elem_size <= sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_element_t)) {
346.         ucs_error("obmm: FIFO_ELEM_SIZE (%u) must be > %zu",
347.                   config->fifo_elem_size, sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_element_t));
348.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
349.     }
350.     if ((config->fifo_elem_size - sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_element_t)) >
351.         UINT16_MAX) {
352.         ucs_error("obmm: FIFO_ELEM_SIZE (%u) too large; payload area must fit "
353.                   "in uint16 (max %zu)",
354.                   config->fifo_elem_size,
355.                   (size_t)UINT16_MAX + sizeof(uct_obmm_fifo_element_t));
356.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
357.     }
358.     if (config->bcopy_seg_size == 0) {
359.         ucs_error("obmm: BCOPY_SEG_SIZE must be > 0");
360.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
361.     }
362.     if (config->bcopy_seg_size > UINT16_MAX) {
363.         ucs_error("obmm: BCOPY_SEG_SIZE (%u) too large; max_bcopy must fit "
364.                   "in uint16 (max %u)",
365.                   config->bcopy_seg_size, (unsigned)UINT16_MAX);
366.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
367.     }
368. 
369.     region = uct_obmm_md_export_region(md);
370.     if (region == NULL) {
371.         ucs_error("obmm: cannot create iface; this MD has no local export "
372.                   "region");
373.         return UCS_ERR_NO_DEVICE;
374.     }
375. 
376.     stride = uct_obmm_slot_stride(config->fifo_size, config->fifo_elem_size,
377.                                   config->bcopy_seg_size);
378.     if (stride > UINT32_MAX) {
379.         ucs_error("obmm: slot stride %zu exceeds uint32_t (fifo_size=%u "
380.                   "elem=%u seg=%u); reduce one of the geometry knobs",
381.                   stride, config->fifo_size, config->fifo_elem_size,
382.                   config->bcopy_seg_size);
383.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
384.     }
385.     required = uct_obmm_pool_required_size(UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT,
386.                                            (uint32_t)stride);
387.     if (required > region->length) {
388.         ucs_error("obmm: mailbox geometry does not fit in region: "
389.                   "fifo_size=%u elem_size=%u seg_size=%u stride=%zu "
390.                   "slot_count=%u required=%zu region=%zu",
391.                   config->fifo_size, config->fifo_elem_size,
392.                   config->bcopy_seg_size, stride,
393.                   UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT, required, region->length);
394.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
395.     }
396. 
397.     UCT_CHECK_PARAM(params->field_mask & UCT_IFACE_PARAM_FIELD_OPEN_MODE,
398.                     "UCT_IFACE_PARAM_FIELD_OPEN_MODE is not defined");
399.     if (!(params->open_mode & UCT_IFACE_OPEN_MODE_DEVICE)) {
400.         ucs_error("only UCT_IFACE_OPEN_MODE_DEVICE is supported");
401.         return UCS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED;
402.     }
403. 
404.     UCS_CLASS_CALL_SUPER_INIT(uct_base_iface_t, &uct_obmm_iface_ops,
405.                               &uct_obmm_iface_internal_ops, tl_md, worker,
406.                               params, &config->super.super
407.                               UCS_STATS_ARG((params->field_mask &
408.                                              UCT_IFACE_PARAM_FIELD_STATS_ROOT) ?
409.                                             params->stats_root : NULL)
410.                               UCS_STATS_ARG(params->mode.device.dev_name));
411. 
412.     self->region           = region;
413.     self->config.bandwidth = config->super.bandwidth;
414.     self->fifo_size        = config->fifo_size;
415.     self->fifo_mask        = config->fifo_size - 1u;
416.     self->fifo_elem_size   = config->fifo_elem_size;
417.     self->bcopy_seg_size   = config->bcopy_seg_size;
418.     self->fifo_max_poll    = (config->fifo_max_poll == 0) ? 1 :
419.                              config->fifo_max_poll;
420.     self->rx_lane_rr       = 0;
421.     memset(self->rx_lanes, 0, sizeof(self->rx_lanes));
422. 
423.     status = uct_obmm_pool_attach(region->base, region->length,
424.                                   UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT,
425.                                   (uint32_t)stride, &self->pool);
426.     if (status != UCS_OK) {
427.         ucs_error("obmm: pool attach failed: %s", ucs_status_string(status));
428.         return status;
429.     }
430. 
431.     status = uct_obmm_pool_alloc_slot(&self->pool, &self->slot_index,
432.                                       &self->slot, &self->generation);
433.     if (status != UCS_OK) {
434.         ucs_error("obmm: failed to allocate mailbox slot: %s",
435.                   ucs_status_string(status));
436.         return status;
437.     }
438. 
439.     for (bank = 0; bank < UCT_OBMM_MAILBOX_BANK_COUNT; ++bank) {
440.         for (slot = 0; slot < UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT; ++slot) {
441.             void *lane = uct_obmm_slot_lane(self->slot, bank, slot,
442.                                             self->fifo_size,
443.                                             self->fifo_elem_size,
444.                                             self->bcopy_seg_size);
445.             uct_obmm_lane_ctl(lane)->sender_generation = self->generation;
446.         }
447.     }
448.     ucs_memory_bus_store_fence();
449. 
450.     ucs_arbiter_init(&self->arbiter);
451. 
452.     ucs_debug("obmm: iface %p attached to region %p slot=%u gen=%u "
453.               "fifo_size=%u elem_size=%u seg_size=%u stride=%zu",
454.               self, region->base, self->slot_index, self->generation,
455.               self->fifo_size, self->fifo_elem_size, self->bcopy_seg_size,
456.               stride);
457.     return UCS_OK;
458. }
459. 
460. 
461. static UCS_CLASS_CLEANUP_FUNC(uct_obmm_iface_t)
462. {
463.     uct_base_iface_progress_disable(&self->super.super,
464.                                     UCT_PROGRESS_SEND | UCT_PROGRESS_RECV);
465.     if ((self->pool.hdr != NULL) &&
466.         uct_obmm_pool_free_slot(&self->pool, self->slot_index)) {
467.         uct_obmm_pool_reset(&self->pool);
468.     }
469.     ucs_arbiter_cleanup(&self->arbiter);
470. }

35. /* In-region pool header. Lives at offset 0 of the local export region. All
36.  * fields are written via non-cacheable mappings: state transitions must be

38.  * host) see the geometry before the READY transition. During cleanup, INITING
39.  * is only a transient coordination state; once reset completes, the shared
40.  * region is fully zero again. */

43.     uint32_t state;             /* UCT_OBMM_POOL_STATE_xx, atomic */
44.     uint32_t slot_count;
45.     uint32_t slot_size;
46.     uint64_t slot_array_offset; /* offset (from region base) of slot 0 */
47.     uint32_t bitmap_words;      /* number of u64 words in alloc bitmap */
48.     uint32_t initializer_pid;   /* pid that owned the INITING transition */
49.     uint64_t initializer_starttime;
50.     /* followed by:
51.      *   uint64_t alloc_bitmap[bitmap_words];
52.      *   uct_obmm_slot_meta_t slot_meta[slot_count];

54. } uct_obmm_pool_hdr_t;
55.

62.                                   scavenge, and when readers must discard
63.                                   in-flight stale elements */

65.     uint32_t reserved;

<sub>⏱️ 2713m 23s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

**已通过。** 根因已经定位清楚：sender-owned mailbox 版的接收路径原先只依赖本地 `ep_create` 时注册 inbound lane，`osu_bcast` 这类 **单向 parent→child** 边会让 receiver 先收、却没先建回 parent 的本地 EP，结果 sender 已经把数据写进 lane，receiver 仍然完全不 poll 它。

我已经把 `iface_progress()` 改成会**动态发现并直接 progress 未注册的 inbound lane**，不再要求这条接收边先经过本地 `ep_create`。之前加的告警正是实锤了这个问题，修完后你的失败场景已经恢复。

46.                                            unsigned max_poll)
47. {

49.     uct_obmm_pool_t        pool;

54.     void                  *slot_base;
55.     void                  *lane_base;
56.     unsigned               i;
57.     unsigned               slot;
58.     unsigned               bank;
59.     unsigned               completions = 0;
60.     uint32_t               head;
61.     uint32_t               tail;
62. 
63.     for (i = 0; i < md->num_regions; ++i) {
64.         region = &md->regions[i];
65.         bank   = (i == (unsigned)md->export_idx) ? UCT_OBMM_MAILBOX_BANK_LOCAL :
66.                                                    UCT_OBMM_MAILBOX_BANK_REMOTE;
67. 
68.         status = uct_obmm_pool_open(region->base, region->length, &pool);
69.         if (status != UCS_OK) {
70.             continue;
71.         }
72. 
73.         for (slot = 0; (slot < pool.slot_count) &&
74.                        (slot < UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT); ++slot) {
75.             if ((bank == UCT_OBMM_MAILBOX_BANK_LOCAL) &&
76.                 (slot == iface->slot_index)) {
77.                 continue;
78.             }
79.             if (iface->rx_lanes[bank][slot].active) {
80.                 continue;
81.             }
82.             if (pool.meta[slot].state != UCT_OBMM_SLOT_STATE_IN_USE) {
83.                 continue;
84.             }
85. 
86.             slot_base = uct_obmm_pool_slot_ptr(&pool, slot);
87.             lane_base = uct_obmm_slot_lane(slot_base, bank, iface->slot_index,
88.                                            iface->fifo_size,
89.                                            iface->fifo_elem_size,
90.                                            iface->bcopy_seg_size);
91.             ctl = uct_obmm_lane_ctl(lane_base);
92. 
93.             ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
94.             if (ctl->sender_generation != pool.meta[slot].generation) {
95.                 continue;
96.             }
97. 
98.             head = ctl->head;
99.             tail = ctl->tail;
100.             if (head == tail) {
101.                 continue;
102.             }
103. 
104.             memset(&lane, 0, sizeof(lane));
105.             lane.ctl               = ctl;
106.             lane.elems             = uct_obmm_lane_elems(lane_base);
107.             lane.descs             = uct_obmm_lane_descs(lane_base,
108.                                                          iface->fifo_size,
109.                                                          iface->fifo_elem_size);
110.             lane.sender_generation = pool.meta[slot].generation;
111.             lane.rx_index          = (ctl->tail_generation == lane.sender_generation) ?
112.                                      tail : 0;
113.             lane.active            = 1;
114. 
115.             iface->unregistered_lane_hits++;
116.             if ((iface->unregistered_lane_hits <= 8) ||
117.                 ucs_is_pow2(iface->unregistered_lane_hits)) {

121.                          " exporter_dcna=0x%lx exporter_deid=0x%lx:0x%lx",
122.                          iface, iface->slot_index, uct_obmm_mailbox_bank_name(bank),
123.                          slot, pool.meta[slot].generation, head, tail,
124.                          region->info.memid,
125.                          (unsigned long)region->info.exporter_dcna,
126.                          (unsigned long)region->info.exporter_deid.hi,
127.                          (unsigned long)region->info.exporter_deid.lo);
128.             }
129. 
130.             completions += uct_obmm_iface_progress_lane(iface, &lane);
131.             if (completions >= max_poll) {
132.                 return completions;
133.             }
134.         }
135.     }

1. ---
2. name: obmm-api-and-env
3. description: >
4.   Authoritative facts about the libobmm API and the target test environment
5.   for the UCT obmm transport. Use whenever writing or reviewing obmm
6.   transport code that touches memory setup, addressing, or peer reachability,

9. ---
10. 
11. # OBMM API and Test Environment
12. 
13. This skill is the **single source of truth** for what the agent may assume
14. about libobmm and the deployment topology. If something is not stated here,
15. the agent must ASK the user instead of inventing it.
16. 
17. ## libobmm public API (from `obmm/src/libobmm/libobmm.h`)
18. 
19. ```c
20. mem_id obmm_export(const size_t length[OBMM_MAX_LOCAL_NUMA_NODES],
21.                    unsigned long flags, struct obmm_mem_desc *desc);
22. int    obmm_unexport(mem_id id, unsigned long flags);
23. 
24. int    obmm_preimport(struct obmm_preimport_info *preimport_info,
25.                       unsigned long flags);
26. int    obmm_unpreimport(const struct obmm_preimport_info *preimport_info,
27.                         unsigned long flags);
28. 
29. mem_id obmm_export_useraddr(int pid, void *va, size_t length,
30.                             unsigned long flags, struct obmm_mem_desc *desc);
31. 
32. mem_id obmm_import(const struct obmm_mem_desc *desc, unsigned long flags,
33.                    int base_dist, int *numa);
34. int    obmm_unimport(mem_id id, unsigned long flags);
35. 
36. int    obmm_set_ownership(int fd, void *start, void *end, int prot);
37. 
38. int    obmm_query_memid_by_pa(unsigned long pa, mem_id *id,
39.                               unsigned long *offset);
40. int    obmm_query_pa_by_memid(mem_id id, unsigned long offset,
41.                               unsigned long *pa);
42. ```
43. 
44. Key data structures:
45. 
46. - `struct obmm_mem_desc { addr; length; seid[16]; deid[16]; tokenid; scna;
47.   dcna; priv_len; priv[]; }` — the descriptor returned by export and
48.   consumed by import.
49. - `struct obmm_preimport_info { pa; length; base_dist; numa_id; seid; deid;
50.   scna; dcna; priv_len; priv[]; }`
51. - `mem_id` is `uint64_t`; `OBMM_INVALID_MEMID == 0`.
52. 
53. ## Test environment — IMMUTABLE FACTS
54. 
55. These were stated by the project owner. The transport implementation MUST
56. be designed against exactly this topology:
57. 
58. 1. **Two nodes**, node 0 and node 1.
59. 2. Each node has **already exported a 128 MiB memory region** to the other
60.    side, before any UCX / MPI process starts.
61. 3. Each node has **already imported** the peer's 128 MiB region.
62. 4. The export / import / preimport / unimport / unexport lifecycle is
63.    handled outside the UCX transport — **the obmm UCT transport must NOT
64.    call** `obmm_export`, `obmm_unexport`, `obmm_import`, `obmm_unimport`,
65.    `obmm_preimport`, or `obmm_unpreimport` at runtime.
66. 5. Inside UCT, access to the local and peer regions is done with
67.    **`open("/dev/obmm_shmdev${memid}", O_RDWR | O_SYNC)` + `mmap`**
68.    (NC mapping; see "Locked-in design decisions" below).
69.    The local export memid and peer import memid are discovered by
70.    scanning `/sys/devices/obmm/obmm_shmdev*/` and inspecting whether
71.    each contains an `export_info/` or `import_info/` subdirectory.
72. 6. **No hardware is available** in the development environment. Do not
73.    attempt to run `mpirun`, real `ucx_perftest`, or any test that requires
74.    the obmm device. Validation is limited to:
75.      - `make` / `make install` succeeding,
76.      - `ucx_info -d` listing the obmm component, md, and tl,
77.      - `ucx_info -c` showing OBMM_* env vars,
78.      - static review against this skill and `uct-transport-patterns`.
79. 
80. ## Locked-in design decisions (do not change without re-asking)
81. 
82. These were explicitly decided with the project owner during the v1
83. am_short plan review. They override any conflicting suggestion the
84. agent may otherwise default to (notably the mm transport's behavior).
85. 
86. 1. **NC mapping for the data path.** Open shmdev with
87.    `O_RDWR | O_SYNC` and mmap with `MAP_SHARED`. This puts the FIFO
88.    region into a non-cacheable mapping, which:
89.      - bypasses the OBMM cacheable consistency model (writers and
90.        readers from any host coexist),
91.      - removes the need to ever call `obmm_set_ownership` from the
92.        transport.
93. 2. **Cross-node atomic RMW on NC is guaranteed.** The project owner
94.    has stated that the obmm fabric supports atomic FAA / CAS on NC
95.    mappings across nodes. The transport may therefore use mm-style
96.    multi-producer FIFOs (FAA on a shared head) without redesigning
97.    for SPSC.
98. 3. **UCT owns the in-region layout.** The 128 MiB exported region is
99.    zero-filled at platform export time. The transport places its own
100.    header (state / version / slot bitmap / slot_meta / fixed-size
101.    slots) at the start of the region. A two-phase init is used:
102.    `state` transitions UNINIT→INITING (CAS) → fill geometry → bus
103.    fence → store READY. Losers spin on READY then bus-load fence.
104.    Single-magic init is racy (geometry not yet visible) and must
105.    not be used.
106. 4. **Topology**: per node there is exactly 1 export region and 1
107.    import region (the peer node's export). Discovered via
108.    `/sys/devices/obmm/obmm_shmdev*/{export_info,import_info}`.
109.    Reachability and mapping table keys are
110.    `(exporter_dcna, exporter_deid, memid)` from sysfs — NOT memid
111.    alone (collision-prone).
112. 5. **Self-loopback inside one node** is supported: same-node processes
113.    communicate by both mapping the local export region (the imported
114.    "peer region" entry simply will not exist in the single-node case,
115.    or will equal the local one — handle both).
116. 6. **Slot lifecycle uses generation tokens.** Each slot has
117.    `(owner_pid, owner_starttime, generation, state)` in slot_meta.
118.    `iface_addr` and every FIFO elem carry `generation`; receiver
119.    discards mismatches. Destroy = mark DEAD → bus fence → bump
120.    generation → clear bit. Crash recovery: scan bitmap, validate
121.    `/proc/<pid>/stat starttime`, reclaim. PID alone is insufficient
122.    (PID reuse).
123. 7. **Cross-node memory ordering uses BUS-domain fences.**
124.    `ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()` / `ucs_memory_bus_load_fence()`
125.    (sfence/lfence on x86, `dmb oshst`/`dmb oshld` on arm64). The
126.    CPU-domain fences mm uses (`ucs_memory_cpu_*_fence`) are
127.    inner-shareable only and DO NOT cover cross-host NC visibility.
128. 
129. ## OBMM consistency model — why NC matters
130. 
131. From `obmm/doc/libobmm.md` and `obmm/doc/obmm_set_ownership.md`:
132. 
133. - For **cacheable** OBMM mappings, at any moment all hosts touching a
134.   region must be in one of two states:
135.     a) all hosts are PROT_READ or PROT_NONE, OR
136.     b) exactly one host has writers; all other hosts must be PROT_NONE.
137. - A receive-FIFO model (writer on the sending host, reader on the
138.   receiving host, on the SAME region) violates this: it would require
139.   one host to write while another host reads simultaneously.
140. - Therefore the obmm transport CANNOT use cacheable mappings for the
141.   FIFO region without expensive ownership flips per message.
142. - NC (O_SYNC) mappings are exempt: per the doc, "用户无需关心一致性
143.   模型，所有的用户均具备读写权限". This is why decision (1) above
144.   is mandatory, not optional.
145. 
146. ## Implications for the transport design
147. 
148. These follow from the facts above and should be treated as defaults; ask
149. the user before deviating:
150. 
151. - **Memory registration** (`uct_md_ops_t::mem_reg` / `mem_dereg`) does not
152.   need to call libobmm. The current placeholders
153.   (`uct_md_dummy_mem_reg` / `uct_md_dummy_mem_dereg`) are appropriate
154.   because the buffers used by am_short live inside the pre-imported
155.   peer region, not in arbitrary user buffers.
156. - **Address exchange** for am_short: `iface_addr` MUST carry
157.   `(exporter_dcna, exporter_deid, memid, slot_index, generation)`
158.   so the peer can (a) look up the already-mmap'd region in our MD's
159.   mapping table by exporter identity + memid, and (b) detect stale
160.   slot reuse via generation. Memid alone is unsafe and was rejected
161.   in plan-review. The current `uct_obmm_iface_addr_t = uint64_t`
162.   must be widened.
163. - **Reachability**: `iface_is_reachable_v2` matches on
164.   `(exporter_dcna, exporter_deid, memid)` against the MD's known
165.   exports + imports. Drop the `uct_sm_iface_is_reachable` (same-host)
166.   call — obmm is cross-node by construction.
167. - **Progress wiring**: `iface_progress_enable/disable` MUST call
168.   `uct_base_iface_progress_enable_cb(...)` /
169.   `uct_base_iface_progress_disable(...)`. The current
170.   `ucs_empty_function` stubs prevent UCP from ever polling the iface.
171. - **EP_CHECK**: do NOT advertise `UCT_IFACE_FLAG_EP_CHECK` in v1.
172.   The current skeleton sets it but `ep_check` only returns OK; no
173.   cross-node liveness check exists. PID-in-addr is not enough.
174. - **Ownership / `obmm_set_ownership`**: only call this if the UCT layer
175.   needs to flip read/write permission on a sub-range of the imported
176.   region; for a first am_short pass with a producer/consumer FIFO this
177.   is typically NOT needed. Ask before adding it.
178. 
179. ## What to ASK the user before writing code
180. 
181. Do not invent answers to any of these. Use the `ask_user` tool:
182. 
183. 1. Whether multiple obmm ifaces per process are expected, or strictly
184.    one peer per local iface (current assumption: 1 iface per process,
185.    pool holds many ifaces from many processes).
186. 2. What the wire `am_id` / header / payload alignment requirements are
187.    on the obmm hardware (e.g. 64 B cache line? 256 B?). Default plan
188.    aligns elements to 64 B; confirm before tuning.
189. 3. ~~Whether NC writes from one host become visible to remote loads
190.    without an explicit fabric-level barrier other than CPU
191.    `dmb`/`mfence`.~~ **RESOLVED in plan-review**: must use bus-domain
192.    fences (`ucs_memory_bus_*_fence`), not CPU-domain. CPU fences are
193.    inner-shareable only and don't reach cross-host NC.
194. 
195. ## Forbidden assumptions
196. 
197. - Do NOT assume libobmm performs its own synchronization — am_short
198.   ordering must be enforced by the transport (release / acquire fences,
199.   same as mm).
200. - Do NOT use cacheable mappings on the FIFO region. NC (`O_SYNC`)
201.   is mandatory; see "Locked-in design decisions".
202. - Do NOT call any `obmm_*` runtime API in the UCT transport unless this
203.   document is updated to allow it. In particular do NOT call
204.   `obmm_set_ownership` — its semantics conflict with the FIFO usage
205.   pattern.
206. - Do NOT use `ucs_memory_cpu_*_fence()` on the obmm data path. They
207.   are inner-shareable / compiler-only and do not cover cross-host NC
208.   visibility. Use `ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()` /
209.   `ucs_memory_bus_load_fence()` (sfence/lfence on x86,
210.   `dmb oshst`/`dmb oshld` on arm64). The mm transport gets away with
211.   CPU fences only because mm peers share an inner-shareable cache
212.   domain; obmm peers do not.
213. 
214. ## Why cacheable + manual cache management was rejected
215. 
216. Asked and answered during plan-review. Do not re-litigate without new
217. information about the obmm fabric.
218. 
219. 1. **OBMM cacheable consistency is enforced at the page-table level**,
220.    not at the cache level. `obmm/doc/libobmm.md:196-211` and
221.    `obmm/doc/obmm_set_ownership.md` require that at any moment either
222.    all hosts touching a region are PROT_READ/PROT_NONE, or exactly
223.    one host has writers and all other hosts are PROT_NONE. Even a
224.    correctly `clflush`-ed write from host A is not legal to read on
225.    host B until ownership is flipped via the `obmm_set_ownership()`
226.    syscall. That is one syscall per message — incompatible with
227.    `am_short` latency goals.
228. 2. **arm64 user-space lacks `dc ivac`** (invalidate by VA to PoC, EL0
229.    typically only exposes `dc civac` = clean+invalidate). A reader-side
230.    "discard cache, then load" sequence would have to clean+invalidate
231.    on every poll, doubling the writer-side cost.
232. 3. **UCX has no precedent** for cross-host cacheable shared memory with
233.    manual coherence on a hot data path. `ucs_arch_clear_cache` exists
234.    (x86: `mfence; clflush; mfence` per line; arm64: `dc cvau` +
235.    `ic ivau`) but is used only for instruction-cache coherence
236.    (JIT / code patching), never for transport data. All cross-host
237.    UCX transports either use a NIC (NIC handles coherence) or rely
238.    on a HW-coherent fabric. Inventing a new pattern here would carry
239.    risk far above what NC mapping costs.
240. 4. **Bulk-flip ownership** (writer holds write, batches N messages,
241.    flips, reader batches N reads) is a possible future path for
242.    `put/get` bulk transfers but trades latency for throughput and
243.    defeats AM short's purpose. Out of scope for v1.
244. 
245. NC (`O_SYNC`) avoids all four issues at the cost of uncached load/store
246. performance, which the project owner has accepted.
247.
````
