1. ---
2. name: uct-transport-patterns
3. description: >
4.   UCX UCT transport-layer development patterns. Use when implementing or
5.   modifying any UCT transport (md / iface / ep) — especially the obmm
6.   transport — to know which existing transports to mimic and which UCX
7.   framework macros / hooks must be wired up correctly.
8. ---
9. 
10. # UCT Transport Patterns
11. 
12. UCX UCT is a heavily macro- and hook-table-driven framework. New transports
13. should be implemented by **mirroring an existing reference transport**, not by
14. inventing structure. This skill tells the agent which references to read and
15. which framework contracts must be honored.
16. 
17. ## Reference transports (in this repo)
18. 
19. Read these before writing any obmm transport code:
20. 
21. - `ucx/src/uct/sm/mm/base/mm_md.{c,h}`     — shared-memory MD base
22. - `ucx/src/uct/sm/mm/base/mm_iface.{c,h}`  — FIFO + AM short reception loop
23. - `ucx/src/uct/sm/mm/base/mm_ep.{c,h}`     — `uct_mm_ep_am_short` reference
24. - `ucx/src/uct/sm/mm/posix/mm_posix.c`     — concrete mm provider
25. - `ucx/src/uct/sm/mm/sysv/mm_sysv.c`       — concrete mm provider
26. - `ucx/src/uct/sm/self/`                   — minimal single-process transport
27. - `ucx/src/uct/sm/base/sm_iface.{c,h}`     — `uct_sm_iface_t` superclass used
28.                                               by both mm and obmm
29. - `ucx/src/uct/base/uct_iface.h`           — `uct_iface_ops_t`,
30.                                               `UCT_TL_DEFINE_ENTRY`,
31.                                               `UCT_SINGLE_TL_INIT`
32. - `ucx/src/uct/api/uct.h`                  — public ep / iface signatures
33. 
34. The obmm skeleton at `ucx/src/uct/obmm/base/{obmm_md,obmm_iface,obmm_ep}.{c,h}`
35. already follows the mm layout; new code must keep that layering.
36. 
37. ## Framework contracts that must NOT be broken
38. 
39. When editing UCT transport code, every one of these must remain consistent or
40. the transport will silently fail to load / register:
41. 
42. 1. Component registration
43.    - `UCT_TL_DEFINE_ENTRY(&uct_obmm_component, obmm, query_tl_devices_fn,
44.      iface_t, "OBMM_", config_table, config_t)` in `obmm_iface.c`
45.    - `UCT_SINGLE_TL_INIT(&uct_obmm_component, obmm, ...)` in `obmm_iface.c`
46.    - `uct_component_t uct_obmm_component = { ... }` in `obmm_md.c`
47. 
48. 2. Class hierarchy (UCS_CLASS_*)
49.    - `uct_obmm_iface_t` derives from `uct_sm_iface_t`
50.    - `uct_obmm_ep_t`    derives from `uct_base_ep_t`
51.    - INIT / CLEANUP / DEFINE / DEFINE_NEW_FUNC / DEFINE_DELETE_FUNC must all
52.      be present and matched, or link will fail with `_init`/`_cleanup`
53.      undefined symbols.
54. 
55. 3. ops tables
56.    - `uct_iface_ops_t`         — set every field; unused fields go to
57.      `ucs_empty_function_return_unsupported` cast to the right func type.
58.    - `uct_iface_internal_ops_t` — same.
59.    - `uct_md_ops_t`            — same.
60.    - When implementing a new capability (e.g. `ep_am_short`), update BOTH:
61.      a) the ops-table entry, and
62.      b) `iface_query` so `attr->cap.flags |= UCT_IFACE_FLAG_AM_SHORT` and
63.         `attr->cap.am.max_short` is set to a real value.
64. 
65. 4. iface_query capability bits
66.    - The transport will be selected by ucp only if its `cap.flags` and the
67.      numeric caps (`max_short`, etc.) match what the protocol layer asks for.
68.      Currently obmm advertises `CONNECT_TO_IFACE | CB_SYNC | EP_CHECK` and all
69.      `cap.am.max_*` are 0 — am_short impl MUST raise `max_short` and add
70.      `UCT_IFACE_FLAG_AM_SHORT`.
71. 
72. 5. Reachability
73.    - `iface_is_reachable_v2` is what UCP uses; the legacy
74.      `iface_is_reachable` field stays as `uct_base_iface_is_reachable`.
75.    - obmm's reachability already piggybacks on `uct_sm_iface_is_reachable`
76.      (same-host check). For two-node obmm, this needs reconsideration; see
77.      the `obmm-api-and-env` skill.
78. 
79. ## AM short pattern (the only semantic to implement now)
80. 
81. Reference: `uct_mm_ep_am_short` in `ucx/src/uct/sm/mm/base/mm_ep.c` and the
82. matching `uct_mm_iface_progress` reception loop in
83. `ucx/src/uct/sm/mm/base/mm_iface.c`.
84. 
85. Conceptual flow on the **sender** side:
86. 
87. 1. Reserve a slot in the peer's receive FIFO (atomic head increment).
88. 2. Pack `[am_id | header | payload]` into the slot's bcopy area or inline
89.    slot data.
90. 3. Publish the slot (release-store of the "valid" / sequence flag).
91. 4. Return `UCS_OK` (or `UCS_ERR_NO_RESOURCE` if FIFO is full — UCP will
92.    retry via pending queue).
93. 
94. Conceptual flow on the **receiver** side, inside `iface_progress`:
95. 
96. 1. Read local FIFO tail.
97. 2. If a new slot is published (acquire-load on flag), read am_id + header
98.    + payload.
99. 3. Dispatch via `uct_iface_invoke_am(&iface->super.super, am_id, data,
100.    length, flags)`.
101. 4. Advance tail.
102. 
103. For obmm, the FIFO and slot memory live in the **pre-imported peer memory
104. region** (see `obmm-api-and-env`), accessed via mmap'd virtual addresses, not
105. via `obmm_export/import` calls at runtime.
106. 
107. ## Helper macros worth knowing
108. 
109. - `UCT_CHECK_AM_ID(am_id)`  — validate AM id at entry of am_short
110. - `UCT_CHECK_LENGTH(length, 0, max_short, "am_short")`
111. - `UCT_TL_EP_STAT_OP(ep, AM, SHORT, length)`
112. - `uct_iface_invoke_am(iface, id, data, len, flags)`
113. - `ucs_derived_of(p, type)`  — downcast
114. - `UCS_CLASS_CALL_SUPER_INIT(super_t, ...)`
115. - `UCS_STATIC_BITMAP_*`, `ucs_arbiter_*`  — used by mm pending queue (not
116.   needed for the first am_short pass unless implementing pending)
117. 
118. ## Required workflow when touching transport code
119. 
120. 1. Before designing a new function, query the vector DB (see
121.    `vector-db-retrieval` skill) for the closest mm/self analogue. Do not
122.    guess macro signatures.
123. 2. Cross-check the chosen reference file with a direct `view` to confirm
124.    the exact prototype, since UCX revisions may have shifted signatures.
125. 3. After implementation, re-read `iface_query` and the ops tables to make
126.    sure capability bits and function pointers stay in sync.
127.
```

</details>

````
1. # obmm UCT transport — design notes
2. 
3. This file is the **single source of truth** for the on-region wire format
4. and the data-path semantics of the `obmm` UCT transport. Update it
5. **before** changing layout, capabilities, or sync rules. AGENTS.md
6. mandates retrieve-before-recall; this doc is the first thing to grep.
7. 
8. Status legend:
9. - **v1** = shipped, MPI cross-node smoke tests pass.
10. - **v2** = current target: complete `am_bcopy` (max_bcopy decoupled from
11.   FIFO element size, no per-message UCP fragmentation below seg_size).
12. 
13. ---
14. 
15. ## Locked-in environment facts
16. 
17. (Mirrors `.github/skills/obmm-api-and-env/SKILL.md`. Do NOT contradict
18. without re-checking that file.)
19. 
20. - Each node pre-exports **one 128 MiB region**; export/import is done
21.   outside UCX. UCT must NOT call `obmm_export/import/preimport/...`.
22. - Data-path mapping is **non-cacheable** (`open(... O_SYNC)` + mmap).
23.   `obmm_set_ownership` is forbidden and irrelevant.
24. - Cross-host 64-bit FAA/CAS on the target NC mapping is **not** reliable enough
25.   for transport ownership or queue reservation. Standalone probe results showed
26.   non-monotonic FAA return values and CAS/readback mismatches, so the protocol
27.   must avoid shared cross-node atomic RMW on hot-path state.
28. - Memory ordering uses **bus-domain fences**
29.   (`ucs_memory_bus_store_fence` / `ucs_memory_bus_load_fence`), NOT the
30.   CPU-domain `ucs_memory_cpu_*_fence` that mm uses. mm peers share an
31.   inner-shareable cache domain; obmm peers do not.
32. - Reachability is keyed on `(exporter_dcna, exporter_deid, memid)`,
33.   never memid alone.
34. - Two-phase pool init (UNINIT → INITING → READY via CAS) plus per-slot
35.   `(generation, owner_pid, owner_starttime)` for crash/PID-reuse safety.
36.   During teardown, INITING is reused only as a transient cleanup lock; after
37.   reset the shared region returns to literal all-zero memory.
38. - ARM64 is the production ISA. NC + bus fences are correct on aarch64.
39. 
40. ---
41. 
42. ## Region layout (v2)
43. 
44. Inside the 128 MiB exported region:
45. 
46. ```
47. +-------------------------------------------------------+ offset 0
48. | uct_obmm_pool_hdr_t (magic, state, geometry)          |
49. +-------------------------------------------------------+
50. | alloc_bitmap[bitmap_words]                            |
51. +-------------------------------------------------------+
52. | slot_meta[slot_count]  (gen, owner_pid, starttime, …) |
53. +-------------------------------------------------------+ hdr->slot_array_offset
54. | slot[0]:                                              |
55. |   bank[local]: lane[0..slot_count-1]                  |
56. |   bank[remote]: lane[0..slot_count-1]                 |
57. +-------------------------------------------------------+
58. | slot[1]: …                                            |
59. …
60. ```
61. 
62. Each slot is **sender-owned** by exactly one iface. Inside that slot:
63. 
64. - there are two banks: `local` and `remote`
65. - each bank has one lane per destination slot index
66. - each lane is SPSC:
67.   - slot owner is the only writer of `head` and `sender_generation`
68.   - the matching receiver is the only writer of `tail` and `tail_generation`
69. 
70. Banking is derived from exporter identity relative to the sender's local export
71. region, not from slot index. This avoids local-slot-index and remote-slot-index
72. collisions in the fixed two-node topology.
73. 
74. Every lane element `elem[N]` has a paired `desc[N]` in that same lane. Their
75. lifetime is identical: once the receiver advances `tail` past index `N`, the
76. sender may reuse both on the next lap.
77. 
78. ### Slot stride
79. 
80. ```
81. lane_stride = align_up(
82.     sizeof(uct_obmm_mailbox_ctl_t) +
83.     fifo_size * elem_size +
84.     fifo_size * seg_size,
85.     cacheline)
86. 
87. slot_stride = align_up(
88.     2 * slot_count * lane_stride,
89.     cacheline)
90. ```
91. 
92. The pool's `slot_count` (compile-time `UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT = 32`)
93. **times** `slot_stride` MUST fit in `region->length` (128 MiB minus pool
94.  header overhead). Defaults are picked to favor short-path coverage over
95.  maximum local process count; lowering `seg_size` and/or `fifo_size`
96.  reduces per-slot footprint, but the supported local attach count remains
97.  the compile-time `slot_count`.
98. 
99. Default budget check:
100. ```
101. fifo_size       =      1
102. elem_size       =  16448   (raw UCT max_short = 16432 total bytes)
103. seg_size        =  32768   (raw UCT max_bcopy = 32768)
104. lane_stride     =  49344
105. ctl + slot data = 64 * 49344 = ~3084 KiB / slot
106. slot_count      =     32
107. total           = ~ 96 MiB / 128 MiB                     ✓
108. ```
109. These defaults are chosen from measured latency sweeps rather than from
110. wire-format arithmetic alone. With Open MPI PML/UCX on this tree, ordinary
111. `MPI_Send` goes through `mca_pml_ucx_send_nbr()` into `ucp_tag_send_nbx()`,
112. and UCX defaults `PROTO_ENABLE=y`, so protocol v2 selects between eager short,
113. eager bcopy single/multi, and rendezvous using its own headers and cost model.
114. The best reasoning-backed configuration found so far is to keep both geometry
115. knobs 64-byte aligned, leave `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE=32768` for 32KiB-class raw bcopy

150. - Hardware probe conclusion:

152.     `lock64` owner mismatches / CAS readback mismatches and `faa64`
153.     non-monotonic old values plus readback failures

156. - SPSC redesign plan:
157.   - switch from the current receiver-owned shared FIFO to **sender-owned

159.   - each slot will contain two mailbox banks (`local`, `remote`) so sender-slot
160.     indexes from the two nodes cannot collide; each bank has one lane per
161.     destination slot index
162.   - each lane is SPSC and depth-1 by default to stay within the current
163.     128 MiB region budget; the sender is the sole writer of `prod_seq`, the
164.     receiver is the sole writer of `cons_seq`
165.   - sender path writes only to its **local owned slot** lane for the target
166.     peer, then publishes `prod_seq` with bus-store ordering; receiver progress
167.     polls inbound lanes and publishes `cons_seq` back to that sender-owned lane
168.   - reuse `elem->generation` for **receiver generation** so a recycled
169.     destination slot drops stale traffic; add a lane-level sender epoch /

53. ## Test environment — IMMUTABLE FACTS
54. 
55. These were stated by the project owner. The transport implementation MUST
56. be designed against exactly this topology:
57. 
58. 1. **Two nodes**, node 0 and node 1.
59. 2. Each node has **already exported a 128 MiB memory region** to the other
60.    side, before any UCX / MPI process starts.
61. 3. Each node has **already imported** the peer's 128 MiB region.
62. 4. The export / import / preimport / unimport / unexport lifecycle is
63.    handled outside the UCX transport — **the obmm UCT transport must NOT
64.    call** `obmm_export`, `obmm_unexport`, `obmm_import`, `obmm_unimport`,
65.    `obmm_preimport`, or `obmm_unpreimport` at runtime.
66. 5. Inside UCT, access to the local and peer regions is done with
67.    **`open("/dev/obmm_shmdev${memid}", O_RDWR | O_SYNC)` + `mmap`**
68.    (NC mapping; see "Locked-in design decisions" below).
69.    The local export memid and peer import memid are discovered by
70.    scanning `/sys/devices/obmm/obmm_shmdev*/` and inspecting whether
71.    each contains an `export_info/` or `import_info/` subdirectory.
72. 6. **No hardware is available** in the development environment. Do not
73.    attempt to run `mpirun`, real `ucx_perftest`, or any test that requires
74.    the obmm device. Validation is limited to:
75.      - `make` / `make install` succeeding,
76.      - `ucx_info -d` listing the obmm component, md, and tl,
77.      - `ucx_info -c` showing OBMM_* env vars,
78.      - static review against this skill and `uct-transport-patterns`.
79. 
80. ## Locked-in design decisions (do not change without re-asking)
81. 
82. These were explicitly decided with the project owner during the v1
83. am_short plan review. They override any conflicting suggestion the
84. agent may otherwise default to (notably the mm transport's behavior).
85. 
86. 1. **NC mapping for the data path.** Open shmdev with
87.    `O_RDWR | O_SYNC` and mmap with `MAP_SHARED`. This puts the FIFO
88.    region into a non-cacheable mapping, which:
89.      - bypasses the OBMM cacheable consistency model (writers and
90.        readers from any host coexist),
91.      - removes the need to ever call `obmm_set_ownership` from the
92.        transport.
93. 2. **Cross-node 64-bit FAA/CAS on NC is not transport-safe.** A
94.    standalone probe on the target NC mapping showed non-monotonic FAA
95.    return values plus CAS/readback mismatches under contention. The
96.    transport must therefore avoid shared cross-node atomic RMW in the
97.    data path and use single-writer sender-owned mailbox state instead.
98. 3. **UCT owns the in-region layout.** The 128 MiB exported region is
99.    zero-filled at platform export time. The transport places its own
100.    header (state / version / slot bitmap / slot_meta / fixed-size
101.    slots) at the start of the region. A two-phase init is used:
102.    `state` transitions UNINIT→INITING (CAS) → fill geometry → bus
103.    fence → store READY. Losers spin on READY then bus-load fence.
104.    Single-magic init is racy (geometry not yet visible) and must
105.    not be used.
106. 4. **Topology**: per node there is exactly 1 export region and 1
107.    import region (the peer node's export). Discovered via
108.    `/sys/devices/obmm/obmm_shmdev*/{export_info,import_info}`.
109.    Reachability and mapping table keys are
110.    `(exporter_dcna, exporter_deid, memid)` from sysfs — NOT memid
111.    alone (collision-prone).
112. 5. **One obmm iface per process** is the current assumption for this
113.    transport baseline.
114. 6. **Self-loopback inside one node** is supported: same-node processes
115.    communicate by both mapping the local export region (the imported
116.    "peer region" entry simply will not exist in the single-node case,
117.    or will equal the local one — handle both).
118. 7. **Wire/layout alignment is 64 bytes.** Keep mailbox lane and element
119.    strides 64-byte aligned unless the user provides new measurements.
120. 8. **Sender-owned mailbox receive must tolerate one-way traffic.**
121.    Collective parent→child traffic may arrive before the receiver has
122.    created a local EP back to the parent, so `iface_progress` must be
123.    able to discover and progress unregistered inbound lanes dynamically.
124. 9. **Slot lifecycle uses generation tokens.** Each slot has
125.    `(owner_pid, owner_starttime, generation, state)` in slot_meta.
126.    `iface_addr` and every FIFO elem carry `generation`; receiver
127.    discards mismatches. Destroy = mark DEAD → bus fence → bump
128.    generation → clear bit. Crash recovery: scan bitmap, validate
129.    `/proc/<pid>/stat starttime`, reclaim. PID alone is insufficient
130.    (PID reuse).
131. 10. **Cross-node memory ordering uses BUS-domain fences.**
132.    `ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()` / `ucs_memory_bus_load_fence()`
133.    (sfence/lfence on x86, `dmb oshst`/`dmb oshld` on arm64). The
134.    CPU-domain fences mm uses (`ucs_memory_cpu_*_fence`) are
135.    inner-shareable only and DO NOT cover cross-host NC visibility.
136. 
137. ## OBMM consistency model — why NC matters
138. 
139. From `obmm/doc/libobmm.md` and `obmm/doc/obmm_set_ownership.md`:
140. 
141. - For **cacheable** OBMM mappings, at any moment all hosts touching a
142.   region must be in one of two states:
143.     a) all hosts are PROT_READ or PROT_NONE, OR
144.     b) exactly one host has writers; all other hosts must be PROT_NONE.
145. - A receive-FIFO model (writer on the sending host, reader on the
146.   receiving host, on the SAME region) violates this: it would require
147.   one host to write while another host reads simultaneously.
148. - Therefore the obmm transport CANNOT use cacheable mappings for the
149.   FIFO region without expensive ownership flips per message.
150. - NC (O_SYNC) mappings are exempt: per the doc, "用户无需关心一致性
151.   模型，所有的用户均具备读写权限". This is why decision (1) above
152.   is mandatory, not optional.
153. 
154. ## Implications for the transport design
155. 
156. These follow from the facts above and should be treated as defaults; ask
157. the user before deviating:
158. 
159. - **Memory registration** (`uct_md_ops_t::mem_reg` / `mem_dereg`) does not
160.   need to call libobmm. The current placeholders
161.   (`uct_md_dummy_mem_reg` / `uct_md_dummy_mem_dereg`) are appropriate
162.   because the buffers used by am_short live inside the pre-imported
163.   peer region, not in arbitrary user buffers.
164. - **Address exchange** uses split device/iface addresses:
165.   - `device_addr` carries `(exporter_dcna, exporter_deid_hi,
166.     exporter_deid_lo)`
167.   - `iface_addr` carries `(slot_index, generation, pid, fifo_size,
168.     fifo_elem_size, bcopy_seg_size)`
169.   Reachability stays keyed on exporter identity; memid filtering belongs
170.   to MD discovery, not to peer matching in the hot path.
171. - **Reachability**: `iface_is_reachable_v2` must validate geometry and
172.   confirm that the MD already has a mapped export/import region for the
173.   peer exporter identity. Do not fall back to same-host-only
174.   reachability checks.
175. - **Progress wiring**: `iface_progress_enable/disable` MUST call
176.   `uct_base_iface_progress_enable_cb(...)` /
177.   `uct_base_iface_progress_disable(...)`. The current
178.   `ucs_empty_function` stubs prevent UCP from ever polling the iface.
179. - **EP_CHECK**: do NOT advertise `UCT_IFACE_FLAG_EP_CHECK` in v1.
180.   The current skeleton sets it but `ep_check` only returns OK; no

42.   reset the shared region returns to literal all-zero memory.
43. - ARM64 is the production ISA. NC + bus fences are correct on aarch64.
44. 
45. ---
46. 
47. ## Region layout (v2)
48. 
49. Inside the 128 MiB exported region:
50. 
51. ```
52. +-------------------------------------------------------+ offset 0
53. | uct_obmm_pool_hdr_t (magic, state, geometry)          |
54. +-------------------------------------------------------+
55. | alloc_bitmap[bitmap_words]                            |
56. +-------------------------------------------------------+
57. | slot_meta[slot_count]  (gen, owner_pid, starttime, …) |
58. +-------------------------------------------------------+ hdr->slot_array_offset
59. | slot[0]:                                              |
60. |   bank[local]: lane[0..slot_count-1]                  |
61. |   bank[remote]: lane[0..slot_count-1]                 |
62. +-------------------------------------------------------+
63. | slot[1]: …                                            |
64. …
65. ```
66. 
67. Each slot is **sender-owned** by exactly one iface. Inside that slot:
68. 
69. - there are two banks: `local` and `remote`
70. - each bank has one lane per destination slot index
71. - each lane is SPSC:
72.   - slot owner is the only writer of `head` and `sender_generation`
73.   - the matching receiver is the only writer of `tail` and `tail_generation`
74. 
75. Banking is derived from exporter identity relative to the sender's local export
76. region, not from slot index. This avoids local-slot-index and remote-slot-index
77. collisions in the fixed two-node topology.
78. 
79. Every lane element `elem[N]` has a paired `desc[N]` in that same lane. Their
80. lifetime is identical: once the receiver advances `tail` past index `N`, the
81. sender may reuse both on the next lap.
82. 
83. ### Slot stride
84. 
85. ```
86. lane_stride = align_up(
87.     sizeof(uct_obmm_mailbox_ctl_t) +
88.     fifo_size * elem_size +
89.     fifo_size * seg_size,
90.     cacheline)
91. 
92. slot_stride = align_up(
93.     2 * slot_count * lane_stride,
94.     cacheline)
95. ```
96. 
97. The pool's `slot_count` (compile-time `UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT = 32`)
98. **times** `slot_stride` MUST fit in `region->length` (128 MiB minus pool
99.  header overhead). Defaults are picked to favor short-path coverage over
100.  maximum local process count; lowering `seg_size` and/or `fifo_size`
101.  reduces per-slot footprint, but the supported local attach count remains
102.  the compile-time `slot_count`.
103. 
104. Default budget check:
105. ```
106. fifo_size       =      1
107. elem_size       =  16448   (raw UCT max_short = 16432 total bytes)
108. seg_size        =  32768   (raw UCT max_bcopy = 32768)
109. lane_stride     =  49344
110. ctl + slot data = 64 * 49344 = ~3084 KiB / slot
111. slot_count      =     32
112. total           = ~ 96 MiB / 128 MiB                     ✓
113. ```
114. These defaults are chosen from measured latency sweeps rather than from
115. wire-format arithmetic alone. With Open MPI PML/UCX on this tree, ordinary
116. `MPI_Send` goes through `mca_pml_ucx_send_nbr()` into `ucp_tag_send_nbx()`,
117. and UCX defaults `PROTO_ENABLE=y`, so protocol v2 selects between eager short,
118. eager bcopy single/multi, and rendezvous using its own headers and cost model.
119. The best reasoning-backed configuration found so far is to keep both geometry
120. knobs 64-byte aligned, leave `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE=32768` for 32KiB-class raw bcopy
121. capacity, and reduce `FIFO_ELEM_SIZE` to `16448` so 16KiB-class payloads stay
122. comfortably on short without over-extending the short window into slower
123. 32KiB-class territory.
124. 
125. When the last local iface on an export exits, UCX resets the entire local
126. export region to zero before another attach may re-initialize the pool.
127. 
128. ---
129. 
130. ## FIFO element layout
131. 
132. `uct_obmm_fifo_element_t` (16 bytes, packed):
133. 
134. | field      | bytes | notes                                          |
135. |------------|-------|------------------------------------------------|
136. | flags      |   1   | BCOPY bit only                                 |
137. | am_id      |   1   |                                                |
138. | length     |   2   | u16 — bytes passed to the AM callback          |
139. | generation |   4   | receiver-slot generation token at TX time      |
140. | header     |   8   | am_short user-visible 8B header (unused bcopy) |
141. 
142. For **am_short**, callback data starts at `&elem->header`, so the callback sees
143. `[header | payload]` and `elem->length = sizeof(header) + payload_length`.
144. The raw UCT limit remains `max_short = elem_size - 16`.
145. 
146. For **am_bcopy**, payload lives in the paired `desc[N]`. On bcopy the sender
147. writes:
148. - `elem->flags  = BCOPY`
149. - `elem->am_id  = id`
150. - `elem->length = pack_cb_returned_length`     (≤ seg_size, so ≤ u16max)
151. - `elem->generation = ep->expected_generation`
152. - `elem->header = 0` (unused)
153. 
154. Receiver, on seeing FLAG_BCOPY, computes
155. `desc[N] = slot_descs + (idx & mask) * seg_size` and calls
156. `uct_iface_invoke_am(am_id, desc[N], length, 0)`.
157. 
158. Because `desc[N]` is bound 1:1 to `elem[N]`, no extra metadata is
159. exchanged in the FIFO element to locate the desc.
160. 
161. ### `length` field width
162. 
163. `elem->length` stays `uint16_t`, capping `seg_size` at 65535. We reject
164. larger `seg_size` at iface init. If a future `seg_size > 64KiB` is
165. needed, widen `length` to `uint32_t` and update the compatibility checks.
166. 
167. ---
168. 
169. ## Sender side (`obmm_ep`)
170. 
171. Each EP binds to one outbound lane in its **local sender-owned slot**:
172. 
173. - slot base = local `iface->slot`
174. - bank = `local` if the peer device address names our export region, otherwise
175.   `remote`
176. - destination lane index = peer `iface_addr.slot_index`
177. 
178. Both `am_short` and `am_bcopy` publish to that lane identically:
179. 
180. ```
181. 1. load local cached tail for this lane
182. 2. if (tx_index - cached_tail) >= fifo_size:
183.         bus_load_fence; refresh cached_tail; recheck;
184.         if still full: return UCS_ERR_NO_RESOURCE
185. 3. idx = tx_index, N = idx & mask
186. 4. payload write:
187.       short: memcpy header+payload into elem[N]+1
188.       bcopy: pack_cb(desc[N], arg) -> length
189. 5. fill elem[N] header fields (flags, am_id, length, generation, [header])
190. 6. ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()                          <- release barrier
191. 7. tx_index++
192. 8. lane_ctl->head = tx_index
193. ```
194. 
195. There is no shared producer lock, shared head CAS, or shared FAA. All hot-path
196. ownership is single-writer by construction.
197. 
198. ### Pending
199. 
200. `ep_pending_add` always queues into the iface arbiter. `iface_progress`
201. dispatches pending on every call, even if no RX completion occurred, because
202. depth-1 lanes will hit `UCS_ERR_NO_RESOURCE` frequently.
203. 
204. ---
205. 
206. ## Receiver side (`obmm_iface_progress`)
207. 
208. ```
209. round-robin over registered inbound lanes, up to fifo_max_poll completions:
210.     if lane is inactive: continue
211.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence()
212.     if lane_ctl->sender_generation != expected_sender_generation:
213.         continue                                             (stale registration)
214.     if lane_ctl->head == rx_index:
215.         continue                                             (no work)
216.     elem = elem[rx_index & mask]
217.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence()                              (acquire payload)
218.     if elem->generation != iface->generation:
219.         drop silently (slot was reused after our death+rebirth)
220.     elif elem->flags & BCOPY:
221.         desc = desc[rx_index & mask]
222.         invoke_am(am_id, desc,  length, 0)
223.     else:
224.         invoke_am(am_id, &elem->header, length, 0)
225.     rx_index++
226.     full bus fence
227.     if lane_ctl->sender_generation != expected_sender_generation:
228.         skip ack publish for this completion
229.     lane_ctl->tail = rx_index
230.     ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()
231.     if lane_ctl->sender_generation != expected_sender_generation:
232.         skip tail_generation publish
233.     lane_ctl->tail_generation = expected_sender_generation
234. ```
235. 
236. Each inbound lane is registered by `(bank, sender_slot_index)` and refcounted,
237. so multiple EPs to the same sender slot do not duplicate-consume one lane.
238. 
239. ---
240.
````

</details>

1. <overview>
2. This segment shifted from speculative fixes to hard diagnosis of the remaining `osu_multi_lat` hang, and then to a protocol-level redesign after proving the platform’s NC-mapped 64-bit atomics are not reliable enough for the current obmm shared-head/lock scheme. The approach was: instrument the full progress path, reduce log spam, isolate the failure to the shared lock word, validate that with a standalone hardware probe, then begin replacing the protocol with sender-owned SPSC mailboxes that avoid cross-node CAS/FAA entirely.
3. </overview>
4. 
5. <history>
6. 1. The user said the lock-token change did not fix the bug and asked to stop blind changes and first locate where the hang actually occurs in the flow.
7.    - I re-read the session plan, retrieved UCX transport references with the vector DB, and inspected obmm `ep/iface/pool/fifo` code plus mm pending/progress references.
8.    - I added bounded diagnostics across the full obmm flow:
9.      - send attempts while pending
10.      - `reserve_slot()` failures and recovery
11.      - `pending_add()` queueing
12.      - `process_pending()` reschedules/recovery
13.      - iface progress idle-with-pending/recovery
14.    - I updated the session plan to record that the goal was now flow localization rather than more lock-behavior guesses.
15. 
16. 2. The user reported that logs still spammed heavily, especially `reserve stalled / reserve recovered`.
17.    - I throttled only the hottest path: `reserve` logs now emit only after a persistent streak (`>= 1024` failures) and only on power-of-two counts beyond that threshold.
18.    - This preserved “real stall” visibility while removing transient lock-contention noise.
19. 
20. 3. The user observed a repeating pattern from the same process/iface/ep/req with `reason=lock-busy`:
21.    - `pending stalled x1`
22.    - `iface idle with pending x1`
23.    - `pending recovered x1`
24.    - `iface pending recovered x1`
25.    and asked whether that was enough to locate the issue.
26.    - I asked a targeted question about the `lock=` value versus the local `token=` in those lines.
27.    - The user answered that `lock` was mostly stable but **not equal** to that EP’s token.
28.    - Based on that, I concluded the request was waiting on a foreign token occupying the peer head lock, not on FIFO-full or a dead iface progress loop.
29. 
30. 4. To attribute that foreign lock value, I added a one-time `ep token map` diagnostic in `ep_create`.
31.    - The user reran and reported that the stuck `lock=0x2e315166` did **not** match any full token, and later also did **not** match any token’s low 32 bits.
32.    - This ruled out “another legitimate EP holds the lock” and strongly suggested the shared lock word itself was being observed as an invalid value.
33. 
34. 5. To classify the invalid lock-word behavior, I added two one-shot diagnostics around unlock:
35.    - `unlock owner mismatch` — before clearing lock, it is already not our token
36.    - `unlock readback nonzero` — after writing zero, reading back still sees non-zero
37.    - The user reported three hits:
38.      - first `unlock owner mismatch`
39.      - then `unlock readback nonzero`
40.      - then another `unlock owner mismatch` from a different EP

42. 
43. 6. I then moved the investigation out of UCX transport code and asked whether cross-node NC FAA return values were known reliable.
44.    - The user answered “不确定”.

48.    - It has:
49.      - `lock64` mode to reproduce the current lock protocol outside UCX
50.      - `faa64` mode to test 64-bit FAA return-value self-consistency
51.    - I hardened it after review:
52.      - do not discard CAS return value
53.      - validate `--mode`
54.      - validate device is a character device
55.      - validate probe offset fits the 128 MiB region

79.    - From this I concluded the platform fact had changed materially: on the target NC mapping, the current transport must **not** assume mm-style cross-node 64-bit CAS/FAA are safe for shared queue ownership.

82. 9. The user then explicitly asked to change the protocol and said they can enlarge the shared memory if necessary.
83.    - I started designing a replacement protocol that does **not** use cross-node atomic RMW:

180. - The crucial runtime diagnosis outcome:

191.   - did **not** match any token’s low 32 bits either
192.   - `unlock owner mismatch` followed by `unlock readback nonzero` showed the lock word itself was not a legitimate shared ownership variable on this NC mapping
193. - The decisive hardware probe result:
194.   - `lock64` mode showed both:
195.     - CAS success followed by wrong readback
196.     - owner mismatch while supposedly holding the lock
197.   - `faa64` mode showed:

199.     - readback less than `old+1`
200.     - final counter less than total issued ops
201.   - This means the current platform cannot safely use mm-style shared-head atomic reservation over these NC mappings, regardless of lock-token scheme
202. - The redesign direction chosen:
203.   - **sender-owned slots**, not receiver-owned shared FIFO
204.   - each slot contains mailbox lanes keyed by:
205.     - bank (`local` vs `remote`)
206.     - destination slot index
207.   - per-lane default depth: **1**
208.   - one sender is sole writer of `prod_seq/head`
209.   - one receiver is sole writer of `cons_seq/tail`
210. - Banking rationale:
211.   - slot indexes can collide between the two nodes
212.   - with fixed two-node topology, two banks avoid local-slot-index vs remote-slot-index collisions
213.   - critique emphasized bank must be derived from exporter identity relative to the slot owner, not from slot number itself
214. - Generation/epoch requirements from critique:
215.   - receiver generation must still be validated per message so recycled destination slots drop stale traffic
216.   - sender-slot epoch/ack generation must be preserved so stale consumers cannot ack into a reclaimed sender slot

218.   - depth-1 lanes will make `NO_RESOURCE` common
219.   - iface progress must still dispatch pending every call, even if there was no RX completion

115. <technical_details>
116. - **BW / UCP contract**
117.   - `iface_attr->bandwidth.dedicated` is consumed by `ucp_tl_iface_bandwidth()` and UCP protocol/lane cost modeling.
118.   - UCP address unpack also rejects non-positive bandwidth values.
119.   - Therefore `UCX_OBMM_BW` is optional as a user knob, but obmm itself must always report a positive bandwidth to UCP.
120.   - The default was changed to `3400MBs` to match sustained measured transport throughput rather than optimistic peak.
121. 
122. - **Meaning of `unexpected tag-receive descriptor ... was not matched`**
123.   - Emitted by `ucp_tag_match_cleanup()` when descriptors remain on `tm->unexpected.all` at UCP worker teardown.
124.   - It proves the receiver accepted extra/late/misrouted tag messages; it is not just a send-drop symptom.
125. 
126. - **Confirmed slot double-claim bug**
127.   - Original `uct_obmm_pool_try_claim()` could allow:
128.     1. process A CASes bitmap bit 0→1
129.     2. before A publishes `slot_meta.state = IN_USE`
130.     3. process B sees `bit=1 && state!=IN_USE`
131.     4. B “takes over” same slot
132.   - This caused multiple processes to publish the same receive slot in their iface address, explaining tag mismatches.
133.   - Fixed by adding explicit `CLAIMING` state and tightening alloc/free/scavenge sequencing.
134.   - `free_slot()` now keeps owner identity until after `clear_bit`, so `DEAD` is meaningful during release/scavenge races.
135. 
136. - **Cross-node 4-rank hang signal**
137.   - Reproducer:
138.     `mpirun -np 4 --hostfile hostfile --map-by node --mca pml ucx --allow-run-as-root -x OPAL_PREFIX -x PATH -x LD_LIBRARY_PATH -x UCX_TLS=obmm -x UCX_OBMM_MEMIDS=1,2 /osu/pt2pt/osu_multi_lat -m 1:1`
139.   - User results:
140.     - same-node reduced cases: no repro
141.     - cross-node 2 proc: no repro
142.     - cross-node 4 proc: probabilistic silent hangs
143.     - diagnostics:
144.       - `lock busy ...` log appeared every 4-proc run
145.       - never on 2-proc
146.       - `stale elem drop` never appeared
147.   - This weakens the “stale-slot/message corruption” hypothesis and points more toward contention/locking issues.
148. 
149. - **`BUSY` semantics in UCT/UCP**
150.   - `uct_ep_pending_add(...)=UCS_ERR_BUSY` means “request was not queued; resources are available now; caller should retry”.
151.   - UCP interprets this as immediate retry rather than queued pending work.
152.   - Because obmm’s `NO_RESOURCE` can mean either FIFO-full or transient head-lock contention, using `BUSY` after such a failure can create retry storms under contention.
153.   - obmm `pending_add()` was therefore changed to **always queue** instead of returning `BUSY`.
154. 
155. - **Remaining unresolved hypothesis: lock-token collision**
156.   - `try_lock_head()` infers lock acquisition success by checking `peer_ctl->lock == ep->lock_token` after attempting CAS, because the CAS return value is considered unreliable on the target NC mapping.
157.   - If two writers can share the same token, both may think they acquired the same lock.
158.   - The old token used simple XOR with a process-local `ep` pointer, which is unsafe across processes because virtual addresses can repeat.
159.   - New token builder now mixes:
160.     - local exporter identity
161.     - local slot/generation
162.     - local pid/starttime
163.     - peer slot/pid
164.     - ep pointer
165.   - This fix was applied, but runtime validation is still pending.
166.   - The code review also requested a one-time warning when `ucs_sys_get_proc_create_time(getpid())` returns `0`, since that weakens token uniqueness; this warning is not yet in the file because the last patch failed.
167. 
168. - **Diagnostics policy used in this segment**
169.   - For difficult bugs, the user has explicitly said to add logs directly when there is a concrete direction.
170.   - Temporary diagnostics were intentionally one-time/high-priority to avoid perturbing timing too much and to avoid burying the interesting signal in repeated WARN spam.

174.   - Real validation depends on the user’s MPI/OSU runs.
175.   - `ompi/` and `obmm/` remain read-only context.

310. static UCS_F_ALWAYS_INLINE unsigned
311. uct_obmm_iface_progress_lane(uct_obmm_iface_t *iface, uct_obmm_rx_lane_t *lane)
312. {
313.     uct_obmm_fifo_element_t *elem;
314.     uint32_t                 head;
315. 
316.     if (!lane->active) {
317.         return 0;
318.     }
319. 
320.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
321.     if (lane->ctl->sender_generation != lane->sender_generation) {
322.         return 0;
323.     }
324. 
325.     head = lane->ctl->head;
326.     if (head == lane->rx_index) {
327.         return 0;
328.     }
329. 
330.     elem = uct_obmm_lane_elem(lane->elems, lane->rx_index, iface->fifo_mask,
331.                               iface->fifo_elem_size);
332.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence();
333. 
334.     if (elem->generation == iface->generation) {
335.         if (elem->flags & UCT_OBMM_MAILBOX_ELEM_FLAG_BCOPY) {
336.             void *desc = uct_obmm_lane_desc(lane->descs, lane->rx_index,
337.                                             iface->fifo_mask,
338.                                             iface->bcopy_seg_size);
339.             uct_iface_invoke_am(&iface->super, elem->am_id,
340.                                 desc, elem->length, 0);
341.         } else {
342.             uct_iface_invoke_am(&iface->super, elem->am_id,
343.                                 &elem->header, elem->length, 0);
344.         }
345.     }
346. 
347.     lane->rx_index++;
348.     uct_obmm_bus_full_fence();
349.     if (lane->ctl->sender_generation != lane->sender_generation) {
350.         return 1;
351.     }
352.     lane->ctl->tail = lane->rx_index;
353.     ucs_memory_bus_store_fence();
354.     if (lane->ctl->sender_generation != lane->sender_generation) {
355.         return 1;
356.     }
357.     lane->ctl->tail_generation = lane->sender_generation;
358.     return 1;
359. }

362. static unsigned uct_obmm_iface_progress(uct_iface_h tl_iface)
363. {
364.     uct_obmm_iface_t *iface = ucs_derived_of(tl_iface, uct_obmm_iface_t);
365.     unsigned          polled = 0;
366.     unsigned          total_lanes = UCT_OBMM_MAILBOX_BANK_COUNT *
367.                                     UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT;
368.     unsigned          scanned;
369. 
370.     for (scanned = 0; (scanned < total_lanes) && (polled < iface->fifo_max_poll);
371.          ++scanned) {
372.         unsigned           idx  = (iface->rx_lane_rr + scanned) % total_lanes;
373.         unsigned           bank = idx / UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT;
374.         unsigned           slot = idx % UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT;
375. 
376.         polled += uct_obmm_iface_progress_lane(iface,
377.                                                &iface->rx_lanes[bank][slot]);
378.     }
379. 
380.     iface->rx_lane_rr = (iface->rx_lane_rr + 1) % total_lanes;
381. 
382.     if (polled < iface->fifo_max_poll) {
383.         polled += uct_obmm_iface_progress_unregistered_lanes(iface,
384.                                                              iface->fifo_max_poll - polled);
385.     }
386. 
387.     ucs_arbiter_dispatch(&iface->arbiter, 1, uct_obmm_ep_process_pending,
388.                          &polled);
389. 
390.     return polled;
391. }

293. retry:
294.     head = ep->fifo_ctl->head;
295.     /* check if there is room in the remote process's receive FIFO to write */
296.     if (!UCT_MM_EP_IS_ABLE_TO_SEND(head, ep->cached_tail, iface->config.fifo_size)) {
297.         if (!ucs_arbiter_group_is_empty(&ep->arb_group)) {
298.             /* pending isn't empty. don't send now to prevent out-of-order sending */
299.             return uct_mm_ep_no_resources_handle(ep, flags);
300.         } else {
301.             /* pending is empty. update the local copy of the tail to its
302.              * actual value on the remote peer */
303.             uct_mm_ep_update_cached_tail(ep);
304.             if (!UCT_MM_EP_IS_ABLE_TO_SEND(head, ep->cached_tail, iface->config.fifo_size)) {
305.                 ucs_arbiter_group_push_head_elem_always(&ep->arb_group,
306.                                                         &ep->arb_elem);
307.                 ucs_arbiter_group_schedule_nonempty(&iface->arbiter,
308.                                                     &ep->arb_group);
309.                 return uct_mm_ep_no_resources_handle(ep, flags);
310.             }
311.         }
312.     }
313. 
314.     status = uct_mm_ep_get_remote_elem(ep, head, &elem);
315.     if (status != UCS_OK) {
316.         ucs_assert(status == UCS_ERR_NO_RESOURCE);
317.         ucs_trace_poll("couldn't get an available FIFO element. retrying");
318.         goto retry;
319.     }
320. 
321.     switch (send_op) {
322.     case UCT_MM_SEND_AM_SHORT:
323.         /* write to the remote FIFO */
324.         uct_am_short_fill_data(elem + 1, header, payload, length,
325.                                UCS_ARCH_MEMCPY_NT_DEST);
326. 
327.         elem_flags   = UCT_MM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_INLINE;
328.         elem->length = length + sizeof(header);
329. 
330.         uct_mm_iface_trace_am(iface, UCT_AM_TRACE_TYPE_SEND, elem_flags, am_id,
331.                               elem + 1, elem->length,
332.                               head & ~UCT_MM_IFACE_FIFO_HEAD_EVENT_ARMED);
333.         UCT_TL_EP_STAT_OP(&ep->super, AM, SHORT, sizeof(header) + length);
334.         break;
335.     case UCT_MM_SEND_AM_BCOPY:
336.         /* write to the remote descriptor */
337.         /* get the base_address: local ptr to remote memory chunk after attaching to it */
338.         status = uct_mm_ep_get_remote_seg(ep, elem->desc.seg_id,
339.                                           elem->desc.seg_size, &base_address);
340.         if (ucs_unlikely(status != UCS_OK)) {
341.             return status;
342.         }
343. 
344.         desc_data    = UCS_PTR_BYTE_OFFSET(base_address, elem->desc.offset);
345.         length       = pack_cb(desc_data, arg);
346.         elem_flags   = 0;
347.         elem->length = length;
348. 
349.         uct_mm_iface_trace_am(iface, UCT_AM_TRACE_TYPE_SEND, elem_flags, am_id,
350.                               desc_data, elem->length,
351.                               head & ~UCT_MM_IFACE_FIFO_HEAD_EVENT_ARMED);
352.         UCT_TL_EP_STAT_OP(&ep->super, AM, BCOPY, length);
353.         break;
354.     case UCT_MM_SEND_AM_SHORT_IOV:
355.         elem_flags   = UCT_MM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_INLINE;
356.         ucs_iov_iter_init(&iov_iter);
357.         elem->length = uct_iov_to_buffer(iov, iovcnt, &iov_iter, elem + 1,
358.                                          SIZE_MAX);
359. 
360.         uct_mm_iface_trace_am(iface, UCT_AM_TRACE_TYPE_SEND, elem_flags, am_id,
361.                               elem + 1, elem->length,
362.                               head & ~UCT_MM_IFACE_FIFO_HEAD_EVENT_ARMED);
363.         UCT_TL_EP_STAT_OP(&ep->super, AM, SHORT, elem->length);
364.         break;
365.     }
366. 
367.     elem->am_id = am_id;
368. 
369.     /* memory barrier - make sure that the memory is flushed before setting the
370.      * 'writing is complete' flag which the reader checks */
371.     ucs_memory_cpu_store_fence();
372. 
373.     /* set the owner bit to indicate that the writing is complete.
374.      * the owner bit flips after every FIFO wraparound */
375.     if (head & iface->config.fifo_size) {
376.         elem_flags |= UCT_MM_FIFO_ELEM_FLAG_OWNER;
377.     }
378.     elem->flags = elem_flags;
379. 
380.     if (ucs_unlikely(head & UCT_MM_IFACE_FIFO_HEAD_EVENT_ARMED)) {
381.         uct_mm_ep_signal_remote(ep);
382.     }
383. 
384.     uct_mm_ep_peer_check(ep, flags);
385. 
386.     switch (send_op) {

388.     case UCT_MM_SEND_AM_SHORT_IOV:
389.         return UCS_OK;
390.     case UCT_MM_SEND_AM_BCOPY:
391.         return length;
392.     default:
393.         return UCS_ERR_INVALID_PARAM;
394.     }

400. static unsigned uct_mm_iface_progress(uct_iface_h tl_iface)
401. {
402.     uct_mm_iface_t *iface = ucs_derived_of(tl_iface, uct_mm_iface_t);
403.     unsigned total_count  = 0;
404.     unsigned count;
405. 
406.     ucs_assert(iface->fifo_poll_count >= UCT_MM_IFACE_FIFO_MIN_POLL);
407. 
408.     /* progress receive */
409.     do {
410.         count = uct_mm_iface_poll_fifo(iface);
411.         ucs_assert(count < 2);
412.         total_count += count;
413.         ucs_assert(total_count < UINT_MAX);
414.     } while ((count != 0) && (total_count < iface->fifo_poll_count));
415. 
416.     uct_mm_iface_fifo_window_adjust(iface, total_count);
417. 
418.     /* progress the pending sends (if there are any) */
419.     ucs_arbiter_dispatch(&iface->arbiter, 1, uct_mm_ep_process_pending,
420.                          &total_count);
421. 
422.     return total_count;
423. }

### 💬 Copilot

**结论先说：按你现在这两套“实际协议形态”来比，原来的跨节点原子 FIFO 的理论性能上限更高；当前这套 mailbox 的上限明显更低。**  
但要补一句：这不是因为 **sender-owned mailbox** 这个思路天生更慢，而是因为你现在这版 mailbox 选了几个非常伤性能的点：**depth=1、receiver 远端轮询、空转时全槽扫描**。

| 维度 | 原跨节点原子 FIFO | 当前 mailbox |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 发送端热路径 | 远端原子保留 head + 远端写 payload | 本地写 payload/head |
| 接收端热路径 | **本地**轮询本地 FIFO | **远端**读 sender slot，再远端写 tail ack |
| 队列深度 | 原来是“可做深”的 FIFO | 当前默认 **FIFO_SIZE=1** |
| 多发送者竞争 | 共享 head/lock，容易争用 | 每 lane SPSC，无共享原子竞争 |
| progress 复杂度 | 接近 **O(1)** 本地 poll | 已注册 lane 轮询 + 未注册 lane 动态扫描 |
| 对 collectives | child 只看本地接收 FIFO | child 可能要扫 remote sender lanes |

### 为什么我判断旧 atomic FIFO 上限更高

1. **当前 mailbox 把“远端写”换成了“远端读轮询”**，这对性能非常不友好。  
   当前设计里 sender 写的是**自己的本地 slot**，receiver 在 `iface_progress()` 里去读 **remote sender slot** 的 `head/elem/desc`，然后再把 `tail` 回写过去。也就是接收侧热路径变成了“远端读 + 远端写 ack”。这在 NC 内存上通常比“receiver 本地 poll”差很多。  
   代码上就是现在的 sender-owned slot 和 receiver 路径：`DESIGN.md:67-81,169-237`，以及 `obmm_iface.c:310-389`。

2. **`FIFO_SIZE=1` 直接把吞吐上限压死了。**  
   当前 mailbox 默认每个 sender→receiver lane 只有 **1 个槽**，意味着任何轻微 burst/pipeline 都会立刻撞 `NO_RESOURCE`，然后走 pending/arbiter。  
   这不是“小优化问题”，而是**协议窗口只有 1**，先天就不可能跑出好吞吐。  
   见 `DESIGN.md:104-112,198-202`。

3. **receiver 的 progress 成本是 O(槽数) 级别，不是 O(1)。**  
   当前已注册 lane 会 round-robin 扫；如果没进展，还会去做 **unregistered lane dynamic scan**，遍历 region/pool/slot，看有没有发给本 `iface-\>slot_index` 的数据。  
   这对 correctness 很关键，但对性能非常重，尤其 collective 场景。  
   代码就是 `obmm_iface.c:37-116` 和 `obmm_iface.c:362-389`。

4. **原 atomic FIFO 的 receiver 热路径其实很干净。**  
   mm/原 obmm 那类 receiver-owned FIFO，本质上是 sender 往 receiver 的 FIFO push，receiver 只需要**本地 poll 一个接收 FIFO**，再本地推进 tail。  
   mm 参考里非常典型：本地 `recv_fifo_ctl/read_index`，`iface_progress()` 主要是本地 poll FIFO。  
   参考 `ucx_code -\> ucx/src/uct/sm/mm/base/mm_iface.h:196-223` 和 `mm_iface.c:400-423`。  
   sender 侧当然要做 head 保留，mm 是共享 head reservation（`mm_ep.c:294-318`），但 receiver 侧比当前 mailbox 轻得多。

### 那 mailbox 有没有理论优势？

**有，但不是你现在这版。**

sender-owned mailbox 的理论优势在于：

1. **每个 lane 是 SPSC**，没有共享 head/lock 的跨节点原子争用。  
   这一点在**多 sender 打一个 receiver**时，理论上比共享 atomic FIFO 更容易扩展。

2. **one-way traffic 语义更自然**。  
   这也是它 correctness 上能稳住 collective 的原因之一。

但你现在这版把这些潜在优势基本抵消了，因为：

- depth=1
- receiver 需要 remote poll
- 还要 dynamic scan unregistered lanes
- pending 几乎会成为常态

所以**当前实现的性能差，不足以说明 sender-owned mailbox 思路本身上限低；只能说明你现在这个具体实现上限低。**

### 更精确的判断

如果你问的是：

1. **“当前这版 mailbox vs 原来的 atomic FIFO，谁的理论上限更高？”**  
   **原 atomic FIFO 更高。**

2. **“sender-owned mailbox 这类协议 vs atomic FIFO 这类协议，谁理论上限更高？”**  
   **不能一刀切。**  
   - **1:1 / 小消息 / 低轮询成本**：atomic FIFO 往往更强，因为 receiver 本地 poll 很便宜。  
   - **高并发多发送者争用同一接收队列**：mailbox/SPSC 可能更强，因为避免共享原子热点。  
   - 但前提是 mailbox 不能像现在这样 **depth=1 + 全扫 remote lanes**。

### 为什么你现在“正确但极慢”是符合理论预期的

因为你现在这版实际上同时踩了 3 个最伤上限的点：

- **窗口太小**：`FIFO_SIZE=1`
- **接收端远端轮询**
- **collective/one-way 场景下需要动态扫未注册 lane**

这三条叠在一起，性能差是非常正常的，不是偶然。

**一句话总结：**  
当前 mailbox 赢在 correctness 和规避共享原子风险，**不赢在性能上限**；在你当前这版实现里，原来的 LSE 原子 FIFO 理论上限大概率更高。

67. Each slot is **sender-owned** by exactly one iface. Inside that slot:
68. 
69. - there are two banks: `local` and `remote`
70. - each bank has one lane per destination slot index
71. - each lane is SPSC:
72.   - slot owner is the only writer of `head` and `sender_generation`
73.   - the matching receiver is the only writer of `tail` and `tail_generation`
74. 
75. Banking is derived from exporter identity relative to the sender's local export
76. region, not from slot index. This avoids local-slot-index and remote-slot-index
77. collisions in the fixed two-node topology.
78. 
79. Every lane element `elem[N]` has a paired `desc[N]` in that same lane. Their
80. lifetime is identical: once the receiver advances `tail` past index `N`, the
81. sender may reuse both on the next lap.
82. 
83. ### Slot stride
84. 
85. ```
86. lane_stride = align_up(
87.     sizeof(uct_obmm_mailbox_ctl_t) +
88.     fifo_size * elem_size +
89.     fifo_size * seg_size,
90.     cacheline)
91. 
92. slot_stride = align_up(
93.     2 * slot_count * lane_stride,
94.     cacheline)
95. ```
96. 
97. The pool's `slot_count` (compile-time `UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT = 32`)
98. **times** `slot_stride` MUST fit in `region->length` (128 MiB minus pool
99.  header overhead). Defaults are picked to favor short-path coverage over
100.  maximum local process count; lowering `seg_size` and/or `fifo_size`
101.  reduces per-slot footprint, but the supported local attach count remains
102.  the compile-time `slot_count`.
103. 
104. Default budget check:
105. ```
106. fifo_size       =      1
107. elem_size       =  16448   (raw UCT max_short = 16432 total bytes)
108. seg_size        =  32768   (raw UCT max_bcopy = 32768)
109. lane_stride     =  49344
110. ctl + slot data = 64 * 49344 = ~3084 KiB / slot
111. slot_count      =     32
112. total           = ~ 96 MiB / 128 MiB                     ✓
113. ```
114. These defaults are chosen from measured latency sweeps rather than from
115. wire-format arithmetic alone. With Open MPI PML/UCX on this tree, ordinary
116. `MPI_Send` goes through `mca_pml_ucx_send_nbr()` into `ucp_tag_send_nbx()`,
117. and UCX defaults `PROTO_ENABLE=y`, so protocol v2 selects between eager short,
118. eager bcopy single/multi, and rendezvous using its own headers and cost model.
119. The best reasoning-backed configuration found so far is to keep both geometry
120. knobs 64-byte aligned, leave `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE=32768` for 32KiB-class raw bcopy
121. capacity, and reduce `FIFO_ELEM_SIZE` to `16448` so 16KiB-class payloads stay
122. comfortably on short without over-extending the short window into slower
123. 32KiB-class territory.
124. 
125. When the last local iface on an export exits, UCX resets the entire local
126. export region to zero before another attach may re-initialize the pool.
127.

169. ## Sender side (`obmm_ep`)
170. 
171. Each EP binds to one outbound lane in its **local sender-owned slot**:
172. 
173. - slot base = local `iface->slot`
174. - bank = `local` if the peer device address names our export region, otherwise
175.   `remote`
176. - destination lane index = peer `iface_addr.slot_index`
177. 
178. Both `am_short` and `am_bcopy` publish to that lane identically:
179. 
180. ```
181. 1. load local cached tail for this lane
182. 2. if (tx_index - cached_tail) >= fifo_size:
183.         bus_load_fence; refresh cached_tail; recheck;
184.         if still full: return UCS_ERR_NO_RESOURCE
185. 3. idx = tx_index, N = idx & mask
186. 4. payload write:
187.       short: memcpy header+payload into elem[N]+1
188.       bcopy: pack_cb(desc[N], arg) -> length
189. 5. fill elem[N] header fields (flags, am_id, length, generation, [header])
190. 6. ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()                          <- release barrier
191. 7. tx_index++
192. 8. lane_ctl->head = tx_index
193. ```
194. 
195. There is no shared producer lock, shared head CAS, or shared FAA. All hot-path
196. ownership is single-writer by construction.
197. 
198. ### Pending
199. 
200. `ep_pending_add` always queues into the iface arbiter. `iface_progress`
201. dispatches pending on every call, even if no RX completion occurred, because
202. depth-1 lanes will hit `UCS_ERR_NO_RESOURCE` frequently.
203. 
204. ---
205. 
206. ## Receiver side (`obmm_iface_progress`)
207. 
208. ```
209. round-robin over registered inbound lanes, up to fifo_max_poll completions:
210.     if lane is inactive: continue
211.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence()
212.     if lane_ctl->sender_generation != expected_sender_generation:
213.         continue                                             (stale registration)
214.     if lane_ctl->head == rx_index:
215.         continue                                             (no work)
216.     elem = elem[rx_index & mask]
217.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence()                              (acquire payload)
218.     if elem->generation != iface->generation:
219.         drop silently (slot was reused after our death+rebirth)
220.     elif elem->flags & BCOPY:
221.         desc = desc[rx_index & mask]
222.         invoke_am(am_id, desc,  length, 0)
223.     else:
224.         invoke_am(am_id, &elem->header, length, 0)
225.     rx_index++
226.     full bus fence
227.     if lane_ctl->sender_generation != expected_sender_generation:
228.         skip ack publish for this completion
229.     lane_ctl->tail = rx_index
230.     ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()
231.     if lane_ctl->sender_generation != expected_sender_generation:
232.         skip tail_generation publish
233.     lane_ctl->tail_generation = expected_sender_generation
234. ```
235. 
236. Each inbound lane is registered by `(bank, sender_slot_index)` and refcounted,
237. so multiple EPs to the same sender slot do not duplicate-consume one lane.
238. 
239. ---
240. 
241. ## Capabilities (`iface_query`)
242. 
243. | flag                            | v1 | v2 | notes                       |
244. |---------------------------------|----|----|-----------------------------|
245. | AM_SHORT                        |  ✓ |  ✓ | max = elem_size - 16        |
246. | AM_BCOPY                        |  ✓ |  ✓ | v1: = max_short (cramped); v2: = seg_size |
247. | PENDING                         |  ✓ |  ✓ | iface arbiter, always queued |
248. | CONNECT_TO_IFACE                |  ✓ |  ✓ |                             |
249. | CB_SYNC                         |  ✓ |  ✓ |                             |
250. | INTER_NODE                      |  ✓ |  ✓ | required for cross-host UCT (otherwise OMPI's NET_ONLY filter strips us — see ucp_worker.c:2962) |
251. 
252. **Not advertised** in v1/v2: PUT/GET (any), ATOMIC, AM_ZCOPY, EP_CHECK,
253. AM_DUP, ERRHANDLE_PEER. Adding any of these requires a separate design
254. note.
255.

1. <overview>
2. This segment focused on stabilizing the obmm transport after earlier tuning work, first by fixing a confirmed receive-slot ownership race that caused UCP tag warnings, and then by continuing diagnosis of a remaining probabilistic cross-node 4-process hang in `osu_multi_lat`. The overall approach was: reduce the reproducer, instrument only when a code-grounded hypothesis existed, confirm the hypothesis with the user’s runtime results, apply a surgical fix, remove temporary diagnostics, then iterate on the next highest-signal concurrency defect.
3. </overview>
4. 
5. <history>
6. 1. The user asked whether the obmm bandwidth setting was really “required”.
7.    - I first changed obmm’s default `BW` config from an unrealistic `12179MBs` to `3400MBs` to match the user’s measured sustained bandwidth.
8.    - I updated the code and docs to clarify that `UCX_OBMM_BW` is **optional for users**, but obmm must still report a positive default bandwidth to UCP.
9.    - I then clarified the user’s deeper question: **the transport must expose a bandwidth value to UCP**, because UCP consumes it in address unpacking and protocol/lane cost modeling; it is not optional at the transport-contract level.
10. 
11. 2. The user reported massive `tag_match.c:62 UCX WARN unexpected tag-receive descriptor ... was not matched` spam, reproducible even with a simplified 2-process, 1-byte intra-node case, and asked whether `ucx_perftest` could be used as a smaller reproducer.
12.    - I followed the diagnose-first workflow: retrieved UCX/UCP tag-match references, inspected `tag_match.c`, `eager_rcv.c`, `tag_match.inl`, and obmm send/receive paths in `obmm_ep.c` / `obmm_iface.c`.
13.    - I concluded that the warning proves the receiver accepted extra/late/misrouted tag messages, not just a send drop.
14.    - I identified the strongest root cause as a **slot double-claim race** in `uct_obmm_pool_try_claim()`: process A could set the bitmap bit, but before publishing `slot_meta.state = IN_USE`, process B could observe `bit=1 && state!=IN_USE` and “take over” the same slot.
15.    - I confirmed that `ucx_perftest -t tag_lat -s 1` would be a smaller UCP tag reproducer than MPI.
16. 
17. 3. The user asked to add a log that would “hammer the nail” into the suspected race without being buried by warning spam.
18.    - I added a one-time high-priority diagnostic in `obmm_pool.c` that logged when `bitmap bit set && slot_meta.state == FREE` was observed.

115. <technical_details>
116. - **BW / UCP contract**
117.   - `iface_attr->bandwidth.dedicated` is consumed by `ucp_tl_iface_bandwidth()` and UCP protocol/lane cost modeling.
118.   - UCP address unpack also rejects non-positive bandwidth values.
119.   - Therefore `UCX_OBMM_BW` is optional as a user knob, but obmm itself must always report a positive bandwidth to UCP.
120.   - The default was changed to `3400MBs` to match sustained measured transport throughput rather than optimistic peak.
121. 
122. - **Meaning of `unexpected tag-receive descriptor ... was not matched`**
123.   - Emitted by `ucp_tag_match_cleanup()` when descriptors remain on `tm->unexpected.all` at UCP worker teardown.
124.   - It proves the receiver accepted extra/late/misrouted tag messages; it is not just a send-drop symptom.
125. 
126. - **Confirmed slot double-claim bug**
127.   - Original `uct_obmm_pool_try_claim()` could allow:
128.     1. process A CASes bitmap bit 0→1
129.     2. before A publishes `slot_meta.state = IN_USE`
130.     3. process B sees `bit=1 && state!=IN_USE`
131.     4. B “takes over” same slot
132.   - This caused multiple processes to publish the same receive slot in their iface address, explaining tag mismatches.
133.   - Fixed by adding explicit `CLAIMING` state and tightening alloc/free/scavenge sequencing.
134.   - `free_slot()` now keeps owner identity until after `clear_bit`, so `DEAD` is meaningful during release/scavenge races.
135. 
136. - **Cross-node 4-rank hang signal**
137.   - Reproducer:
138.     `mpirun -np 4 --hostfile hostfile --map-by node --mca pml ucx --allow-run-as-root -x OPAL_PREFIX -x PATH -x LD_LIBRARY_PATH -x UCX_TLS=obmm -x UCX_OBMM_MEMIDS=1,2 /osu/pt2pt/osu_multi_lat -m 1:1`
139.   - User results:
140.     - same-node reduced cases: no repro
141.     - cross-node 2 proc: no repro
142.     - cross-node 4 proc: probabilistic silent hangs
143.     - diagnostics:
144.       - `lock busy ...` log appeared every 4-proc run
145.       - never on 2-proc
146.       - `stale elem drop` never appeared
147.   - This weakens the “stale-slot/message corruption” hypothesis and points more toward contention/locking issues.
148. 
149. - **`BUSY` semantics in UCT/UCP**
150.   - `uct_ep_pending_add(...)=UCS_ERR_BUSY` means “request was not queued; resources are available now; caller should retry”.
151.   - UCP interprets this as immediate retry rather than queued pending work.
152.   - Because obmm’s `NO_RESOURCE` can mean either FIFO-full or transient head-lock contention, using `BUSY` after such a failure can create retry storms under contention.
153.   - obmm `pending_add()` was therefore changed to **always queue** instead of returning `BUSY`.
154. 
155. - **Remaining unresolved hypothesis: lock-token collision**
156.   - `try_lock_head()` infers lock acquisition success by checking `peer_ctl->lock == ep->lock_token` after attempting CAS, because the CAS return value is considered unreliable on the target NC mapping.
157.   - If two writers can share the same token, both may think they acquired the same lock.
158.   - The old token used simple XOR with a process-local `ep` pointer, which is unsafe across processes because virtual addresses can repeat.
159.   - New token builder now mixes:
160.     - local exporter identity
161.     - local slot/generation
162.     - local pid/starttime
163.     - peer slot/pid
164.     - ep pointer
165.   - This fix was applied, but runtime validation is still pending.
166.   - The code review also requested a one-time warning when `ucs_sys_get_proc_create_time(getpid())` returns `0`, since that weakens token uniqueness; this warning is not yet in the file because the last patch failed.
167. 
168. - **Diagnostics policy used in this segment**
169.   - For difficult bugs, the user has explicitly said to add logs directly when there is a concrete direction.
170.   - Temporary diagnostics were intentionally one-time/high-priority to avoid perturbing timing too much and to avoid burying the interesting signal in repeated WARN spam.
171.

174.   - Real validation depends on the user’s MPI/OSU runs.

<sub>⏱️ 3818m 29s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

**结论：如果允许把内存放宽到 512MiB / 1GiB，并且两边都顺手把内存布局一起优化，我更看好“改良后的跨节点原子 FIFO / receiver-local queue”理论上限更高。**  
原因不是 mailbox 不能变快，而是 **sender-owned mailbox 有一个去不掉的基本代价：接收侧热路径仍然是远端读 + 远端写 ack**；而原子 FIFO 这边一旦用更大内存把队列**做深并做分片**，就能把主要热点留在发送侧的少量远端原子上，同时把接收侧保留为**本地 poll**，这在上限上更占优。

| 方案 | 放大内存后最关键的收益 | 去不掉的根本代价 | 理论上限判断 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sender-owned mailbox | 可把 depth 从 1 提到 4/8，去掉大量 pending；再加目录/位图减少扫描 | RX 仍要消费 remote lane，并回写 remote tail | 会大幅变好，但上限仍受 remote RX 限制 |
| atomic FIFO / receiver-local queue | 可把队列做深、按 sender/shard 分片，降低 head 争用 | TX 仍需远端 FAA/CAS/LSE | 更容易把热点压到少量远端原子，RX 保持本地，理论上限更高 |

基于你当前 `DESIGN.md` 里的公式，**保持现在这套 mailbox 几何不变** 时，预算大致是：

- **128MiB**：最大 depth = **1**
- **512MiB**：最大 depth = **5**，实际可选 2 的幂就是 **4**
- **1GiB**：最大 depth = **10**，实际可选 2 的幂就是 **8**

这已经能解释很多事：当前 mailbox 差，首先是因为 **depth=1** 太狠；把预算提到 512MiB/1GiB 后，它会明显变强，尤其 pending/arbiter 压力会大幅下降。  
但即便如此，**它的接收面仍然不是本地队列**。哪怕你把未注册 lane 扫描优化成目录索引、预注册表、活跃位图，甚至把 short/bcopy 存储拆开，最后 RX 还是在“看远端 sender slot”，这一点和 mm 那种 **receiver-local FIFO** 的本地 poll 不是一个级别。

所以更精确地说：

1. **如果只做小改**，比如单纯把 mailbox 深度拉到 4/8，再减少扫描，它会从“很差”变成“可用甚至不错”。  
2. **如果允许认真重做布局**，那我更看好 **atomic FIFO 这条线**，但不是老的“单共享 head/lock”原样复活，而是：
   - **receiver-local**
   - **多 shard / 每 sender 一条子队列或少量分片队列**
   - **发送侧用 LSE FAA/CAS 做 ticket/reserve**
   - **接收侧只做本地 poll**

这样做以后，mailbox 的优势只剩“避免远端原子热点”；但 atomic 方案已经用**分片**把这个热点稀释了，同时保住了**本地 RX**，所以理论峰值更高，尤其是：

- **大消息吞吐**
- **多进程 fan-in**
- **collective 的接收侧压力**
- **CPU 开销/轮询效率**

**一句话总结：**  
**512MiB / 1GiB 能把当前 mailbox 从“窗口太小导致先天吃亏”救回来，但如果两边都按最优思路重构，最终理论天花板还是更偏向“分片后的 receiver-local atomic FIFO”。**

1. # obmm UCT transport — design notes
2. 
3. This file is the **single source of truth** for the on-region wire format
4. and the data-path semantics of the `obmm` UCT transport. Update it
5. **before** changing layout, capabilities, or sync rules. AGENTS.md
6. mandates retrieve-before-recall; this doc is the first thing to grep.
7. 
8. Status legend:
9. - **v1** = shipped, MPI cross-node smoke tests pass.
10. - **v2** = current target: complete `am_bcopy` (max_bcopy decoupled from
11.   FIFO element size, no per-message UCP fragmentation below seg_size).
12. - **Current validated baseline** = sender-owned mailbox transport with
13.   `am_short`, `am_bcopy`, pending dispatch, dynamic progress of one-way
14.   inbound lanes, and OSU point-to-point plus collective suites passing on
15.   the target hardware per user report.
16. 
17. ---
18. 
19. ## Locked-in environment facts
20. 
21. (Mirrors `.github/skills/obmm-api-and-env/SKILL.md`. Do NOT contradict
22. without re-checking that file.)
23. 
24. - Each node pre-exports **one 128 MiB region**; export/import is done
25.   outside UCX. UCT must NOT call `obmm_export/import/preimport/...`.
26. - Data-path mapping is **non-cacheable** (`open(... O_SYNC)` + mmap).
27.   `obmm_set_ownership` is forbidden and irrelevant.
28. - Cross-host 64-bit FAA/CAS on the target NC mapping are available only when
29.   emitted as explicit arm64 **LSE** instructions; compiler-default **LL/SC**
30.   atomics are not supported on this NC memory. A follow-up LSE-based probe
31.   confirmed both FAA and CAS are usable. The current transport baseline still
32.   keeps shared cross-node atomic RMW out of the hot path.
33. - Memory ordering uses **bus-domain fences**
34.   (`ucs_memory_bus_store_fence` / `ucs_memory_bus_load_fence`), NOT the
35.   CPU-domain `ucs_memory_cpu_*_fence` that mm uses. mm peers share an
36.   inner-shareable cache domain; obmm peers do not.
37. - Reachability is keyed on `(exporter_dcna, exporter_deid, memid)`,
38.   never memid alone.
39. - Two-phase pool init (UNINIT → INITING → READY via CAS) plus per-slot
40.   `(generation, owner_pid, owner_starttime)` for crash/PID-reuse safety.
41.   During teardown, INITING is reused only as a transient cleanup lock; after
42.   reset the shared region returns to literal all-zero memory.
43. - ARM64 is the production ISA. NC + bus fences are correct on aarch64.
44. 
45. ---
46. 
47. ## Region layout (v2)
48. 
49. Inside the 128 MiB exported region:
50. 
51. ```
52. +-------------------------------------------------------+ offset 0
53. | uct_obmm_pool_hdr_t (magic, state, geometry)          |
54. +-------------------------------------------------------+
55. | alloc_bitmap[bitmap_words]                            |
56. +-------------------------------------------------------+
57. | slot_meta[slot_count]  (gen, owner_pid, starttime, …) |
58. +-------------------------------------------------------+ hdr->slot_array_offset
59. | slot[0]:                                              |
60. |   bank[local]: lane[0..slot_count-1]                  |
61. |   bank[remote]: lane[0..slot_count-1]                 |
62. +-------------------------------------------------------+
63. | slot[1]: …                                            |
64. …
65. ```
66. 
67. Each slot is **sender-owned** by exactly one iface. Inside that slot:
68. 
69. - there are two banks: `local` and `remote`
70. - each bank has one lane per destination slot index
71. - each lane is SPSC:
72.   - slot owner is the only writer of `head` and `sender_generation`
73.   - the matching receiver is the only writer of `tail` and `tail_generation`
74. 
75. Banking is derived from exporter identity relative to the sender's local export
76. region, not from slot index. This avoids local-slot-index and remote-slot-index
77. collisions in the fixed two-node topology.
78. 
79. Every lane element `elem[N]` has a paired `desc[N]` in that same lane. Their
80. lifetime is identical: once the receiver advances `tail` past index `N`, the
81. sender may reuse both on the next lap.
82. 
83. ### Slot stride
84. 
85. ```
86. lane_stride = align_up(
87.     sizeof(uct_obmm_mailbox_ctl_t) +
88.     fifo_size * elem_size +
89.     fifo_size * seg_size,
90.     cacheline)
91. 
92. slot_stride = align_up(
93.     2 * slot_count * lane_stride,
94.     cacheline)
95. ```
96. 
97. The pool's `slot_count` (compile-time `UCT_OBMM_POOL_SLOT_COUNT = 32`)
98. **times** `slot_stride` MUST fit in `region->length` (128 MiB minus pool
99.  header overhead). Defaults are picked to favor short-path coverage over
100.  maximum local process count; lowering `seg_size` and/or `fifo_size`
101.  reduces per-slot footprint, but the supported local attach count remains
102.  the compile-time `slot_count`.
103. 
104. Default budget check:
105. ```
106. fifo_size       =      1
107. elem_size       =  16448   (raw UCT max_short = 16432 total bytes)
108. seg_size        =  32768   (raw UCT max_bcopy = 32768)
109. lane_stride     =  49344
110. ctl + slot data = 64 * 49344 = ~3084 KiB / slot
111. slot_count      =     32
112. total           = ~ 96 MiB / 128 MiB                     ✓
113. ```
114. These defaults are chosen from measured latency sweeps rather than from
115. wire-format arithmetic alone. With Open MPI PML/UCX on this tree, ordinary
116. `MPI_Send` goes through `mca_pml_ucx_send_nbr()` into `ucp_tag_send_nbx()`,
117. and UCX defaults `PROTO_ENABLE=y`, so protocol v2 selects between eager short,
118. eager bcopy single/multi, and rendezvous using its own headers and cost model.
119. The best reasoning-backed configuration found so far is to keep both geometry
120. knobs 64-byte aligned, leave `BCOPY_SEG_SIZE=32768` for 32KiB-class raw bcopy
121. capacity, and reduce `FIFO_ELEM_SIZE` to `16448` so 16KiB-class payloads stay
122. comfortably on short without over-extending the short window into slower
123. 32KiB-class territory.
124. 
125. When the last local iface on an export exits, UCX resets the entire local
126. export region to zero before another attach may re-initialize the pool.
127. 
128. ---
129. 
130. ## FIFO element layout
131. 
132. `uct_obmm_fifo_element_t` (16 bytes, packed):
133. 
134. | field      | bytes | notes                                          |
135. |------------|-------|------------------------------------------------|
136. | flags      |   1   | BCOPY bit only                                 |
137. | am_id      |   1   |                                                |
138. | length     |   2   | u16 — bytes passed to the AM callback          |
139. | generation |   4   | receiver-slot generation token at TX time      |
140. | header     |   8   | am_short user-visible 8B header (unused bcopy) |
141. 
142. For **am_short**, callback data starts at `&elem->header`, so the callback sees
143. `[header | payload]` and `elem->length = sizeof(header) + payload_length`.
144. The raw UCT limit remains `max_short = elem_size - 16`.
145. 
146. For **am_bcopy**, payload lives in the paired `desc[N]`. On bcopy the sender
147. writes:
148. - `elem->flags  = BCOPY`
149. - `elem->am_id  = id`
150. - `elem->length = pack_cb_returned_length`     (≤ seg_size, so ≤ u16max)
151. - `elem->generation = ep->expected_generation`
152. - `elem->header = 0` (unused)
153. 
154. Receiver, on seeing FLAG_BCOPY, computes
155. `desc[N] = slot_descs + (idx & mask) * seg_size` and calls
156. `uct_iface_invoke_am(am_id, desc[N], length, 0)`.
157. 
158. Because `desc[N]` is bound 1:1 to `elem[N]`, no extra metadata is
159. exchanged in the FIFO element to locate the desc.
160. 
161. ### `length` field width
162. 
163. `elem->length` stays `uint16_t`, capping `seg_size` at 65535. We reject
164. larger `seg_size` at iface init. If a future `seg_size > 64KiB` is
165. needed, widen `length` to `uint32_t` and update the compatibility checks.
166. 
167. ---
168. 
169. ## Sender side (`obmm_ep`)
170. 
171. Each EP binds to one outbound lane in its **local sender-owned slot**:
172. 
173. - slot base = local `iface->slot`
174. - bank = `local` if the peer device address names our export region, otherwise
175.   `remote`
176. - destination lane index = peer `iface_addr.slot_index`
177. 
178. Both `am_short` and `am_bcopy` publish to that lane identically:
179. 
180. ```
181. 1. load local cached tail for this lane
182. 2. if (tx_index - cached_tail) >= fifo_size:
183.         bus_load_fence; refresh cached_tail; recheck;
184.         if still full: return UCS_ERR_NO_RESOURCE
185. 3. idx = tx_index, N = idx & mask
186. 4. payload write:
187.       short: memcpy header+payload into elem[N]+1
188.       bcopy: pack_cb(desc[N], arg) -> length
189. 5. fill elem[N] header fields (flags, am_id, length, generation, [header])
190. 6. ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()                          <- release barrier
191. 7. tx_index++
192. 8. lane_ctl->head = tx_index
193. ```
194. 
195. There is no shared producer lock, shared head CAS, or shared FAA. All hot-path
196. ownership is single-writer by construction.
197. 
198. ### Pending
199. 
200. `ep_pending_add` always queues into the iface arbiter. `iface_progress`
201. dispatches pending on every call, even if no RX completion occurred, because
202. depth-1 lanes will hit `UCS_ERR_NO_RESOURCE` frequently.
203. 
204. ---
205. 
206. ## Receiver side (`obmm_iface_progress`)
207. 
208. ```
209. round-robin over registered inbound lanes, up to fifo_max_poll completions:
210.     if lane is inactive: continue
211.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence()
212.     if lane_ctl->sender_generation != expected_sender_generation:
213.         continue                                             (stale registration)
214.     if lane_ctl->head == rx_index:
215.         continue                                             (no work)
216.     elem = elem[rx_index & mask]
217.     ucs_memory_bus_load_fence()                              (acquire payload)
218.     if elem->generation != iface->generation:
219.         drop silently (slot was reused after our death+rebirth)
220.     elif elem->flags & BCOPY:
221.         desc = desc[rx_index & mask]
222.         invoke_am(am_id, desc,  length, 0)
223.     else:
224.         invoke_am(am_id, &elem->header, length, 0)
225.     rx_index++
226.     full bus fence
227.     if lane_ctl->sender_generation != expected_sender_generation:
228.         skip ack publish for this completion
229.     lane_ctl->tail = rx_index
230.     ucs_memory_bus_store_fence()
231.     if lane_ctl->sender_generation != expected_sender_generation:
232.         skip tail_generation publish
233.     lane_ctl->tail_generation = expected_sender_generation
234. ```
235. 
236. Each inbound lane is registered by `(bank, sender_slot_index)` and refcounted,
237. so multiple EPs to the same sender slot do not duplicate-consume one lane.
238. 
239. ---
240. 
241. ## Capabilities (`iface_query`)
242. 
243. | flag                            | v1 | v2 | notes                       |
244. |---------------------------------|----|----|-----------------------------|
245. | AM_SHORT                        |  ✓ |  ✓ | max = elem_size - 16        |
246. | AM_BCOPY                        |  ✓ |  ✓ | v1: = max_short (cramped); v2: = seg_size |
247. | PENDING                         |  ✓ |  ✓ | iface arbiter, always queued |
248. | CONNECT_TO_IFACE                |  ✓ |  ✓ |                             |
249. | CB_SYNC                         |  ✓ |  ✓ |                             |
250. | INTER_NODE                      |  ✓ |  ✓ | required for cross-host UCT (otherwise OMPI's NET_ONLY filter strips us — see ucp_worker.c:2962) |
251. 
252. **Not advertised** in v1/v2: PUT/GET (any), ATOMIC, AM_ZCOPY, EP_CHECK,
253. AM_DUP, ERRHANDLE_PEER. Adding any of these requires a separate design
254. note.
255.

22. /* Every sender-owned slot contains two mailbox banks so destination slot

37. /* Per-lane mailbox control. One sender owns head/sender_generation; one
38.  * receiver owns tail/tail_generation. The slot owner initializes all lanes'
39.  * sender_generation to its slot generation when the slot is allocated. */
40. typedef struct uct_obmm_mailbox_ctl {
41.     /* 1st cacheline: sender-touched */

61.                              elements whose generation doesn't match its local
62.                              iface generation */
63.     uint64_t header;      /* am_short 64-bit header */
